chapters.title: Chapter 1151
paragraphs: The moment he activated the secret device that only one person in the world was permitted to use, Vladimir Furin thought:
*This is as far as I go.*
Was he reluctant to let go of life? Afraid of death?
Of course he was.
The more a person had, the harder it was to let go. That was human nature. And for a man who had ruled as a dictator for nearly half a century, there was no need to ask.
He wanted to live.
He had to live.
He had to raise the name Vladimir Furin to the level of a god.
He had to become greater than the tsars, who had ruled this land for generations by virtue of their noble blood, and greater even than the Iron Marshal, against whom no one had dared rebel.
But if that proved impossible—
If someone else appeared and tried to take everything he had built—
*I’ll burn it all down. With my own hands, so no one else can have it.*
The old dictator, who had dreamed of immortality, smiled faintly.
Or rather, he tried to.
Time slowed, stretching out like a passing life flashing before his eyes. Then he saw the looter wearing a vivid smile.
“You really are an interesting human.”
Furin’s shrewd eyes widened.
Rrrrrumble.
The enormous rumble, as if it would swallow the Kremlin—or Moscow itself—drew closer.
Slowly. Deliberately.
As though it moved at someone’s will.
At last, Vladimir Furin saw the source of this unexpected phenomenon with his own eyes.
Wooooom.
Would thousands—tens of thousands—of bees swarming together sound like this?
Furin could only stare blankly at the vortex of flames rising through the melting floor of his office.
Everything was red. Everything was hot.
Surrounded by an aura as dark as pitch, it had been compressed into a great sphere that blazed like a tiny sun.
And the old dictator, staring at it in shock, knew better than anyone that “tiny sun” was no exaggeration.
He also knew that a power once great enough to terrify the entire world was now in the grasp of the monster smiling at him.
*Tsar Bomba.*
The most powerful weapon in human history.
The mother and emperor of all bombs.
Only a handful of people involved knew that the most powerful hydrogen bomb of the Cold War—the one that had frozen the five oceans and six continents with fear—lay sleeping deep beneath the Kremlin.
They also knew that decades of secret experiments, carried out on the dictator’s orders, had given it a new name and destructive power far beyond what it had possessed before.
“Remarkable. Truly remarkable. To think you humans created power like this. What do you call this weapon?”
At Morgoth’s genuine expression of awe, Furin—sensing that everything was over—answered in a hollow voice.
“Vladimir.”
“What?”
Morgoth looked from the old dictator, already all but fallen, to the catastrophic power bearing his name. Then he laughed aloud.
“That’s a masterpiece. Or should I say, very like you?”
Morgoth found it truly amusing.
That a human granted barely a hundred years could harbor such enormous ambitions.
And that these mere mortals had tried to kill him, a being with power close to immortality, using a weapon they had made.
“Did you think this alone could bring me down? With Magic Gems taken from lowly monsters, you dare challenge me?”
At Morgoth’s words, as though he had already seen through everything, Furin quietly swallowed.
He was right. Tsar Bomba—or rather, the weapon now called Vladimir—was not merely a product of science.
The Great Cataclysm.
After that event had overturned the world’s common sense and order, one thought had taken root in the mind of the dictator who had barely survived.
*I have to become stronger. So this can never happen again. So we can win any war.*
And the means were close at hand.
Magic and Magic Gems. The new knowledge born from them: magical engineering.
And so Tsar Bomba became Vladimir.
As one of the world’s great powers—and a dictatorship at that—Russia had countless ways to obtain Magic Gems for the experiments.
Of course, that meant violating more international treaties than anyone could count and killing even his own scientists and mages to keep everything secret...but what did that matter?
Mother Russia.
Russia—or rather, he—had to become greater still.
Even if a second Demon King descended, he and Russia alone had to survive and rewrite the world order.
*Or die together.*
Yes.
That was how it had to be.
Plop.
Ash fell away in clumps.
Despite decades of not smoking, Furin had managed only a few drags from the cigar. He stared at it blankly, then spoke.
“What are you going to do now?”
Morgoth didn’t answer.
But Furin immediately understood the meaning behind the gentle curve of his lips.
“Right. It has nothing to do with me anymore.”
The cigar trembled.
No—it was Furin himself who was shaking.
“Any last words?”
At Morgoth’s kind offer, Furin raised a hand that shook like a leaf and brought the cigar to his lips.
He drew deeper than he ever had before, then blew the smoke toward the monster before him.
“No. But there’s one thing I have to tell you.”
He spoke the name of the man who had crossed his mind just before he activated the bomb bearing his own name.
“If Jin comes back, you’re finished.”
At that moment—
“I look forward to it. Truly.”
Swoooosh.
With Morgoth’s calm reply, the pitch-black aura restraining the catastrophic power slowly dispersed and enveloped its master.
Like the touch of death announcing the end of this land.
Whoosh.
A blinding flash swallowed the old, wretched dictator’s final sight.
It was warm.
Eight meters long. Two meters in diameter. Twenty-seven tons.
Packed into a volume that could fill a large truck was the destructive power of fifty megatons—fifty million tons of TNT.
Those were the publicly known figures for Tsar Bomba.
It had enough power to make Little Boy, the bomb that turned Hiroshima into a land of death during World War II, seem like a little boy indeed.
But no one had expected it.
No one had expected this monster from a bygone era, born of the Cold War’s displays of power, to awaken again more than eighty years later.
And no one had expected the monster’s first cry after its long sleep to ring out from the Kremlin.
Gooooom.
The air trembled in an instant.
Everyone in the Kremlin—or rather, everyone in Moscow—felt that deep, ominous rumble.
The soldiers and Hunters holding their posts despite their fear. The citizens who had rushed into bomb shelters or out onto the streets when Red Square collapsed.
No one was spared.
Everyone felt it, and everyone instinctively understood.
This was the last moment they would ever draw breath.
And then—
Whoooosh.
There was light.
A terrible heat beyond human perception, atomic power mingled with potent energy drawn from countless Magic Gems—it all spread out, devouring everything in its path.
Endlessly. Greedily.
Kraaaaaash!
In the storm of power, everything melted.
The living died. The lifeless lost their shape.
Underground or aboveground, whatever life they had lived—it didn’t matter.
The blinding light that burst from the Kremlin made everyone equal.
Just as Icarus had lost his wings and fallen when he flew too close to the sun, the tiny sun born of a dictator’s ambition and fear swallowed countless lives, including his own.
All of them, save one.
Rrrrrumble.
At the heart of the rumbling that shook everything around him, Morgoth lifted his head and surveyed the scene he had created.
Nothing remained.
Everything that had surrounded him just minutes earlier was gone.
Molten metal flowed in rivers. Above it rose a massive mushroom cloud, looming over the surface now transformed into a land of death.
It was quite a sight.
“Such power. I didn’t even need to use Breath.”
Morgoth felt both admiration and regret.
How could mortals be so greedy and yet so foolish?
They had saved him a great deal of trouble, but the place now shadowed by calamity was desolate beyond measure.
A city with a long history and a population of over ten million had become a land where nothing could live for hundreds of years.
“But birth awakens from within death.”
The moment Morgoth spread both hands with those quiet words—
Pop.
The air stopped. The wind stopped.
And the Magic Gem energy that had swept across the city with a deadliness greater than radiation changed in response to his will.
Darker than before. Purer still.
Wooooom.
Dragon.
Great beings blessed by mana from the moment of their birth.
Morgoth had been revered as the strongest among them, yet in the end he had chosen corruption of his own accord. At his fingertips, space trembled.
Gathering. Compacting. Rising.
And at last—
Rrrrrumble.
It was built.
A gigantic castle unlike anything ever seen in this world.
His own kingdom.

In place of concrete and marble, it stood upon pitch-black earth amid air saturated with dense magical power. It was overwhelming, yet beautiful. Morgoth smiled as he gazed at its spire piercing the clouds.
Or, more precisely, at the camera lens of the drone hidden in the thick black clouds, watching him.
“Have you seen it, humans?”
That day, people all over the world saw it.
They watched Moscow disappear and a Dragon Lair come into being.
The calamity that had reached their doorstep.

chapters.title: Chapter 1152
paragraphs: There are no absolute secrets in modern society.
Cameras and the internet are everywhere, carrying countless pieces of information across the world.
And sometimes, a truth is better left unknown.
Like a Pandora’s box that should never have been opened.
—KABOOOOOM!
With one last terrible roar—more than the speakers could fully convey—the screen went black.

The viewers watching a famous influencer’s livestream from near the Kremlin knew instinctively what had happened. The stream had just passed one hundred million simultaneous viewers, making internet-broadcasting history. And they would never see the influencer behind that record again.
After several seconds of stillness, a single line appeared in the chat. It said enough about everything they had seen and felt over the past half hour.
└ Oh, God.
A Dragon’s wings crossing the skies above Moscow. Red Square vanishing without a trace.
The creature taking human form, just like them, then slaughtering the Hunters and soldiers who stood in its way as it strode into the Kremlin.
And then...
The calamity that engulfed Moscow.
Rrrrrumble!
The rumble traveled hundreds, even thousands of kilometers. It reached far beyond the rectangular screen and shook the world.
Countless eyes and ears—and even more cameras—caught the distant flash and the enormous mushroom cloud. The footage was quickly compiled into a single video and uploaded to the internet.
Its title captured the overwhelming shock and despair humanity felt at the news from Moscow.
—Where is God?
Where was God?
No one could answer.
No one.
All they could do was hope desperately.
If God had truly abandoned them, perhaps someone else would appear to save them.
No.
Perhaps he would wake from his deep sleep as soon as possible.
And unlike God, too far away for their voices to reach, the savior of this new age answered their pleas before long.
“He has returned.”
At those first words from the flushed fifty-seventh President of the United States on the holographic TV, the whole world erupted once more.
The modern world meant something special to me.
It was where I’d been born and raised. A home I could never forget.
That was why I’d always loved it.
Compared to Murim, where danger and trouble lurked around every corner, I could rest here in relative peace.
But when had that started to change?
Like a broken gear, everything had begun to slip out of place.
And it happened faster, with consequences more terrible, than I could ever have imagined.
What the hell was I supposed to say?
I kept trying to think, muttering words that meant nothing, but my mind had gone completely blank. Nothing came to me.
The hour-long video had just ended.
I stared silently at the black-haired man smiling at the camera in the paused holographic footage.
I wanted someone to break the heavy silence.
“I hear it happened three hours ago.”
At Magic Johnson’s low, subdued voice, the question I’d been holding back slipped past my dry lips.
“How many casualties?”
“Tell me. I’m prepared for it.”
Magic Johnson let out a quiet sigh.
“More than twenty million, even by the lowest estimate.”
“Shit.”
“Moscow, and the surrounding cities in the metropolitan area, were swept away. We’ve thrown every resource we have at investigating, but...”
He trailed off and bit his lip.
“There are no signs of life. They’re probably all dead.”
*Erasure.*
The word flashed through my mind. It was the most accurate way to describe what had happened.
“Vladimir. That fucking old man hid a hydrogen bomb in the Kremlin.”
At the start of the Great Cataclysm, humanity learned two important things.
First:
No matter how tight the security, modern science couldn’t stop teleportation magic.
Second:
Teleportation magic could move objects, not just people.
Objects like tactical nuclear weapons or hydrogen bombs.
That was why every nuclear-armed country in the world, led by the United States and Russia, had signed an international treaty and disposed of all weapons above a certain yield.
Or so we’d been told.
Until three hours ago, when a giant mushroom cloud filled the sky above Moscow.
“Russia is finished.”
That was true.
For every other country, though, this was a beginning of another kind. A crossroads.
Resist to the bitter end?
Or surrender now and stay alive?
*Black Dragon Duke Morgoth.*
I repeated the name in my mind as I stared at the holographic screen.
On the land, blackened by magical power, a gigantic castle towered behind him. I took in his smiling face and burned it into my heart.
*Can I defeat him?*
The question came to me naturally. I realized my hand had clenched into a fist.
Dragon.
The unprecedented monster whose single appearance in the past had shaken the entire world.
But as his title, Black Dragon Duke, suggested, Morgoth was no ordinary Dragon.
*He’s strong. Horrifyingly strong.*
I turned to the dozens of holographic screens filling the spacious monitor room and looked from one to the next.
A predator brought down a forest of skyscrapers with one flap of its wings, shrugged off a barrage of magic, and trampled Hunters underfoot.
Among those dying with one last scream were faces I knew.
“Die! Just die!”
On a crackling screen, a bloodied woman screamed.
Her lower body had already been crushed beyond recognition. Her abdomen was split open, her entrails spilling out.
Still, at the rear of her retreating allies, she drew her bow as if possessed.
She kept drawing until the Dragon’s claws came at her faster than an arrow and took both her arms.
Crunch!
Blood spurted along with the severed flesh.
A deep shadow fell across her face, twisted with unbearable pain.
“You foolish human. Didn’t you know this would happen?”
The Black Dragon’s question rang down from high above. She spat up bloody phlegm and answered.
“I did.”
“Then why?”
“Because we were taught to call this courage. Not foolishness.”
“Good. Then, brave human, would you follow me even now?”
“Fuck off, you monster. And...”
She grinned, baring her blood-soaked teeth.
“My name is Faye Chen. Not just *human*. Faye Chen.”
“I’ll remember that, human.”
“You’d better. Soon, someone incredible is going to come looking for you and ask about that name. Ask about... the name...”
Her voice faded. Then her ragged breathing stopped.
Her unfocused eyes stared into empty space.
The woman—no, Faye Chen—died just like that.
Hong Kong’s pride. An S-rank Hunter, a hero of the last Great Cataclysm, and my friend.
She had died a week ago.
*How about we all grab a drink?*
The memory came back to me.
The day we first met in Sichuan to hunt the Arch Lich, she’d suggested we go drinking. When I asked why it had to be that day, she answered:
*Today’s the kind of day you drink.*
*Huh?*
*It might be our last chance.*
That day, we drank until we could barely stand.
Neither of us thought it really would be our last drink together.
“She was a good person.”
A voice broke into my thoughts.
Rough and gravelly, it was different from Magic Johnson’s deep voice.
“And a great Hunter.”
I didn’t ask who the unwelcome guest was.
The acrid smell of cigar smoke had slipped in before the monitor room door even opened, telling me who it was.
“Her sacrifice saved a lot of lives. Including one bastard who came back alive in disgrace.”
Chuck Hagel.
Also known as Uncle Chuck, he approached slowly and put a hand on my shoulder.
With his right arm—the only one he had left.
“As soon as I woke up, I thought I should’ve died instead of Faye Chen.”
“...Hagel.”
“I know. It’s meaningless bullshit. And I’ve repeated it hundreds—no, thousands of times by now.”
Chuck Hagel exhaled cigar smoke and smiled bitterly.
He looked at the familiar faces and the deaths playing over and over on the dozens of holographic screens.
“I swore I’d never let anything like that happen again... Yet here we are.”
What was I supposed to say?
No. What right did I have to say anything?
Whenever I needed them, they came running without hesitation. But when they needed me, I hadn’t been there.
I hadn’t stopped Morgoth’s summoning. I hadn’t realized soon enough that the axis of time had shifted.
And this was the result.
Ten days of indiscriminate destruction and death.
The weight of it all pressed down on my chest, more than I could bear.
Along with the anger roiling deep in my gut like lava.
“You know what?”
I let out the breath I’d been holding.
Reason and emotion tangled together. Then my mind went cold.
Before my eyes, Faye Chen died once more.
“From now on, I won’t let anyone else be sacrificed.”
I stared at her on the screen, my eyes burning.
At her warning Morgoth, with what little breath she had left, that someone was coming for him.
Yes.
That was exactly what would happen.

For every other country, though, this was a beginning of another kind.
A crossroads.
Resist to the bitter end?
Or surrender now and stay alive?
*Black Dragon Duke Morgoth.*
I repeated the name in my mind as I stared at the holographic screen.
On the land, blackened by magical power, a gigantic castle towered behind him.
I took in his smiling face and burned it into my heart.
*Can I defeat him?*
The question came to me naturally.
I realized my hand had clenched into a fist.
Dragon.
The unprecedented monster whose single appearance in the past had shaken the entire world.
But as his title, Black Dragon Duke, suggested, Morgoth was no ordinary Dragon.
*He’s strong.
Horrifyingly strong.*
I turned to the dozens of holographic screens filling the spacious monitor room and looked from one to the next.
A predator brought down a forest of skyscrapers with one flap of its wings, shrugged off a barrage of magic, and trampled Hunters underfoot.
Among those dying with one last scream were faces I knew.
“Die!
Just die!”
On a crackling screen, a bloodied woman screamed.
Her lower body had already been crushed beyond recognition.
Her abdomen was split open, her entrails spilling out.
Still, at the rear of her retreating allies, she drew her bow as if possessed.
She kept drawing until the Dragon’s claws came at her faster than an arrow and took both her arms.
Crunch!
Blood spurted along with the severed flesh.
A deep shadow fell across her face, twisted with unbearable pain.
“You foolish human.
Didn’t you know this would happen?”
The Black Dragon’s question rang down from high above.
She spat up bloody phlegm and answered.
“I did.”
“Then why?”
“Because we were taught to call this courage.
Not foolishness.”
“Good.
Then, brave human, would you follow me even now?”
“Fuck off, you monster.
And...”
She grinned, baring her blood-soaked teeth.
“My name is Faye Chen.
Not just *human*.
Faye Chen.”
“I’ll remember that, human.”
“You’d better.
Soon, someone incredible is going to come looking for you and ask about that name.
Ask about... the name...”
Her voice faded.
Then her ragged breathing stopped.
Her unfocused eyes stared into empty space.
The woman—no, Faye Chen—died just like that.
Hong Kong’s pride.
An S-rank Hunter, a hero of the last Great Cataclysm, and my friend.
She had died a week ago.
*How about we all grab a drink?*
The memory came back to me.
The day we first met in Sichuan to hunt the Arch Lich, she’d suggested we go drinking.
When I asked why it had to be that day, she answered:
*Today’s the kind of day you drink.*
*Huh?*
*It might be our last chance.*
That day, we drank until we could barely stand.
Neither of us thought it really would be our last drink together.
“She was a good person.”
A voice broke into my thoughts.
Rough and gravelly, it was different from Magic Johnson’s deep voice.
“And a great Hunter.”
I didn’t ask who the unwelcome guest was.
The acrid smell of cigar smoke had slipped in before the monitor room door even opened, telling me who it was.
“Her sacrifice saved a lot of lives.
Including one bastard who came back alive in disgrace.”
Chuck Hagel.
Also known as Uncle Chuck, he approached slowly and put a hand on my shoulder.
With his right arm—the only one he had left.
“As soon as I woke up, I thought I should’ve died instead of Faye Chen.”
“...Hagel.”
“I know.
It’s meaningless bullshit.
And I’ve repeated it hundreds—no, thousands of times by now.”
Chuck Hagel exhaled cigar smoke and smiled bitterly.
He looked at the familiar faces and the deaths playing over and over on the dozens of holographic screens.
“I swore I’d never let anything like that happen again...
Yet here we are.”
What was I supposed to say?
No.
What right did I have to say anything?
Whenever I needed them, they came running without hesitation.
But when they needed me, I hadn’t been there.
I hadn’t stopped Morgoth’s summoning.
I hadn’t realized soon enough that the axis of time had shifted.
And this was the result.
Ten days of indiscriminate destruction and death.
The weight of it all pressed down on my chest, more than I could bear.
Along with the anger roiling deep in my gut like lava.
“You know what?”
I let out the breath I’d been holding.
Reason and emotion tangled together.
Then my mind went cold.
Before my eyes, Faye Chen died once more.
“From now on, I won’t let anyone else be sacrificed.”
I stared at her on the screen, my eyes burning.
At her warning Morgoth, with what little breath she had left, that someone was coming for him.
Yes.
That was exactly what would happen.

chapters.title: Chapter 1153
paragraphs: Everyone dies.

No matter how much wealth and fame a person amasses—more than anyone else in the world—or how strong their body and mind become, until they’re called superhuman, they can never escape the shadow of death.
That was why we had no choice but to accept, however painfully, the news that our close companions had died.
No. We had to.
The reality before us was too horrific to let ourselves be swept away by emotion.
“...That concludes the meeting.”
The lights came on with the presenter’s exhausted voice, but the heavy silence pressing down on the room didn’t disperse so easily.
Not until someone who had kept silent throughout the meeting finally spoke.
“Rest is important, isn’t it? Especially at a time like this.”
It was a simple remark, but everyone understood what he meant.
Anyone who couldn’t read the room that well wouldn’t have been here in the first place.
“I can finally breathe a little.”
Once the conference room had mostly emptied, a middle-aged man walked over to the coffee machine in one corner and glanced at me.
“Would you like a cup, Mr. Jin?”
His hair was greasy and disheveled, and dark circles ringed his eyes. He looked like an office worker worn down by exhaustion. I shook my head.
“No, thank you, Mr. Presi—”
“You can just call me Donny.”
“Sure. Donny.”
At my matter-of-fact reply, Donald Doramp Jr., the fifty-seventh President of the United States, smiled faintly.
Even that was a forced smile. It appeared for a moment, then vanished without a trace.
*Of course it did.*
My eyes drifted to the hologram still hanging in the air. Its catastrophic figures were enough to wipe the smile from even a thoroughly jaded politician’s face.
“When I first received the report at the White House, I thought, *Is this a dream?*”
He downed a cup of coffee heavily laced with potion and continued.
“To be honest, I still think that sometimes. I keep hoping all of this is one goddamn nightmare.”
But it was real. The figures in the reports hadn’t leveled off; they’d climbed higher every day.
Property damage in the tens of quadrillions. Tens of millions dead or injured, and even more refugees. The whole world was in a panic.
“That’s why I had to announce as soon as possible that you’d returned.”
As he said, the international community had moved quickly.

The UN Security Council, led by its permanent members, had immediately issued an emergency statement. News that I’d returned after going missing in the Middle East spread around the world before I’d even arrived here at the Pentagon.
“Some people thought it was too soon to make the announcement while we were still discussing it. But given the circumstances, we had no choice. If we made the wrong call—”
“No. You didn’t.”
I waved off the President’s apology.
Because it was too late to take the announcement back?
That was part of it, of course.
But if the news of my return hadn’t gotten out, people would have been swept into an even more uncontrollable maelstrom.
Disaster, after all, takes root in fear and confusion.
And the seed of that disaster had already blossomed, thanks to an unprecedented monster: Black Dragon Duke Morgoth.
“Jin, I’ve dealt with countless matters of national importance in my twelve years as President of the United States. But one issue has always come before all the others.”
I knew the answer before he could continue.
Ever since Demon King Asmodeus descended upon this world, every country had been facing the same problem.
“The war against monsters.”
Donald nodded at my words, spoken almost under my breath.
“That’s right. Dealing with the Gates that remained after the Great Cataclysm—and preparing for the possibility of a second one—have been our highest priorities.”
He stared silently at his empty coffee cup, then added weakly, “And those preparations failed. Or, more precisely...”
“Something appeared that was too strong for us to handle, even though we’d prepared for it. I understand.”
Morgoth was that powerful.
Even if what I’d seen on the video wasn’t the full extent of his strength, no Named Monster that had appeared since the Great Cataclysm could compare to him.
Except one.
Demon King Asmodeus, the absolute evil called not merely a calamity, but the end of the world.
And besides...
“But those preparations could only be complete with *him*, couldn’t they?”
Donald nodded gravely.
“That’s right. Our plan lost its strength when Sky fell into a coma.”
Sky. Cheon Taemin.
If two atomic bombs had brought World War II to an end, Cheon Taemin had saved all of humanity by fighting his way through the Great Cataclysm.
*Right. Just as the Martial God did.*
I swallowed the words on the tip of my tongue. Donald continued.
“But Sky’s absence isn’t our only problem. Morgoth’s power is a calamity in itself...but there’s something about him that sets him apart from every other monster.”
Once again, I knew the answer.
“Diplomacy.”
“So you’ve noticed it too.”
“I’ve dealt with enough monsters to be sick of them.”
Just as I couldn’t count every meal I’d eaten in my life, I couldn’t count the monsters I’d brought down since my days as an F-rank Hunter.
So I knew.
Regardless of how intelligent or powerful they were, monsters were born with an instinct to kill.
*If anything, the stronger they were, the more they wanted to crush everything beneath them. They tried to settle everything with overwhelming force.*
Of course, there were exceptions.
The Skeleton King, who wasn’t here, was one. The Doppelganger whose actions had led to Morgoth’s summoning had even infiltrated human society long ago and worked in secret.
But Morgoth was different.
He wasn’t merely bluffing or trying to deceive anyone. He offered surrender in earnest, and if people accepted, he guaranteed their survival.
*A monster that keeps its promises.*
And that had caused greater division than ever.
“Twenty-three countries have already surrendered to Morgoth. Along with the Arab League, which suffered the heaviest losses, several major South American countries have given up resisting.”
“The Middle East has more or less fallen, but South America too?”
“What happened in Moscow had a huge impact. We tried to control the situation, but we couldn’t stop the news from spreading.”
Disaster breeds fear, and fear leads to fractures.
Faced with the most powerful desire of all—survival—people were crumbling one after another.
“Something similar happened early in the Great Cataclysm, but this is different. Everyone’s shaken.”
The reason humanity had managed to win the Great Cataclysm was simpler than you might think.
They united.
Ironically, it was their enemy, Asmodeus, who made that possible.
He truly lived up to the title of Demon King.
He killed those who resisted and those who surrendered.
He burned down cities and overturned mountains and seas.
Compromise? Promises?
To him, that would have been like a cockroach he’d found in his house one day pledging obedience in exchange for living there alongside him.
And so humanity had fought back with all its strength, united in purpose.
Fortunately, they’d had a savior in Cheon Taemin. They’d had no other choice.
*But Morgoth kept his promises. Unlike Asmodeus.*
He took human form and followed human ways.
For those who resisted, he offered devastating destruction and death. For those who surrendered, he guaranteed survival.
Like a cruel conqueror from the Middle Ages.
“If you hadn’t appeared when you did, I might be signing a goddamn surrender document right now.”
President Doramp smiled bitterly, but I couldn’t smile. My thoughts were racing.
*I appeared in time? Me?*
I didn’t know.
What if I hadn’t lost consciousness after defeating the Blood Lord?
If I’d woken up even a day earlier—or tried to log out just a few hours sooner...
*Drip.*
Blood drops fell, one after another. It was running from between my fingers where I’d clenched my fist without realizing it. After a brief silence, President Doramp spoke.
“Jin, it’s already happened. And nobody blames you. While you were gone, the rest of us were at our posts, and we still couldn’t stop Morgoth.”
I knew.
Ever since I’d gained powers unlike anyone else’s, I’d struggled at every turn. And as a result, I’d saved countless lives.
But the sudden surges of anger and self-blame still refused to fade.
*They probably won’t go away even after this is over.*
People called me the savior of a new age, but I was human, just like them.
I fixated on what I’d lost instead of what I had, and feared the danger that was coming.
And that danger was closer than I thought.
“Mr. President!”
An aide rushed into the conference room. Behind him, I saw familiar faces.
Every one of them wore a tight expression, their eyes downcast.
The air froze in an instant. At the aide’s touch, a holographic video sprang into the air.
*Pop.*
Through the constant crackle of static, a scene from tens of thousands of kilometers away filled the vast conference room.
A Dragon Lair rose over the blackened earth once known as Moscow, blocking everyone’s view.

chapters.title: Chapter 1154
paragraphs: Everything in my field of vision was dark and murky.
The magical power that had erased even the radioactive fallout drifted as a blackish fog, and the walls, arranged in the shape of a pentagram, towered like mountains.
And—
Goooooong.
At the center of it all stood that bastard.
Black Dragon Duke Morgoth.
KWAaaaaa!
In an instant split into ever smaller fractions, the gigantic black dragon opened its jaws, and an explosion of magical power burst forth.
A pitch-black pillar shot up from the highest spire and stretched endlessly onward.
It pierced the clouds and cleaved the sky in two, as if it meant to reach the distant moon.
No—maybe it really could.
It was the breath of the most powerful living creature in the world, and a roar filled with rage.
*Dragon Breath...!*
I barely managed to suppress the groan rising in my throat.
It was only a video, but the tremor and the atmosphere it conveyed were enough to awaken my instincts.
This was different.
I could say with certainty that it was on an entirely different level from any Breath I’d ever seen or experienced.
My heart was suddenly pounding wildly. The fine hairs all over my body stood on end, and the blood in my veins felt cold as ice. Together, they bore witness and passed judgment.
The One-Eyed Black Wyvern that had left me with an indelible trauma years ago.
The Water God Dragon of Dongting Lake, corrupted and driven mad by magical power.
Even Michael Silbert, who had made a Dragon Heart his own.
None of them had ever unleashed a Breath that powerful.
Perhaps it was the difference in their species itself, combined with the weight of power amassed over countless years.
*So this is a Dragon.*
Its terrifying power felt more real than a mere hologram. I couldn’t help but shudder—and neither could anyone else in the conference room.
We even forgot to ask the obvious question: *Why* had Morgoth fired a Dragon Breath into empty space?
But the next moment—
Fwaaaash.
As I watched the sky turn pitch-black, I suddenly understood Morgoth’s true purpose.
Rrrrrumble.
With a deafening roar, countless dark clouds surged in, covering the moon and stars. Then, like ink spreading through water, they took over the skies above Moscow for thousands of kilometers.
Like a single line dividing the world.
And the place where the abyss had settled resembled another world beyond our dimension, one humanity had only ever imagined.
The source and beginning of this entire calamity.
The Demon Realm.
Was this what it felt like to be struck by lightning right on the crown of the head?
The air had frozen. Those who grasped the meaning of the static-riddled holographic footage could only stare, eyes wide, unable to speak.
They clenched their fists as if they might crush them, gritted their teeth, and watched with bloodshot eyes.
At the same time, we heard it.
The cry of the black dragon standing atop the highest spire, calling out to the pitch-black sky.
“ᚨᚾᛊᚹᛖᚱ ᚦᛖ ᚲᚨᛚᛚ!”
The roar seemed to ring out not in my ears, but inside my head.
It was more than a sound; it reached the level of will. No one here—or anywhere in the world—could understand the mysterious language.
Except me.
“...Answer the call.”
The words escaped me in a groan.
Shaaah.
The clouds, swirling like the eye of a typhoon, parted.
The roar that had shaken heaven and earth vanished, along with the wind that had been raging like mad.
All noise disappeared in an instant. With even the air seemingly still, the world looked impossibly peaceful.
Until a dreadful wave of disaster poured through the gap in the clouds.
Krrrk—KWAaaaaa!
The empty space rippled.
No—it tore open.
Hundreds, thousands of Wyverns and Drakes poured toward the ground, their bright yellow eyes flashing. Countless monsters clung to their enormous bodies and wings.

When the Liches cast their spells in unison, the giant monsters plunging from high above like meteors drifted gently to the ground like feathers. Death Knights raced through the air on ghostly horses and led their legions across the vast ruins.
They roared with joy and bloodlust.
—GRAAAAAH!
Clang! Clang!
Countless weapons swayed like a field of reeds in the wind.
Thud. Thud. Rrrrrumble!

The giant monsters, each one like a small mountain, stamped their feet. Hundreds of Liches and Death Knights went down on one knee, while ten times as many dragonkin cut through the sky with savage beats of their wings.
All in reverence for the one being who had brought them into this world.
But the black dragon’s eyes were fixed on the camera, not on the Gate in the clouds slowly closing above, nor on the hundreds of thousands of monsters gathered beneath it.
“On my soul and in my name, I, Morgoth, master of the Silver Mountains and Archduke of the Demon Realm, swear this to you humans:”
The moment my eyes met the monster’s through the hologram, I realized something.
This video was Morgoth’s declaration of war—and his demand for humanity’s surrender.
“If you resist, I promise you an end more horrific than any you have ever seen. If you surrender, I promise complete peace and survival.”
But—
“If you wish to survive, come to this land, reborn under my rule, and swear your loyalty.”
Even so—
“But everything has its price.”
I hadn’t seen everything coming.
“Three days from now, I will sit upon the throne here and gladly accept the tribute you offer as a token of our eternal pact.”
Just how cunning Morgoth was.
“Just two humans—a paltry price next to the lives of billions of your kind.”
What his true purpose was.
“Make them kneel before me.”
The dragon’s eyes flashed, black as obsidian and swirling like the abyss.
“Cheon Taemin and Jin Taekyung.”
At that moment—
Ding.
A System notification pierced my ears with a chill, and a holographic window only I could see appeared, blocking my view.
Humanity was already recovering its stability faster than the various international organizations had predicted—or perhaps even faster than that.
The footage of Moscow’s destruction was enough to plunge everyone into an abyss of shock and fear. Yet a single fact announced less than a few hours later was like a ladder of salvation to them.

└ *He’s* back. └ Oh my God. Please tell me this isn’t a joke. └ It’s true. Official UN announcement. Turn on the TV right now. It’s on every channel. └ Holy shit, that’s incredible. I thought we were all done for. └ What the hell happened? I’m glad he’s back, but why did he only show up after things got this bad? └ Because while you were becoming Pornhub’s best customer, he was traveling the world and saving people. He already came close to dying in the Middle East. └ I’m genuinely worried about you, so delete that stupid comment before the FBI shows up in about thirty minutes, breaks down your door, and kicks your fat ass. └ What did I do wrong? I didn’t do anything wrong. └ He’s got a point, actually. The poor guy’s only guilty of having a lower IQ than a dolphin. └ Yeah, don’t be too hard on him. If you happen to run into him on the street, just put a shotgun round in him. └ You motherfukcer, you wanna die? └ Oh, our Korean friend is here. He’s so worked up he even made a typo. That guy won’t be able to play games properly anymore. Koreans never miss a target once they’ve locked on. └ And the Korean who gives him a headshot will probably be a kid around twelve. └ Anyway, the important thing is that we’re alive. └ Right. He’s back.
People quickly found hope again.
Ever since Morgoth appeared, the internet message boards had been frozen, without so much as an ordinary joke. Now they were lively again.
Everyone knew who *he* was, even without anyone saying his name.
That was what Jin Taekyung meant to humanity now.
Stronger than anyone, impossibly devoted, and able to overcome whatever hardship came his way and prove himself in the end.
Some still called him a second Cheon Taemin, but most disagreed.
Jin Taekyung had become the savior of a new age, one who needed no grand description.
He had done more than fill the place left by the unconscious Cheon Taemin. He had made it his own, dealt with disasters across the world, and saved countless lives. Who could take his place?
That was why people felt relieved.
Jin Taekyung was back. Surely everything that had fallen into disarray would return to its proper place.
Just as he always had, he would step in and set things right.
But less than a day later, a warning reached the Pentagon and the rest of the world. Humanity understood all too well:
“ᚨᚾᛊᚹᛖᚱ ᚦᛖ ᚲᚨᛚᛚ!”
How futile their brief hope was before the vast army that had invaded Earth through a Gate unlike any before it.
“But everything has its price.”
And how they were already listening to the monster’s sweet offer.
“Make them kneel before me.”
How cowardly the desire to survive could make them.
“Cheon Taemin and Jin Taekyung.”
Once again, the whole world was thrown into turmoil.
Some were enraged, while others kept their mouths firmly shut.
The former called for a fight to the death; the latter hid their opinions to avoid criticism.
But another half day passed.
Rrrrrumble!
At last, people saw footage of the monster army that had seized all of Russia and was advancing in every direction. They had no choice but to fall silent.
All thinking the same thing, though they couldn’t bring themselves to say it to anyone.

sentences.text: Everything in my field of vision was dark and murky.
The magical power that had erased even the radioactive fallout drifted as a blackish fog, and the walls, arranged in the shape of a pentagram, towered like mountains.
And—
Goooooong.
At the center of it all stood that bastard.
Black Dragon Duke Morgoth.
KWAaaaaa!
In an instant split into ever smaller fractions, the gigantic black dragon opened its jaws, and an explosion of magical power burst forth.
A pitch-black pillar shot up from the highest spire and stretched endlessly onward.
It pierced the clouds and cleaved the sky in two, as if it meant to reach the distant moon.
No—maybe it really could.
It was the breath of the most powerful living creature in the world, and a roar filled with rage.
*Dragon Breath...!*
I barely managed to suppress the groan rising in my throat.
It was only a video, but the tremor and the atmosphere it conveyed were enough to awaken my instincts.
This was different.
I could say with certainty that it was on an entirely different level from any Breath I’d ever seen or experienced.
My heart was suddenly pounding wildly.
The fine hairs all over my body stood on end, and the blood in my veins felt cold as ice.
Together, they bore witness and passed judgment.
The One-Eyed Black Wyvern that had left me with an indelible trauma years ago.
The Water God Dragon of Dongting Lake, corrupted and driven mad by magical power.
Even Michael Silbert, who had made a Dragon Heart his own.
None of them had ever unleashed a Breath that powerful.
Perhaps it was the difference in their species itself, combined with the weight of power amassed over countless years.
*So this is a Dragon.*
Its terrifying power felt more real than a mere hologram.
I couldn’t help but shudder—and neither could anyone else in the conference room.
We even forgot to ask the obvious question: *Why* had Morgoth fired a Dragon Breath into empty space?
But the next moment—
Fwaaaash.
As I watched the sky turn pitch-black, I suddenly understood Morgoth’s true purpose.
Rrrrrumble.
With a deafening roar, countless dark clouds surged in, covering the moon and stars.
Then, like ink spreading through water, they took over the skies above Moscow for thousands of kilometers.
Like a single line dividing the world.
And the place where the abyss had settled resembled another world beyond our dimension, one humanity had only ever imagined.
The source and beginning of this entire calamity.
The Demon Realm.
Was this what it felt like to be struck by lightning right on the crown of the head?
The air had frozen.
Those who grasped the meaning of the static-riddled holographic footage could only stare, eyes wide, unable to speak.
They clenched their fists as if they might crush them, gritted their teeth, and watched with bloodshot eyes.
At the same time, we heard it.
The cry of the black dragon standing atop the highest spire, calling out to the pitch-black sky.
“ᚨᚾᛊᚹᛖᚱ ᚦᛖ ᚲᚨᛚᛚ!”
The roar seemed to ring out not in my ears, but inside my head.
It was more than a sound; it reached the level of will.
No one here—or anywhere in the world—could understand the mysterious language.
Except me.
“...Answer the call.”
The words escaped me in a groan.
Shaaah.
The clouds, swirling like the eye of a typhoon, parted.
The roar that had shaken heaven and earth vanished, along with the wind that had been raging like mad.
All noise disappeared in an instant.
With even the air seemingly still, the world looked impossibly peaceful.
Until a dreadful wave of disaster poured through the gap in the clouds.
Krrrk—KWAaaaaa!
The empty space rippled.
No—it tore open.
Hundreds, thousands of Wyverns and Drakes poured toward the ground, their bright yellow eyes flashing.
Countless monsters clung to their enormous bodies and wings.
When the Liches cast their spells in unison, the giant monsters plunging from high above like meteors drifted gently to the ground like feathers.
Death Knights raced through the air on ghostly horses and led their legions across the vast ruins.
They roared with joy and bloodlust.
—GRAAAAAH!
Clang!
Clang!
Countless weapons swayed like a field of reeds in the wind.
Thud.
Thud.
Rrrrrumble!
The giant monsters, each one like a small mountain, stamped their feet.
Hundreds of Liches and Death Knights went down on one knee, while ten times as many dragonkin cut through the sky with savage beats of their wings.
All in reverence for the one being who had brought them into this world.
But the black dragon’s eyes were fixed on the camera, not on the Gate in the clouds slowly closing above, nor on the hundreds of thousands of monsters gathered beneath it.
“On my soul and in my name, I, Morgoth, master of the Silver Mountains and Archduke of the Demon Realm, swear this to you humans:”
The moment my eyes met the monster’s through the hologram, I realized something.
This video was Morgoth’s declaration of war—and his demand for humanity’s surrender.
“If you resist, I promise you an end more horrific than any you have ever seen.
If you surrender, I promise complete peace and survival.”
But—
“If you wish to survive, come to this land, reborn under my rule, and swear your loyalty.”
Even so—
“But everything has its price.”
I hadn’t seen everything coming.
“Three days from now, I will sit upon the throne here and gladly accept the tribute you offer as a token of our eternal pact.”
Just how cunning Morgoth was.
“Just two humans—a paltry price next to the lives of billions of your kind.”
What his true purpose was.
“Make them kneel before me.”
The dragon’s eyes flashed, black as obsidian and swirling like the abyss.
“Cheon Taemin and Jin Taekyung.”
At that moment—
Ding.
A System notification pierced my ears with a chill, and a holographic window only I could see appeared, blocking my view.
Humanity was already recovering its stability faster than the various international organizations had predicted—or perhaps even faster than that.
The footage of Moscow’s destruction was enough to plunge everyone into an abyss of shock and fear.
Yet a single fact announced less than a few hours later was like a ladder of salvation to them.

Please tell me this isn’t a joke. └ It’s true.
Official UN announcement.
Turn on the TV right now.
It’s on every channel. └ Holy shit, that’s incredible.
I thought we were all done for. └ What the hell happened?
I’m glad he’s back, but why did he only show up after things got this bad? └ Because while you were becoming Pornhub’s best customer, he was traveling the world and saving people.

paragraphs: “Russia has officially declared its surrender. General Vasily Gerasimov, current Chief of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces and acting president since the Moscow catastrophe, has...”
Beep.
“Eastern European countries, particularly Ukraine and Belarus, which suffered severe damage from yesterday’s catastrophe in Moscow, are mobilizing all available forces along their borders...”
Beep.
“We now bring you an update on the current disaster. Over the past eleven days, the world has seen an average of more than four Monster Waves and around fifty Mutated Gate incidents every day.”
“That’s truly horrifying news. Amy, what about the magical power distribution?”
“I’m afraid I have bad news, Steve. Today’s magical power distribution rose by 2.8 points.”
“What?”
“Yes. A full 2.8 points. If you’re having trouble judging what that means, take a close look at this graphic.”
“Here, it says the daily increase was 5.0 points. What’s the problem, you ask? This graph shows how magical power distribution changed at the beginning of the Great Cataclysm.”

“In other words, we’ve caught up to more than half of the magical power levels from the Great Cataclysm. In the Middle East, where Monster Waves and Mutated Gate incidents have been occurring in particularly high numbers, it’s no exaggeration to say that a second Great Cataclysm has begun.”
“And on top of that, the situation around Moscow is already... I’m sure you all know. There’s only one thing I can say.”
“May God be with you.”
Beep.

“Breaking news. Morgoth has accepted Russia’s surrender. As of 16:30 South Standard Time, the Russian Federation will disarm completely and, like the twenty-odd countries that surrendered before it, retain its current system of government.”
“Meanwhile, a large number of Hunter groups opposed to the decision have reportedly engaged monsters in battles throughout Russia...”
Beep.
“...I agree with part of what you’re saying. Our situation is extremely difficult right now.”
“Should we take that to mean humanity ought to surrender?”
“Not at all. I’m simply speaking on the basis of statistical evidence.”
“But according to what you said earlier, Doctor, humanity has no chance of defeating Morgoth, does it?”
“I’m beginning to wonder if your ears are attached to your anus. As I’ve told you several times, the chance is exactly 5.2 percent.”
“That’s an embarrassingly low probability. I’m sure our viewers are thinking the same thing.”
“I won’t deny the odds are low. But understand this: compared with when the Great Cataclysm first began, that figure is dramatically higher.”
“I know. According to that excellent paper that even won you a Nobel Prize, the figure was 0.2 percent.”
“Congratulations. Unlike your ears, your eyes seem to be in the right place.”
“Thank you. But I can’t overlook the fact that the 0.2 percent in your paper applied only to the period before Sky appeared.”
“True. But even Sky—”
“—had less than a 20 percent chance of winning right up until the final battle with the Demon King Asmodeus. Yes, I know. But unlike then, humanity has another option now, doesn’t it?”
“You!”
“It’s a reality too appalling to say aloud, but we can’t ignore it forever. Before it’s too late, we need to face the problem in front of us. Don’t you agree?”

“Thirty years ago, we had no choice. We could only resist with everything we had. But Morgoth is offering peace, and the countries that surrendered to him have kept their governments and are calming their people.”
“...Morgoth is a monster. A fucking monster. Do you really not understand what that cunning bastard wants?”
“I know exactly what people want. Peace. A chance to protect the lives of the people they love.”

“Bullshit. Listen, young man, cut the nonsense. You’re nothing but a despicable coward. You’re hypnotizing yourself into thinking you speak for all of humanity while arguing that we should offer up a living sacrifice. And not just anyone—two heroes who’ve done more for us than anyone else.”
“Sky and Jin are heroes who’ll be remembered throughout human history. I’m grateful for their sacrifices, too.”

“If that’s true, then shut your damn mouth and go home right now. Hug your family, one by one. Then go to your study and take out the pistol you’ve hidden there. No need to bother writing a will. Everyone watching this broadcast, myself included, knows why you need to die.”
“My, how rude. I’m simply saying I expect those two to choose a noble sacrifice of their own accord, as great heroes would, for the sake of billions of people—”
“Fine. Then I have no choice.”
“What?”
“Go to hell, you son of a bitch.”
Bang! Bang-bang!
“Aaah!”
“Fuck! Healer! Get a healer in here, now!”
“Doctor, calm down and put the gun down! This is a warn—”
BEEEEEP!
“We apologize for the unfortunate incident during our live broadcast. We will do everything we can to resolve the situation—”
Beep.
At last, silence settled over the room. The Skeleton King stared without a word at the holographic TV, now giving off only a dim glow. Then he spoke.
“Humans.”
His voice was thick with unconcealed disgust. Chuck Hagel, who had been staring at the whiskey bottle on the table, answered him.
“As a human, I have to say, that’s a weird thing to listen to.”
“Why don’t you try arguing against it, then?”
“I’m not going to. He wasn’t wrong. Especially that last guy. He deserved to get shot.”
The Skeleton King nodded.
Even he thought the old doctor, the foremost scholar on the Great Cataclysm and magical power, had handled the situation admirably.
The man looked to be in his nineties and, far from being Awakened, seemed to need a shot of stimulants just to move. But America’s venerable martial art of gun-fu had no age limit.
“Do you think he survived?”
“He wasn’t hit in the head, so probably.”
“Pity.”
“I agree completely. But it’s better for that guy to stay alive. If he died there, it could actually hurt public opinion.”
“...Fair enough.”
In the silence that followed, the Skeleton King replayed the scenes he’d seen on TV.
Anxiety and fear boiling over everywhere.
The magical power distribution soaring toward the levels of the Great Cataclysm—and the nonsense now being broadcast openly across the world.
Things were happening everywhere that the Skeleton King simply couldn’t understand.
“You human, steeped in alcohol and tobacco. May I ask you something?”
“I quit drinking and smoking a few hours ago, but go ahead.”
“What is the essence of humanity?”
“That’s a difficult question. Philosophy isn’t really my field.”
“I already know you’re not particularly intelligent, so don’t worry.”
“...Fine.”
Chuck Hagel glared at the Skeleton King, then shrugged.
“All of it.”
“All of it?”
“Yeah. Everything you’ve seen and felt while you’ve been with us. That’s what I think, anyway.”
“Humans are stupid enough to make me want to crack open their skulls and examine their brains, and so greedy and cowardly it’s hard to believe. That’s their essence?”
“I wish I could deny it, but that’s part of it, too. It isn’t all you’ve seen, though, is it?”
Of course it wasn’t.
If all the Skeleton King had ever seen were those ugly sides of humanity, he never would have lived among them in human form.
He liked humans.
He’d always felt different from ordinary monsters. Ever since he’d met a human in the dark forest inside a Gate, he’d stayed with them.
But...
“Even so, this... This shouldn’t be possible.”
“Listen, my bony friend. There’s no such thing as impossible.”
Chuck Hagel ran his fingers over the whiskey bottle, still unopened after several hours, as if testing the limits of his own patience. Then he added:
“Things that should never happen are happening anyway.”
“Then...”
“Right. More people will start agreeing with that damn ‘noble sacrifice’ the guy who just got shot was talking about. Humanity’s running out of time, but it has a choice.”
“Even if humans have an evil side, they’d offer up the heroes who risked their lives fighting for them?”
“Offer them up? What are you talking about?”

“I said ‘sacrifice.’ That’s what they really want. To look away without getting their hands dirty or taking the blame. To leave the people they’d sacrifice with no choice but to decide for themselves.”
“The biggest problem is that Jin is exactly the kind of person who’d do it.”
For a moment, the Skeleton King bit down on his lip without realizing it.
Chuck was right.
That was the kind of human Jin Taekyung was.
He was always scolding and teasing the Skeleton King, but he carried a heavier burden than anyone else in the world.
And that made the Skeleton King more anxious than ever.
If the world wanted him dead, Jin Taekyung was exactly the sort of person who would sacrifice himself.
“That’s ridiculous. Even if that treacherous human... even if Jin Taekyung sacrificed himself alongside Sky, how could we be sure Morgoth would keep his promise?”
“Humans see what they want to see and believe what they want to believe. Morgoth knows that all too well.”
It was true.
As the news had just reported, Morgoth had kept his promise.
He’d left the governments of the twenty-odd countries that had declared their surrender in place, Russia among them, and completely stopped his monsters from killing people.
And that had given people hope.
Hope that Morgoth was different from the Demon King Asmodeus.
Hope that, even if they could no longer enjoy the freedom they’d had before, countless lives could be saved.
“But the chance that Morgoth will kill those two and break his promise...”
“Is overwhelmingly high. There’s no question about it. At least, we know that with absolute certainty. But do you think people, half-crazed with fear, are going to think that way?”
Chuck Hagel continued, his voice growing rougher.
“By the time those bastards realize their mistake, it’ll be too late. The only Hunter who can fight Morgoth right now will be inside that bastard’s stomach.”
As Chuck’s voice rang with pent-up anger, a thought suddenly flashed through the Skeleton King’s mind.

Hope that, even if they could no longer enjoy the freedom they’d had before, countless lives could be saved.
“But the chance that Morgoth will kill those two and break his promise...”
“Is overwhelmingly high.
There’s no question about it.
At least, we know that with absolute certainty.
But do you think people, half-crazed with fear, are going to think that way?”
Chuck Hagel continued, his voice growing rougher.
“By the time those bastards realize their mistake, it’ll be too late.
The only Hunter who can fight Morgoth right now will be inside that bastard’s stomach.”
As Chuck’s voice rang with pent-up anger, a thought suddenly flashed through the Skeleton King’s mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 1156
paragraphs: At the moment the Skeleton King thought of something during his conversation with Chuck Hagel, the man they were talking about stood alone in the deepest, most secret chamber of the heavily guarded Pentagon.
Or perhaps “alone” wasn’t quite right.
Strictly speaking, Jin Taekyung wasn’t alone.
“I should’ve come to see you more often. Circumstances kept me away.”
He looked slowly around the vast white space. It was as bright as if hundreds of lights were shining at once, and so empty it felt hollow.
“I heard you moved recently. I didn’t know it was to a place like this.”
He truly hadn’t. The moment he stepped inside, he’d been startled by the resemblance.
It looked so much like the mysterious space he called the Inventory, where he’d had an encounter he never could have expected.
“Just a coincidence, I’m sure. Probably.”
It had to be. The massive Grand Mage who had painstakingly designed this secret space for one person didn’t even know the Inventory existed, much less what it looked like.
But...
“Honestly, I don’t know what to believe anymore. I’m not even sure what I know, or what’s true and what’s false.”
At some point, everything he’d taken for granted had begun to fall apart. Faced with a reality beyond comprehension, his reason had grown hazy, and instinct had filled the void.
An uncertain instinct, closer to a wild guess—one even Jin Taekyung could hardly make sense of.
And now, reflected in his eyes, was the person who might well be the beginning and end of it all.
“Can you hear me? Can you see me?”
Jin Taekyung lowered his gaze.
Before him stood an oval recovery capsule connected to countless Magic Formations and machines. Inside that coffin for the living lay an old man, sunk in a sleep from which no one could wake him.
“If you can, please answer me.”
Of course, Jin Taekyung knew no answer would come, no matter how many times he asked or how long he waited.
Even so, he had to ask.
“Are you the person I think you are?”
The greatest hero humanity had ever produced.
His real name was Cheon Taemin. His titles were Slayer and Sky.
And...
“The Martial God.”
Jin Taekyung let out the breath he’d been holding.
Through the translucent membrane fogged by his warm breath, he stared at Cheon Taemin’s peaceful, sleeping face.
“I could feel it. The person I met back then, in that place... was you. I’m sure of it.”
Hiss. Crackle!

His voice had grown louder without him noticing, echoing through the space. His hand, tensing on its own, struck the countless protective spells surrounding the capsule. But Jin Taekyung paid no mind to the pain in his skin.
He needed an answer to the conviction he’d only recently arrived at, incomplete though it was.

He needed to confirm that Cheon Taemin and the old man he called The Helper were the same person. That Cheon Taemin, too, had been a Player like him. And he needed to know how things had come to this.
More than anything—
“Why? Why won’t you wake up?”
No matter how hard he tried to hold it back, the anger in his chest kept boiling over. He needed somewhere to let it out.
*Why do I, who fall so far short of you, have to bear this burden?*
At that moment—
Hiss.
Unable to speak the thought aloud, Jin Taekyung pulled his hand from the capsule.
Then he turned and blurted, “What, I thought it was one visitor at a time?”
His surging emotions weren’t the only reason he’d stopped speaking. A second visitor had just arrived.
“As far as I know, there’s no such rule. And even if there were, family ought to be an exception.”
“Wow. When you put it like that, what can I say?”
“For the record, I only just got here.”
“They say a guilty conscience needs no accuser. Who said anything?”
Jin Taekyung’s expression and tone were as playful as ever, at odds with how he’d been only moments before.
Team Leader Choi—Choi Minwoo—watched him for a moment, then shrugged.
“I should have knocked. Not that it would have made a sound through the barrier magic.”
“You didn’t have to go that far.”
“I suddenly thought of my grandfather and went looking for Mr. Johnson. I heard he’d already brought you here. I’m sorry if I intruded.”
“Don’t be. If anything, I’m the one intruding.”
Jin Taekyung smiled and waved a hand as he started walking.
“May I ask why you came to see my grandfather?”
After a moment’s silence, Jin Taekyung gave a short laugh.
“What, worried something might happen?”
In a situation like this, there was only one thing to worry about: Jin Taekyung taking Cheon Taemin to the Dragon Lair, just the two of them.
Of course, Cheon Taemin had been unconscious for a long time, and nobody in the Pentagon wanted that to happen. If it did, it would effectively be Jin Taekyung acting on his own.
But while Jin Taekyung’s question had sounded like a joke, Choi Minwoo’s answer came in a low, steady voice.
“Yes.”
“To be honest, I’m very worried.”
Before Jin Taekyung could answer, eyes widening, Choi Minwoo added calmly, “I’m worried that you, Mr. Jin Taekyung, might make the stupid choice of fighting Morgoth alone.”
“Answer me, please. Deny it if you want.”
Jin Taekyung stared at him in silence, then spoke.
“Fine. Let me make this perfectly clear. I would never do that.”
“I see.”
“Yeah. So that settles it, right?”
“No.”
“What? Why not?”
“Because I don’t believe you at all.”
“Anyone who knows you well would feel the same. Spend enough time around you, and it becomes obvious how recklessly and foolishly you choose to act.”
Choi Minwoo stepped closer and looked at his grandfather sleeping inside the recovery capsule.
“My maternal grandfather must have been the same. The two of you are so alike.”
“Alike?”
“Yes. Realizing that has brought me a little comfort. Only very recently, in fact.”
“What do you mean...?”
“Even after you came back from the Middle East, you haven’t gone to see your family. Even though you’re staying right here in the Pentagon.”
*Family.*
At that one word, Jin Taekyung’s eyes trembled.
His mother and younger sister. His family by blood, more precious to him than anything else in the world, had been under the Pentagon’s protection for quite some time.
But he hadn’t gone to see them once.
No. He couldn’t see them.
If he did, the invisible pillar barely holding him up would collapse. And if he crumbled now, he wouldn’t be able to summon even the smallest shred of courage.
“You’ve refused to meet the other Guild members, too. I’m sure it’s for the same reason.”
Jin Taekyung had come to know countless Hunters, but there were only two people left whom he and Choi Minwoo could call Guild members.
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong.
Jin Taekyung had avoided them, too.
The path ahead of him was riddled with danger. Death came for everyone, but it didn’t come for everyone at the same speed.
What would happen if those two joined the battle to come, when neither was an S-rank Hunter or a Supreme Peak master?
*They’d die. Without a doubt.*
This was a colossal gamble with the lives of billions at stake, not just his own. In a world without the Three Saints or the Fire King, he couldn’t bear the weight he alone had to carry.
So he ran.
From his family. From his friends.

He’d fled everyone around him and come here, wanting to face Cheon Taemin once more, even like this. The only person who could understand him. The person who might hold the answer—and the key—to everything.
Then Choi Minwoo’s next words reached him, and Jin Taekyung realized something.
“Watching you, Mr. Jin Taekyung, finally made me understand how my grandfather felt when he never came to see his only grandson.”
Something he’d failed to notice until now.
“Maybe I just want to find a reason for it. But... I’ve decided to think that he had no choice but to keep me at a distance because of some danger only he could sense.”
Choi Minwoo’s voice held a bitter smile. And in his words was a meaning even he hadn’t noticed.
*Some danger only he could sense?*
That couldn’t be. At the time, there had been no danger left for humanity.

The once-mighty Demon King Asmodeus had been reduced to dust, without even a body left behind. The monster legions that had stained the Five Oceans and Six Continents with blood had become nothing more than prey.
Yet as soon as peace arrived, the hero who had achieved that great feat shut himself away from the world.
He kept everyone at a distance.
No one was an exception.
Not even his closest companions, practically sworn brothers, or the daughter he’d cherished above all else.
When that daughter and her husband died in an accident, he left his young grandson in Butler Kim’s care rather than look after the boy himself.
Then, one day, without warning, he lost consciousness.
And remained unconscious for more than a decade.
*...Were you that afraid, too?*
With those words swallowed on the tip of his tongue, Jin Taekyung gazed at Cheon Taemin, his eyes sinking into darkness.
He’d been right.
He still had no definite proof or testimony, but Choi Minwoo’s words had made him see it again: Cheon Taemin and the Martial God had been the same person all along.
The shadow of that old hero, sleeping as if dead, stretched across two worlds.
*He knew. He knew it wasn’t over yet. That Asmodeus hadn’t been completely erased.*
There was still so much Jin Taekyung hadn’t uncovered, so much he wanted to ask.
But this was enough.
At least he now knew what choice he had to make.
Step.
He turned without hesitation and started walking.
He’d taken only a few steps when he noticed a tiny but important change and stopped.
The door.
It was gone.
The only exit from this secret space, created through advanced magic, had vanished without a trace.
“Team Leader.”
At his quiet call, Jin Taekyung turned. Choi Minwoo stood there, his expression unwavering.
“I’m sorry.”
The brief, calm apology told Jin Taekyung everything.
“Was this your plan from the beginning?”
“As I said earlier, we know exactly what kind of person you are, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“We?”
“Of course, this wasn’t a decision I made on my own. Most of them, including Mr. Johnson and me, have already agreed to the plan.”
“Most? Then someone must have opposed this ridiculous plan.”
“No. No one did. We didn’t tell the people who might have caused trouble from the start, in case they became an unexpected variable. We’ve also made every other preparation we can.”
Thinking of Chuck Hagel and the Skeleton King, who still knew nothing about it, Choi Minwoo continued in a composed voice.
“So... for the time we have left, you’ll stay here with me, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
The many people involved in the plan had a single goal: use every means at their disposal to keep Jin Taekyung—their only hope—here until the three days Morgoth had declared to the world were over.
Fortunately, the secret space Jin Taekyung had found was perfectly suited to carry out the plan. Countless barrier spells had been installed to protect Cheon Taemin.
Even so, one unpredictable element remained: Jin Taekyung himself.
The savior of a new age.
The greatest and strongest Hunter in the world, successor to Cheon Taemin—a man no one else could replace.
That was precisely why they couldn’t let him sacrifice himself in vain. And Choi Minwoo hadn’t forgotten one final precaution.
“No matter how strong you are, Mr. Jin Taekyung, you won’t be able to get out of here.”
“Is that so?”
Jin Taekyung reached into the air. A silver spear, invisible until now, appeared in his grasp.
Whoosh.
Dark blue flames surged along White Flame’s spearhead. The fire was refined to an extraordinary degree and carried heat beyond anything Choi Minwoo had felt from it the last time he’d seen it.
But Choi Minwoo didn’t waver.
“Come to think of it, there’s one thing I haven’t told you.”
The final precaution he’d taken was never meant to counter Jin Taekyung’s strength.
“If you try to break the barrier spells by force, the resulting backlash could bring down the entire Pentagon.”
At least, Choi Minwoo didn’t waver until he heard Jin Taekyung’s answer.
“You really think so?”
Grgrgrk.
As the space warped beneath the unbearable heat, Jin Taekyung’s quiet voice echoed through it like a distant refrain.
“I think otherwise.”
Choi Minwoo’s eyes widened.
Slice.
Along a seam only one person could see, the vast wave of mana that joined and sustained hundreds of spells split in two.

chapters.title: Chapter 1157
paragraphs: The spearhead, wreathed in dark blue flames, rose as if to pierce the ceiling. Choi Minwoo wasn’t the only one whose eyes went wide.
There wasn’t even time to utter a curse.

Magic Johnson stared in shock at Jin Taekyung’s unexpected move. He’d designed this secret space himself, and he’d been watching what happened inside it with a heavy heart. Now he felt as if even the hair he didn’t have was standing on end.
*No way. Surely not.*
He swallowed hard.
Why was he so tense?
Simple. If the magic was forcibly broken, the backlash would batter him—the caster—before it ever shook the Pentagon.
No. Maybe...
*I could die.*

To a mage, mana was another sense beyond the five, as much a part of the body as flesh and bone. When a spell cast with a mage’s own mana was forcibly dispelled, the mage suffered a worse blow than anyone else.
Magic Johnson knew that better than most. He’d only done something as insane as packing hundreds of security and barrier spells into the space because he trusted Jin Taekyung.
He trusted that the Jin Taekyung he knew would never hurt him.
But at that very moment—
Whoosh!
The spearhead swept down without hesitation, mercilessly cutting through the last shred of his trust.
“Fuuuck—!”
Johnson squeezed his eyes shut and finally let out the curse he’d been holding back.
The mana links connecting him to countless spells snapped. He felt the onset of a backlash powerful enough to kill him.
A warm breeze blew past.
*...Wait. A breeze?*
He heard nothing. Felt nothing. No earthshaking roar, no tremendous force rocking everything around him.
Only energy drifting away like sea fog in the sun.
His eyelids twitched. Unable to make sense of it, the massive Grand Mage finally gathered the courage to open his eyes.
Someone was standing in front of him. Johnson stared blankly for a moment, then spoke as if he’d made up his mind.
“Jin, be honest with me.”
Jin Taekyung straightened his spear. “Go ahead.”
“Did I die and go to heaven?”
“Whether you’re dead is another question, but isn’t this place a little bleak for heaven? We can’t even see the sky.”
“Everything’s hazy. Like we’re at the top of Mount Everest.”
“That’s water vapor, not clouds.”
“Damn, you’re right. Then if it’s not heaven, is this a dream?”
“I hope not.”
“Why?”
“If I’m showing up even in your dreams, maybe I’m your type.”
“Oh, dear. I hadn’t thought of that.”
Johnson gave a bitter smile.
“All right. So it’s come to this.”
Jin Taekyung nodded calmly. “Looks like it.”
“I’m truly sorry. I didn’t want to go this far.”
“I understand. I’m not just saying that. I really do.”
“Thanks. I think our friend over there feels the same way.”
Right on cue, Choi Minwoo emerged through the thick steam and studied Jin Taekyung with a complicated expression.
“You’ve gotten stronger. Even stronger than the last time I saw you.”

In Choi Minwoo’s memory, Jin Taekyung had always been strong. Even on their first raid, when Jin had gone along as a mere porter rather than a combatant. He’d gone on to surpass Choi Minwoo’s expectations by a staggering margin, again and again.
Today was no different. And that pained Choi Minwoo.
“To be honest... I don’t know whether I should be happy that you’ve gotten stronger again, or sad.”

Choi Minwoo had often thought about that famous line from a superhero movie that was now a classic: *With great power comes great responsibility.* Sometimes it seemed as though it had been written for Jin Taekyung.
To Choi Minwoo, Jin Taekyung seemed as vulnerable as he was strong. The stronger he became, the greater the threats he tried to face alone.
But Jin Taekyung’s reply was light and cheerful, nothing like Choi Minwoo’s words.
“Better to be happy, if you ask me.”
“Is that so?”
“That’s what I’d prefer. There’s always plenty to be sad about anyway.”
“If you died, what would I do then?”
“What kind of question is that?”
Jin Taekyung gave a short laugh.
“Be sad when it happens. As much as you want.”

Only Jin Taekyung knew why.
*If I died...*

Jin Taekyung turned that sticky, dark word over in his mind.

What he truly feared wasn’t death itself. It was what would happen after he died.
The danger the people he left behind would face.

Their eyes widened. Jin Taekyung added firmly, “But no one is to do anything rash until I give further orders. Unless I’m unable to issue them, of course.”
“Right. Good thinking. We’ll all fight together—wait. What do you mean, ‘unless you’re unable to issue them’?”

Maybe...

He’d only done something as insane as packing hundreds of security and barrier spells into the space because he trusted Jin Taekyung.
He trusted that the Jin Taekyung he knew would never hurt him.

“Fuuuck—!”
Johnson squeezed his eyes shut and finally let out the curse he’d been holding back.
The mana links connecting him to countless spells snapped.
He felt the onset of a backlash powerful enough to kill him.
A warm breeze blew past.
*...Wait.
A breeze?*
He heard nothing.
Felt nothing.
No earthshaking roar, no tremendous force rocking everything around him.
Only energy drifting away like sea fog in the sun.
His eyelids twitched.
Unable to make sense of it, the massive Grand Mage finally gathered the courage to open his eyes.
Someone was standing in front of him.

“That’s water vapor, not clouds.”
“Damn, you’re right.

“I hope not.”
“Why?”
“If I’m showing up even in your dreams, maybe I’m your type.”
“Oh, dear.

“All right.

“Looks like it.”

I didn’t want to go this far.”
