chapters.title: Chapter 1158
paragraphs: It was a ruin.
A complete ruin. No other words were needed.
But the man who had appeared in a sudden flash of light barely ten seconds ago saw it a little differently.
*A grave.*
That was the first thought that came to him.

He could feel it the moment he looked around—no, even before he opened his eyes. Death saturated the air like thick fog at dawn. From every corner of this enormous grave, where the clouds overhead shut out every ray of light, rose the screams of countless vengeful spirits.
“...I suppose so.”
The man muttered bitterly, then kicked off the ground and shot forward.
*Fwoooosh!*
Perhaps it was the magical power swirling in his wake as he streaked forward like an arrow. The spirits reacted to it, stopped screaming, and began following him one by one.
“Don’t follow me. I’m not your enemy.”
*Whoooom.*
Beyond the howl of the wind, the man heard the spirits’ answer and nodded.
“Yeah. I’m going there.”
*Whooom—*
“If that’s what you really want... Fine, I’ll allow it. Having you along for a little while wouldn’t be so bad.”
If an ordinary person had seen this, they would surely have been surprised by two things.
First, the man was behaving like a lunatic.
Second, this lunatic was someone the whole world knew.
But the spirits were different. Just as the man could sense their presence and hear their voices, they could see him as he truly was.
They were different kinds of beings, certainly, but death linked them.
“I know. It’s unfair. I’m sorry I couldn’t save you.”
The man went on as if talking to himself.
“Of course not. You did nothing wrong. It was just a misfortune, the kind that could happen to anyone.”
“You’re asking whether God or heaven really exists? Why?”
“...Your child, huh? I see. But don’t worry. A child that young would have gone to heaven. No, I’m sure of it.”
“I don’t know what God looks like. It was so long ago that my memory’s a little hazy.”
“You there. Take that back. I am a great being, far beyond the likes of you. My memory’s just a little bad, that’s all.”

“Yeah, damn it. You’re right. I don’t remember a thing. But ever since I started traveling with a strange fellow, I sometimes get déjà vu. Like I’ve been through something similar several times before.”

“I’ve given it some serious thought, and I think I must have been human once, too. An incredibly noble and admirable human, just like I am now—damn it. Everyone, quiet down. I’m trying to say something important.”
“Oh, don’t cry. I wasn’t talking to you. How old are you? Where are your parents?”
“...All right. I can’t promise anything, but if I find your parents, I’ll make sure you see them.”
The man continued forward, talking with the spirits as he went.

A young man who had only just taken his first steps into adulthood. An old man who had accepted his death and wanted to know about the afterlife. Parents who had lost a child, and a child who had lost their parents.
The scenery changed in an instant, but the spirits never stopped whispering. They were indignant and furious at the death that had struck without warning, grieving even as they trembled with fear.
And the man never once turned away from their voices.
Because he was their king.
He alone had the right and the duty to guide those who had lost everything in an instant and now wandered the Nine Springs—those who had become his people.
But perhaps the spirits weren’t the only ones finding comfort and peace in this strange conversation.
“Why did I come here? Hmm, excellent question. This is an epic tale that begins with the most handsome and admirable hero in the world.”
The man leaped over the ruins in his path and continued.

“The hero had many talents. He was incredibly strong and had a noble heart. But despite all that, he was surrounded by idiots and incompetents. Then one day, he learned that the biggest fool of them all was in trouble.”
But the hero knew the surest way to help the fool. It was something only he could do.
Because he was a hero.

“While the hero was deep in thought, some ignorant bastard who was crazy about booze and cigarettes told him that people see what they want to see and believe what they want to believe. So the hero decided to borrow the fool’s appearance for a while.”
It hadn’t been all that difficult. As he’d said, the hero was unbelievably talented, and his greatest ability was “absorption.”
“Actually, I didn’t know I could do that. No, the hero didn’t. But when he tried it, it worked. It wasn’t nearly as good as the Doppelganger’s own ability, though.”

Was it because of his innate ability to grow stronger by absorbing the magical power of monsters that had been destroyed? Or was it because his magical power levels had already reached the point of going berserk?
Amazingly, the hero, who wasn’t human, had gained a new power he’d never discovered before. After traveling thousands of kilometers by way of several Warp Gates, he had made it here.
Of course, there had been some trouble along the way.
He’d threatened the mages who refused to activate the Warp Gate. Or he’d taken a selfie in his current appearance, posted it on social media, and deliberately spread the word far and wide.
But none of those little things mattered to the man.
The crowning touch of his story was still to come.
“Most of you figured it out from the start, didn’t you? Yes, that’s right. I am that hero.”
*Fwoosh.*
Silence fell. The man blinked, his solemn declaration still hanging in the air.
“Why is everyone so quiet? You’d think you were dead. Oh, right. You are dead.”
“What? You didn’t see it coming? That’s impossible. The foreshadowing was perfect from the start. I said I was the most handsome and excellent man in the world—damn it. Forget it. You stupid humans.”
That was when the grumbling man suddenly stopped walking.
“...I’m here already?”
He murmured and looked at the scenery, now completely transformed.
As if someone had drawn a line across the world, pitch-black earth lay only a few steps ahead, starkly different from the ground behind him.
*Whooom. Whoooooom—*
At the same time, the countless spirits surrounding him began to scream.
Screams filled with a terror unlike anything they had shown before.
“Don’t be so afraid. Weak spirits like you would have a hard time entering that place anyway. Not that I was planning to take you with me in the first place.”
But the man was different.
While the spirits writhed as if burned by fire, he knew he would grow stronger the closer he came to that ominous, pitch-black earth.
*After all, the only thing I can fake is my appearance.*
The thought faded hollowly in his mind as he drew the sword tucked at his waist.
*Shing.*
Its blade was clear as untainted ice.
The man silently gazed at his reflection.
Or rather, at the face of the person who was probably chasing him as fast as he could somewhere out there.
“You’re a step too late this time, you wily human bastard.”
The man—the Skeleton King—snickered. Someone reflected in the blade snickered along with him.
“Yeah, keep smiling like that. Don’t scowl with that ugly face of yours.”
He meant it.
That fool—Jin Taekyung—deserved to smile.
“Then, here I go.”
With a final farewell that would never reach him, the Skeleton King took a firm step forward.
Using the light spilling from his sword as a torch, he headed for the land of death, where magical power churned, and thought:
*Sacrifice, huh? This isn’t so bad.*
Even if he died, he wouldn’t regret it.
Once he met a glorious end in the form of Jin Taekyung—not the Skeleton King or the Stone-King—all of humanity would understand.
They would see how foolish they had been to believe the monster’s promise to stop the destruction and slaughter if they handed over Jin Taekyung.
And they would understand the only way to escape this catastrophe.
*Fwoooosh.*
The dense fog drifting over the pitch-black earth swallowed his retreating figure.
Morgoth recalled an old saying he’d heard long ago: Sometimes, a certain kind of curiosity can shorten a person’s life.
He’d first heard it while living among humans, and it had fascinated him.
Unlike humans, Dragons couldn’t live long without curiosity. Morgoth himself was a prime example.
He had always been curious.
Ever since he was no more than a Hatchling—before he’d even broken out of his egg.
Perhaps that was why Morgoth had become unlike other Dragons.
His curiosity would not rest until he had reached the highest level of whatever caught his interest.
Humans, Dwarves, Elves, and other races besides—driven solely by curiosity, he had spent ages among them, learning and giving in turn, and ruling over them as well.
No matter how often he changed his appearance or where he went, Morgoth was a born ruler.
His election as Dragon Lord before he was even a thousand years old was proof.
The pride of his race and the king of the world.
He was more complete and absolute than anyone.
At least, he would have been, if not for the one curiosity he had never been able to satisfy.
*The Demon Realm.*
The home of all monsters. A land of demons where poison, corpses, and death flowed instead of clear river water.
His curiosity about the unknown deepened with every passing day, until Morgoth took his first step into that forbidden realm.
*Yes. That was where it all began.*
But why? Even after an extraordinarily long time, the curiosity filling Morgoth’s heart had not faded.
And among his unanswered questions was one that, as the human saying went, might truly shorten his life.
*Asmodeus, why did you choose me of all people?*
Morgoth possessed knowledge and power beyond measure, yet he did not know why he had come to this world.
One day, a call had reached him from beyond those distant stars and the space between them, and he had answered it. That was all.
Which made it even harder to understand.
Unlike the others, he was neither devoted to serving Demon King Asmodeus nor willing to give his life for him.
*Besides, how could you, when you don’t even exist in this world, have prepared a stage like this?*
But Morgoth did not pursue these questions further.
No. More precisely, he had to set them aside for now.
The guest he had truly wanted to meet had just arrived at his palace.
“Come in, hero.”
Morgoth rose from his throne and welcomed his first guest with delight.

He was incredibly strong and had a noble heart.
But despite all that, he was surrounded by idiots and incompetents.
Then one day, he learned that the biggest fool of them all was in trouble.”
But the hero knew the surest way to help the fool.
It was something only he could do.
Because he was a hero.
“While the hero was deep in thought, some ignorant bastard who was crazy about booze and cigarettes told him that people see what they want to see and believe what they want to believe.
So the hero decided to borrow the fool’s appearance for a while.”
It hadn’t been all that difficult.
As he’d said, the hero was unbelievably talented, and his greatest ability was “absorption.”
“Actually, I didn’t know I could do that.
No, the hero didn’t.
But when he tried it, it worked.
It wasn’t nearly as good as the Doppelganger’s own ability, though.”
Was it because of his innate ability to grow stronger by absorbing the magical power of monsters that had been destroyed?
Or was it because his magical power levels had already reached the point of going berserk?
Amazingly, the hero, who wasn’t human, had gained a new power he’d never discovered before.
After traveling thousands of kilometers by way of several Warp Gates, he had made it here.
Of course, there had been some trouble along the way.
He’d threatened the mages who refused to activate the Warp Gate.
Or he’d taken a selfie in his current appearance, posted it on social media, and deliberately spread the word far and wide.
But none of those little things mattered to the man.
The crowning touch of his story was still to come.
“Most of you figured it out from the start, didn’t you?
Yes, that’s right.
I am that hero.”
*Fwoosh.*
Silence fell.
The man blinked, his solemn declaration still hanging in the air.
“Why is everyone so quiet?
You’d think you were dead.
Oh, right.
You are dead.”
“What?
You didn’t see it coming?
That’s impossible.
The foreshadowing was perfect from the start.
I said I was the most handsome and excellent man in the world—damn it.
Forget it.
You stupid humans.”
That was when the grumbling man suddenly stopped walking.
“...I’m here already?”
He murmured and looked at the scenery, now completely transformed.
As if someone had drawn a line across the world, pitch-black earth lay only a few steps ahead, starkly different from the ground behind him.
*Whooom.
Whoooooom—*
At the same time, the countless spirits surrounding him began to scream.
Screams filled with a terror unlike anything they had shown before.
“Don’t be so afraid.
Weak spirits like you would have a hard time entering that place anyway.
Not that I was planning to take you with me in the first place.”
But the man was different.
While the spirits writhed as if burned by fire, he knew he would grow stronger the closer he came to that ominous, pitch-black earth.
*After all, the only thing I can fake is my appearance.*
The thought faded hollowly in his mind as he drew the sword tucked at his waist.
*Shing.*
Its blade was clear as untainted ice.
The man silently gazed at his reflection.
Or rather, at the face of the person who was probably chasing him as fast as he could somewhere out there.
“You’re a step too late this time, you wily human bastard.”
The man—the Skeleton King—snickered.
Someone reflected in the blade snickered along with him.
“Yeah, keep smiling like that.
Don’t scowl with that ugly face of yours.”
He meant it.
That fool—Jin Taekyung—deserved to smile.
“Then, here I go.”
With a final farewell that would never reach him, the Skeleton King took a firm step forward.
Using the light spilling from his sword as a torch, he headed for the land of death, where magical power churned, and thought:
*Sacrifice, huh?
This isn’t so bad.*
Even if he died, he wouldn’t regret it.
Once he met a glorious end in the form of Jin Taekyung—not the Skeleton King or the Stone-King—all of humanity would understand.
They would see how foolish they had been to believe the monster’s promise to stop the destruction and slaughter if they handed over Jin Taekyung.
And they would understand the only way to escape this catastrophe.
*Fwoooosh.*
The dense fog drifting over the pitch-black earth swallowed his retreating figure.
Morgoth recalled an old saying he’d heard long ago: Sometimes, a certain kind of curiosity can shorten a person’s life.
He’d first heard it while living among humans, and it had fascinated him.
Unlike humans, Dragons couldn’t live long without curiosity.
Morgoth himself was a prime example.
He had always been curious.
Ever since he was no more than a Hatchling—before he’d even broken out of his egg.
Perhaps that was why Morgoth had become unlike other Dragons.
His curiosity would not rest until he had reached the highest level of whatever caught his interest.
Humans, Dwarves, Elves, and other races besides—driven solely by curiosity, he had spent ages among them, learning and giving in turn, and ruling over them as well.
No matter how often he changed his appearance or where he went, Morgoth was a born ruler.
His election as Dragon Lord before he was even a thousand years old was proof.
The pride of his race and the king of the world.
He was more complete and absolute than anyone.
At least, he would have been, if not for the one curiosity he had never been able to satisfy.
*The Demon Realm.*
The home of all monsters.
A land of demons where poison, corpses, and death flowed instead of clear river water.
His curiosity about the unknown deepened with every passing day, until Morgoth took his first step into that forbidden realm.
*Yes.
That was where it all began.*
But why?
Even after an extraordinarily long time, the curiosity filling Morgoth’s heart had not faded.
And among his unanswered questions was one that, as the human saying went, might truly shorten his life.
*Asmodeus, why did you choose me of all people?*
Morgoth possessed knowledge and power beyond measure, yet he did not know why he had come to this world.
One day, a call had reached him from beyond those distant stars and the space between them, and he had answered it.
That was all.
Which made it even harder to understand.
Unlike the others, he was neither devoted to serving Demon King Asmodeus nor willing to give his life for him.
*Besides, how could you, when you don’t even exist in this world, have prepared a stage like this?*
But Morgoth did not pursue these questions further.
No.
More precisely, he had to set them aside for now.
The guest he had truly wanted to meet had just arrived at his palace.
“Come in, hero.”
Morgoth rose from his throne and welcomed his first guest with delight.

chapters.title: Chapter 1159
paragraphs: Boom. Rumble, rumble.
As the iron doors opened with a heavy roar, the Skeleton King had a sudden thought.
If he’d really been human, he might have mistaken the sound for his own heartbeat.
But even without a heart, he could feel it clearly.
With every step he took, the distance narrowed. With every iron door that opened in turn, the immense magical power ahead of him swelled.
And at the end of it all, the being at the source of everything waited for him.
“Come in, hero.”
The last door opened at the sound of a low voice, and the Skeleton King swallowed without meaning to.
*This is...*
Until now, his eyes had held nothing but darkness. Now they were filled with dazzling light.
Was this what it would look like if someone brought a palace from the myths of old gods into the world?

The chamber was hundreds of meters across, filled with antique furniture that had endured the ages and jewels of every color. Countless images were engraved into its towering ceiling and the walls on every side.
Beautiful.
No—more than beautiful. Astonishing.
Yet even amid that dazzling sight, the Skeleton King looked in only one direction.
At a being more beautiful than everything in the chamber combined, no matter how many times you added it up or multiplied it—and possessed of a power more terrifying than anything else in the world.
“You seem to like the place. Good.”
The palace’s master smiled as he drifted gently down from the throne towering in the distance, as if he’d spread invisible wings.
“I don’t need to introduce myself, do I?”
He certainly didn’t.
The Skeleton King knew who he was. So did all of humanity.
“...Morgoth.”
The name escaped the Skeleton King like a groan. Morgoth smiled and nodded.
“So you do know me. Still, it wouldn’t hurt to formally exchange names, as is the custom in this world.”
The Skeleton King understood what he meant and replied, thinking once more of the one person who wasn’t here—and shouldn’t be.
“Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung.”
“I see. Jin Taekyung...”
Morgoth seemed to mull it over.
“No matter how many times I hear it, it’s a strange name. Does it have some special meaning?”
“Of course it does.”
The Skeleton King shrugged, then gave an answer so perfectly suited to Jin Taekyung that, had the real Jin Taekyung been there, he might have mistaken him for a Doppelganger.
“It means ‘fuck you.’”
Morgoth stared at him, momentarily dumbfounded, then burst out laughing.
“Well, you got me. That’s rather funny.”
“Get all your laughing out now. After you’ve taken a few hits in a minute, you won’t find it so funny.”
The Skeleton King made no effort to hide his hostility.
The moment he’d faced Morgoth, he’d realized that a surprise attack meant to catch him off guard would never work.
*How is this possible?*
He’d never felt so overwhelmed just by standing before someone.
Strictly speaking, he’d felt something similar once, back when he was called the Skeleton Warlord and fought Jin Taekyung. But there was no comparing the two.
Just as the Jin Taekyung of then couldn’t be compared to the Jin Taekyung of now, the Skeleton King had grown at a terrifying pace, too.
If anything, his rate of growth might even have surpassed Jin Taekyung’s.
Since joining Jin Taekyung, he’d defeated one Named Monster after another, starting with the Arch Lich, and absorbed their vast magical power like nourishment.
He’d become so powerful that the title of king no longer seemed inadequate.
But...
*We’re on different levels.*
Undead: a cursed being.
A Dragon: a being born with the blessing of all creation.
The two faced each other at eye level, but everything else about them was different—their very natures, and the magnitude and depth of the power born of them.
So why did the Skeleton King feel more at ease as he gripped his sword hilt?
Even with Morgoth watching his every move, it felt as natural as folding his arms.
“Are you planning to fight me?”
“Why? Didn’t you expect it?”
“I did, from the moment you appeared alone. I only wanted to tell you it’s a poor choice.”
“There was never another choice.”
“Never another choice? I find it hard to understand why you think that.”
Morgoth tilted his head.
“I’ve lived for a very long time, and yet you’re a fascinating being. I’ve always had a weakness for exceptional talent.”
“So you’re telling me to surrender?”
“Become my Guardian. You’ll have the honor of protecting the true king at his side, and gain greater power and eternal life as well.”
“What an honor.”
“It’s an entirely reasonable and peaceful solution, too. What do you say?”
The Skeleton King gave a disbelieving laugh.
“Jin Taekyung.”
“What?”
“I told you what it means earlier.”
At that moment—
*Shing.*
A silver blade, its edge sharp as frost, finally emerged from its sheath.
“This is my answer.”
It was Jin Taekyung’s answer, too. The Skeleton King knew he would have done exactly the same.
Morgoth watched him and murmured, almost to himself, “How strange. I simply don’t understand.”
“What, are you that shocked I turned down your shitty offer?”
“I won’t deny that your foolish choice disappoints me. But that isn’t what I find so hard to understand.”
*Rustle.*
Morgoth’s obsidian eyes moved slowly over his opponent. More precisely, over the Skeleton King and the [Hero’s Sword] in his hand.
His next words sent a shiver through the Skeleton King.
“How can an Undead Monster like you wield an Ego Sword like that?”
“Oh, forgive me if I’ve offended you. It’s just that even I can’t explain what I’m seeing. Do you have any idea why?”
The Skeleton King didn’t answer.
He couldn’t. It took everything he had just to steady himself against the shock that had struck through his whole body like a bolt of lightning.
*He knew. He knew what I was.*
Since when?
When he gave his name? Or when he drew a sword instead of the spear Jin Taekyung always used?
Or... had Morgoth known from the moment he first set foot on the pitch-black ground of his territory, leaving the spirits’ pleas behind?
*Damn it.*
The Skeleton King clenched his teeth. He met the Black Dragon’s eyes, which seemed to see through everything he was.
“You were playing with me. From beginning to end.”
“Oh dear.”
Morgoth let out a soft sigh.
“Don’t let a misunderstanding upset you. Everything I’ve said was sincere. You truly are that special and fascinating. Even in thousands of years, I’ve encountered few cases like yours.”
“Shut your mouth.”
“How rude. But I’ll forgive you. Unlike an inferior race, I won’t let a moment’s anger drive me to destroy something precious. My intelligence and curiosity won’t allow it.”
Morgoth wasn’t the least bit shaken. If anything, he looked at the Skeleton King with even greater interest.
The old, cunning Dragon’s eyes glittered like those of a child heading into the hills to collect insects.
Even as a silver blade charged with powerful energy came slashing down at him.
*Fwoosh—CRASH!*
Fierce wind clawed through the chamber, and the energy carried by the sword swallowed everything within a radius of a dozen or so meters.
It was a blow so fierce that even the Named Monsters who had once struck terror across the world would have faced death if it hit them directly.
But before the roar rang out, the Skeleton King knew.
The strike he’d poured all his strength into hadn’t harmed so much as a hair on his enemy’s head.
Rumble, rumble...
Beyond the enormous tremor shaking the space, Morgoth had already moved to the towering throne in the distance. He brought his hands together in a heartfelt round of applause.
“Impressive. Truly impressive. Such immense magical power—and of so many different kinds.”
“Ah, yes. The Arch Lich, Leviathan, Behemoth. You absorbed their magical power. But your current appearance doesn’t seem to be the work of magic... Have you ever met a being called a Doppelganger?”
For an instant, the Skeleton King felt his mind go cold.
Morgoth had seen through him.
Too quickly, and with such chilling accuracy.
Seeing the Skeleton King’s face go rigid, Morgoth broke into a broad smile.
“So you have. You can absorb not only a target’s magical power, but part of their abilities, too. Astonishing. Now I understand how a mere undead—a Skeleton, no less—came to possess such power.”
“That mere undead might kill a Dragon here today.”
“Is that a taunt?”
“No. I mean it. It’s a lesson I learned from watching a certain lunatic of a human.”
The Skeleton King spat the words out as he approached. Morgoth nodded.
“Yes, of course you might. Even the mighty Asmodeus was stopped by a mere human. But...”
He looked the Skeleton King straight in the eye.
“Just as you learned a lesson through Jin Taekyung, I also realized the most important thing when I heard the news.”
*Whoooom.*
Space warped.
Incredibly powerful, pure magical power filled the chamber, taking the form of invisible blades.
“Asmodeus’s greatest mistake was his arrogance.”
“I do not underestimate any of you.”
At the moment the Skeleton King’s eyes widened—
*Fwoooosh!*
A flash of black, deeper and darker than the night sky, shot toward his entire body.

chapters.title: Chapter 1160
paragraphs: Undead.
Beings who had met death but had not died; who could move, yet could not be called alive.
But even the undead were not immortal.
They simply met another kind of death: Erasure.
*Erasure, huh.*
As time slowed, the Skeleton King watched countless black flashes fill the space around him and murmured to himself.
A path he had not yet taken.
And yet, one he would have to walk in the end.
He quietly closed his eyes.

Of course, he knew. If he moved now, he could still avoid Erasure. If he struggled with every ounce of his strength, until the last fragment of his soul crumbled into ash, he might even leave a tiny sword wound on that terrifyingly powerful Ancient Dragon’s body.
But it would be pointless. The gap in their power—the difference in their very being—was too vast for him to hope for anything more.
*There’s no turning this around. This body—no, Jin Taekyung—will fall here today. At the hands of a monster bent on destroying the world.*
And word would spread soon. Everything moved fast in this world.
That was why he had drawn as much attention as possible on his way here in Jin Taekyung’s form. By now, everyone around the world would be watching Moscow closely.
*If that happens, I won’t regret it.*
But unlike the Skeleton King, the people would regret what they had done—and be furious.
At the sight of a hero driven by an unseen hand to willingly meet his end, they would finally realize their mistake. Then they would unite and fight.
Even if the whole truth came to light, hearts once set would not be easily swayed.
*Yeah. That’s enough.*
But why?
Even after making that resolve and repeating it to himself countless times, why did his heart feel as heavy as lead?
The sound of space being crushed left his ears ringing. His eyes were shut tight, yet he could still see those faces and hear those voices. What were they?
And why—
*KA-BOOOOM!*
—hadn’t a single one of those terrible black flashes touched him? That tremendous magical power had seemed capable of devouring both his body and the soul within it without a trace.
*This is...*
A sudden sense of déjà vu swept over him. The Skeleton King opened his eyes.
And saw him.
Far away, the Black Dragon leaned back at an angle against his throne, staring at him with eyes that gleamed strangely.
“Just as I thought. Was that your plan from the start?”
“I suppose I should take back what I said earlier. It seems I underestimated all of you... No, I underestimated you.”
The Skeleton King’s reflection gleamed in eyes like pieces of obsidian.
The Ancient Dragon’s heart, worn down little by little over thousands of years, was pounding fiercely now.
“Why didn’t you dodge?”
The Skeleton King gritted his teeth. Morgoth’s question made it clear he had seen through not only the Skeleton King’s appearance, but the whole situation.
“Because I had to.”
*Crack.*
The armrest of the golden throne crumbled to dust.
But Morgoth was not angry at the Skeleton King for trying to deceive him.
He was trembling with rising excitement and joy.
*Because you had to?*
Yes. This was it.
If the Skeleton King had tried to fight back in any way, Morgoth would have erased him with all his power, without the slightest hesitation.
He had no intention of letting a moment’s curiosity cost him the two prized catches he sought: Cheon Taemin and Jin Taekyung.
*The Adversary who defeated the Demon King in a mere human body. And the one who leads the world after him.*
Those two alone had been Morgoth’s greatest purpose and reason for coming to this world.
At least, until a moment ago.
But what the Skeleton King had just shown him was enough to shake him to the core.
*A cursed undead monster, with a soul like this.*
Everyone wanted to live. Humans and monsters alike.
But sacrifice was different.
Morgoth had spent vast stretches of time among many races in the name of amusement. Yet even the Elves of the forest, supposedly the noblest of them all, had never astonished him like this.
No. There was no point in comparing them.
Just as Morgoth had been born to rule the world, they had been born with pure hearts.
But the Skeleton King was unmistakably an undead monster. A being corrupted by an inescapable curse.
And yet he had tried to sacrifice himself—an undead monster who should have been made of nothing but rage and fear.
Though he feared Erasure and had the power to delay his end, if only for a little while, he had refused to retreat.
*How is this possible?*
It was like discovering an entirely new species.
Morgoth had chosen to become an evil Dragon, abandoning everything he had built over the ages in pursuit of curiosity alone. Now he felt the strongest urge of his life.
More precisely, a greed that even his lofty intellect could not suppress.
*I want him.*
No. He had to have him.
A noble soul dwelling in the most corrupted of bodies.

If he could make this strange being, unlike any he had ever seen, completely his own, he felt he might grasp not only its extraordinary nature but also the unknown realm he had longed to reach for thousands of years.
The greatest question—and driving force—that had made Morgoth who he was.
“This won’t do. I can’t hold back.”
The moment Morgoth murmured to himself and rose from his throne—
*Flash.*
It happened in an instant.
Morgoth vanished without a trace, though he had been dozens of meters away. The Skeleton King, every nerve on edge, felt a sudden chill rush over him.
*Blink!*
The thought flashed through his mind, but it was already too late.
His opponent was a Dragon, born with a blessing of mana no other race could approach.
Morgoth cast a wordless spell as naturally as breathing, surpassed the limits of Blink magic, and struck the Skeleton King in the back.
*CRRACK!*
He couldn’t block it or dodge it.
With a dreadful cracking sound, his body flew like a cannonball.
Before the Skeleton King could regain his balance in midair, Morgoth leapt across space again and reached for him.
*Fwoosh—slice!*
A chillingly low whistle cut through the air by his ear.
At the same time, the Skeleton King put everything he had into widening the distance—and realized his left arm had just been severed from his body.
If he hadn’t twisted instinctively at the last moment, he would have lost something other than his arm.
*He was aiming for both my legs from the start. He wasn’t trying to erase me.*
Morgoth’s voice followed, confirming his suspicion.
“Stop resisting. You’re only wasting time.”
It was true. There was nothing to add to it or take away.
The gap between them was dozens of times greater than the distance separating them.
“I’ve changed my mind. I have to have you.”
Morgoth’s eyes flickered with greed now, not mere curiosity.
The Skeleton King couldn’t fully understand this change in him, but he was certain of one thing.
In the pitch-black darkness where he could see nothing, a faint glimmer of light had finally begun to seep in.
“I understand. I am pretty damn handsome, after all. In fact, it feels unfair to be stuck with a face this ugly.”
With a calm retort, the Skeleton King raised the [Hero’s Sword] at an angle in his one remaining hand.
*One chance.*
The only path left to him now. It would surely be the first and last.
*Vwooom.*
His enormous but murky magical power welled up, wrapping around his body and the silver blade—so utterly at odds with its nature.
Yet even that mighty power, rippling like living mist as it filled the space around them, could not compare to Morgoth’s.
“Skeleton King. You awoke in the darkest, coldest grave and took the crown in your hand—the king of the cursed undead.”
The Black Dragon Duke Morgoth, once a Dragon Lord who had ruled over three moons and a sun, twelve continents and nine seas, smiled brightly and spread his arms.
His impossibly pure and powerful magical power, worthy of his title as an Archduke of the Demon Realm, pressed down on everything.
“Come to me—to your true master.”
At that very moment—
*Fwoooosh!*
The space between them disappeared.
No—the Skeleton King saw it twist and vanish at the same time.
But unlike Morgoth, who came hurtling toward him faster than sound with wings of magical power spread wide, the Skeleton King kept both feet planted firmly where he stood.
All he had was the final strike he would make with his one remaining hand.
*Shwoosh!*
The tip of the sword shot through the air.
Without the slightest tremor.
Boldly, yet calmly.
Carrying a force greater than it had ever borne, it flew in the single direction its wielder intended.
Toward the Skeleton King’s own neck.
If a scream could make no sound, would it look like this?
In an instant divided into countless fractions, Morgoth witnessed the unbelievable sight. His eyes flew wide, and he reached out.
And then—
*FWOOSH!*
A flash deeper and more vast than any darkness erupted, swallowing everything around them.
If someone living in Moscow had survived to see it, they would surely have thought of one word:
Apocalypse.
The world’s death cry.
The end of all living things.
But in that place, already a land of death and little different from part of the Demon Realm, the first to sense danger were not humans.
*Thud.*
A rumble seemed to rise from deep beneath the earth.
The vast wave stirred something beyond instinct, reaching into the soul. Across the area, countless monsters raised their heads in unison.
Even the large monsters who, seized by a moment’s hunger, had been chewing a nearby Orc alive.
Even the Death Knights approaching to punish them, and the Liches raising undead monsters to reinforce their ranks.
Even the dragonkin circling the tall spires and beneath the black clouds.
Every last one of them stopped moving and turned toward the source of the ominous rumble.
The dwelling of the Black Dragon Duke Morgoth, now as good as their new king.
The Dragon Lair.
*Whoooosh!*
Suddenly, a beam of light shot upward.
No—darkness.
For some reason, it felt not the least bit familiar. It burst from the heart of the lair and rose skyward in a single enormous pillar.
Without end.
Erasing everything in its path.
It split the spires, the dragonkin, and the clouds blocking the light above them, then finally pierced the sky.
And then—
*Thud.*
The monsters watched the strange sight with vacant stares. At the same moment, they realized how precious the brief time they had just been given was.
*Rrrrrumble!*
A beam of light poured down through the rift in the torn black clouds, illuminating the earth as it heaved and rolled in waves.

sentences.text: Undead.
Beings who had met death but had not died; who could move, yet could not be called alive.
But even the undead were not immortal.
They simply met another kind of death: Erasure.
*Erasure, huh.*
As time slowed, the Skeleton King watched countless black flashes fill the space around him and murmured to himself.
A path he had not yet taken.
And yet, one he would have to walk in the end.
He quietly closed his eyes.
Of course, he knew.
If he moved now, he could still avoid Erasure.
If he struggled with every ounce of his strength, until the last fragment of his soul crumbled into ash, he might even leave a tiny sword wound on that terrifyingly powerful Ancient Dragon’s body.
But it would be pointless.
The gap in their power—the difference in their very being—was too vast for him to hope for anything more.
*There’s no turning this around.
This body—no, Jin Taekyung—will fall here today.
At the hands of a monster bent on destroying the world.*
And word would spread soon.
Everything moved fast in this world.
That was why he had drawn as much attention as possible on his way here in Jin Taekyung’s form.
By now, everyone around the world would be watching Moscow closely.
*If that happens, I won’t regret it.*
But unlike the Skeleton King, the people would regret what they had done—and be furious.
At the sight of a hero driven by an unseen hand to willingly meet his end, they would finally realize their mistake.
Then they would unite and fight.
Even if the whole truth came to light, hearts once set would not be easily swayed.
*Yeah.
That’s enough.*
But why?
Even after making that resolve and repeating it to himself countless times, why did his heart feel as heavy as lead?
The sound of space being crushed left his ears ringing.
His eyes were shut tight, yet he could still see those faces and hear those voices.
What were they?
And why—
*KA-BOOOOM!*
—hadn’t a single one of those terrible black flashes touched him?
That tremendous magical power had seemed capable of devouring both his body and the soul within it without a trace.
*This is...*
A sudden sense of déjà vu swept over him.
The Skeleton King opened his eyes.
And saw him.
Far away, the Black Dragon leaned back at an angle against his throne, staring at him with eyes that gleamed strangely.
“Just as I thought.
Was that your plan from the start?”
“I suppose I should take back what I said earlier.
It seems I underestimated all of you...
No, I underestimated you.”
The Skeleton King’s reflection gleamed in eyes like pieces of obsidian.
The Ancient Dragon’s heart, worn down little by little over thousands of years, was pounding fiercely now.
“Why didn’t you dodge?”
The Skeleton King gritted his teeth.
Morgoth’s question made it clear he had seen through not only the Skeleton King’s appearance, but the whole situation.
“Because I had to.”
*Crack.*
The armrest of the golden throne crumbled to dust.
But Morgoth was not angry at the Skeleton King for trying to deceive him.
He was trembling with rising excitement and joy.
*Because you had to?*
Yes.
This was it.
If the Skeleton King had tried to fight back in any way, Morgoth would have erased him with all his power, without the slightest hesitation.
He had no intention of letting a moment’s curiosity cost him the two prized catches he sought: Cheon Taemin and Jin Taekyung.
*The Adversary who defeated the Demon King in a mere human body.
And the one who leads the world after him.*
Those two alone had been Morgoth’s greatest purpose and reason for coming to this world.
At least, until a moment ago.

*A cursed undead monster, with a soul like this.*

No.

paragraphs: A storm.
A storm of power that swept away and destroyed everything in its path—and a colossal explosion born of the collision.
KABOOOOOM!

The world shook beneath a roar that seemed to split the sky. The monsters had been staring blankly at the Dragon Lair, forgetting even the savagery etched into their souls. Now they felt darkness fall over them.
Then came a force they could never have imagined.
Eyes wide. Mouths agape. Legs frozen by primal fear.
The monsters could not even let out a death cry.
No—in their final moments, the pitiful screams they managed were swallowed and erased by the deafening roar.
The impact was so horrific that “unprecedented” hardly did it justice. They were swept away helplessly, crushed into ruin.
RUMBLE, RUMBLE—!
Was this what it would look like if thousands upon thousands of meteors covered the sky?

The colossal castle, shattered into countless fragments by the blast, filled the air as its pieces plunged toward the earth. At the ends of their destructive arcs stood the monsters, frozen like statues.
CRASH! CRASH-CRASH-CRASH!
Destruction and death.
Those two things ruled the area in an instant. Sky and earth shuddered.
Everything mixed together.
Buried. Crumbling.
There was no way to stop it, no time to flee far enough.
Their tough hides and skin—so resilient that ordinary artillery could barely hurt them. Their bones, harder than alloy, and the immense durability those bones gave them.
Even the powerful magical power unique to high-tier monsters, which made all of it possible.
Nothing they possessed could save them from the death bearing down on them.
However brave a fighting dog might be, a tiger would still devour it. Strength yielded to greater strength.
CRUNCH! CRACK!
An ogre with both legs crushed let out a shriek. A Troll, half its body torn away by a fragment that had flashed past in an instant, shuddered and fell.
Even the Wyverns, descendants of Dragons who claimed the open sky as their domain, would never fly again.
Those closest to the explosion’s center had either died the moment the shock wave reached them or were now falling helplessly, their proud wings gone.
The explosion of power spread in every direction beyond the vast Dragon Lair. Its unprecedented magical power engulfed the monster army that had been in the area.
Relentlessly. Greedily.
The wave of death seemed as if it would never end. Only after swallowing tens of thousands of monsters did it begin to subside.
And at the center of it all, one being opened his eyes.
*Psshh.*
Ash slid down his slender frame.
Morgoth rose from the ashes of the Dragon Lair—no, even calling it a ruin would be too generous now—and turned to look around.

The earth had been overturned as if by a massive earthquake. Monster corpses lay piled like mountains. Green blood flowed in rivers, while a single shaft of sunlight peered through a break in the dark clouds at the dreadful scene.
Yet in this moment, not a hint of anger shone in the Black Dragon’s obsidian eyes.
“What a sight.”
The brief exclamation slipped through his parched lips.
That was all.
Though a moment’s carelessness had cost him countless subordinates, Morgoth didn’t care in the slightest.
More precisely, he had no reason to care.
He had gained a treasure far more precious and fascinating than those trifling losses.
“To obtain something, one must pay a fitting price. Don’t you agree?”
It sounded like a question to himself, but an answer came before long.
From right at his feet.
“Shut... up.”
At the faint voice, as hazy as a broken radio, Morgoth breathed a sigh of relief.
“I’m glad you still have some strength left. I was worried you might be erased.”
He wasn’t exaggerating.
The shock wave from the collision of two immense, utterly different forces had been truly terrifying.
If Morgoth hadn’t used all his power to protect himself, his entire body might now have been covered not in dust, but in his own blood.
“Still, there was some unintended damage... What can you do? This, too, must be the order of things, determined by someone.”
Morgoth smiled and brushed the dust from his shoulder. Like the dust drifting away in a pale cloud, the deaths of inferior monsters meant nothing to him.
Only one being mattered now: the one before him, his greatest interest and his sole objective.
“Thank you for holding on. You’ve exceeded my expectations in every way.”
In truth, even *exceeded* didn’t begin to cover it.
The blow his opponent had aimed at himself, prepared to be erased, had awakened a sensation Morgoth had forgotten over the ages.
*Tap. Drip, drip.*
Liquid began to wet the ground at his feet.
Morgoth frowned at his own silver blood, gleaming like molten silver, and at the blade jutting through his palm.
“Yes. So this is pain.”
A sensation he hadn’t felt in a thousand years.
It hurt all the more for that. Stung all the more.
Perhaps the memory of the last time he had felt pain made it worse—the day he had also endured a humiliation greater than the pain itself.
“...Asmodeus.”
Morgoth whispered the name. Then, as if shaking off the memory, he yanked the [Hero’s Sword] free and seized it.
*Crash!*
The blade split in two, and both pieces plunged deep into the ground, reflecting the image of their owner, now reduced to a head.
“Skeleton King. King of the cursed wraiths.”
Morgoth slowly bent toward the Skeleton King, who glared up at him, and stroked the skull where blue ghostly flames flickered in place of eyes.
“Can you see it? Your true self.”
“I told you... to shut up.”
“Calm your anger. You need only acknowledge and accept where you came from—and whom you should be with.”
His captivating voice rang out like a hypnotic spell.
But the Skeleton King didn’t waver.
Clinging to a thread of consciousness that seemed ready to snap, he squeezed out what little strength remained and spoke.
“You really are different from that guy.”
“That guy?”
“Yeah. An arrogant, downright devious human. But...”
That guy—Jin Taekyung—had once told him:
*You’re just you.*
And—
“He’s my friend.”
“He’s the one who pulled me out of that godforsaken darkness. He’s the one who showed me a new world I’d never known.”
He had seen so much.
He had learned so much.
He had left the Gate, where only darkness and death churned, and spent time with everyone beneath the shining sun.
There had been happy days and sad days, but every moment had been dazzling.
Because he wasn’t alone anymore.
Because he was with them.
That was enough.
“So quit wasting your time with that stupid bullshit. You’d better get ready.”
The Skeleton King smiled.
Brighter and more radiant than ever.
“My friends will be here soon.”
At that moment—
*Flick.*
Like a lamp going out, the ghostly flames flickering in his empty eye sockets suddenly vanished.
“...Your friends, you say?”
Morgoth turned the Skeleton King’s final words over in his mind. The Skeleton King had finally lost his grip on consciousness, leaving Morgoth to ponder them alone.
Friend.
A familiar word, yet strange, as though he were hearing it for the first time.
Though he had once spent many years among humans in another world, he had never been able to understand friendship.
Why did people who shared not a drop of blood care so deeply for one another? Why did they sometimes make the foolish choice to give their lives for each other?
Morgoth knew all too well that they did such things. Why they did so remained a source of fascination and astonishment to him.
First, that the Skeleton King—nothing more than a cursed Undead Monster—could show such humanity.
And second—
*Jin Taekyung.*
A human who might have changed the Skeleton King into this extraordinary being.
*There’s more I need to find out.*
Of course, Morgoth already knew about Jin Taekyung.
The savior of a new age. The center of this world, a young hero who stood at the head of them all.
After Cheon Taemin, Jin Taekyung was among those Morgoth had to watch most carefully. That hadn’t changed.
Now, though, Morgoth was intensely curious about him in a way he hadn’t been before.
“Yes. I’ll have to get ready, as you advised.”
Morgoth murmured to the silent skull, then looked out over the earth. The rumbling had finally stopped.

Perhaps it was the shaft of sunlight peeking through the split dark clouds, but the overturned, fractured land had lost much of the pitch-black color that had made it resemble the Demon Realm—and much of the dense magical power that had permeated it.
Morgoth didn’t care.
He began to rouse the endless power within his heart: magical power, nearly infinite and utterly pure, born of corruption.
Or rather, he was about to.
Then he sensed someone he hadn’t expected.
*Vwoom.*
The magical power that had seemed ready to erupt like a volcano sank back down. So did the Black Dragon’s gaze.
The air trembled uneasily. The wind fell still. Morgoth’s tightly closed lips parted.
“My apologies. I didn’t realize a guest had arrived.”
Dark mist drifted away as he spoke in a low voice.
Beyond it, someone answered.
“I’m asking because I’m curious.”
The voice was calm, yet seething like lava.
“What’s that in your hand?”

“I told you... to shut up.”
“Calm your anger.
You need only acknowledge and accept where you came from—and whom you should be with.”
His captivating voice rang out like a hypnotic spell.
But the Skeleton King didn’t waver.
Clinging to a thread of consciousness that seemed ready to snap, he squeezed out what little strength remained and spoke.
“You really are different from that guy.”
“That guy?”
“Yeah.
An arrogant, downright devious human.
But...”
That guy—Jin Taekyung—had once told him:
*You’re just you.*
And—
“He’s my friend.”
“He’s the one who pulled me out of that godforsaken darkness.
He’s the one who showed me a new world I’d never known.”
He had seen so much.
He had learned so much.
He had left the Gate, where only darkness and death churned, and spent time with everyone beneath the shining sun.
There had been happy days and sad days, but every moment had been dazzling.
Because he wasn’t alone anymore.
Because he was with them.
That was enough.
“So quit wasting your time with that stupid bullshit.
You’d better get ready.”
The Skeleton King smiled.
Brighter and more radiant than ever.
“My friends will be here soon.”
At that moment—
*Flick.*
Like a lamp going out, the ghostly flames flickering in his empty eye sockets suddenly vanished.
“...Your friends, you say?”
Morgoth turned the Skeleton King’s final words over in his mind.
The Skeleton King had finally lost his grip on consciousness, leaving Morgoth to ponder them alone.
Friend.
A familiar word, yet strange, as though he were hearing it for the first time.
Though he had once spent many years among humans in another world, he had never been able to understand friendship.
Why did people who shared not a drop of blood care so deeply for one another?
Why did they sometimes make the foolish choice to give their lives for each other?
Morgoth knew all too well that they did such things.
Why they did so remained a source of fascination and astonishment to him.
First, that the Skeleton King—nothing more than a cursed Undead Monster—could show such humanity.
And second—
*Jin Taekyung.*
A human who might have changed the Skeleton King into this extraordinary being.
*There’s more I need to find out.*
Of course, Morgoth already knew about Jin Taekyung.
The savior of a new age.
The center of this world, a young hero who stood at the head of them all.
After Cheon Taemin, Jin Taekyung was among those Morgoth had to watch most carefully.
That hadn’t changed.
Now, though, Morgoth was intensely curious about him in a way he hadn’t been before.
“Yes.
I’ll have to get ready, as you advised.”
Morgoth murmured to the silent skull, then looked out over the earth.
The rumbling had finally stopped.

Perhaps it was the shaft of sunlight peeking through the split dark clouds, but the overturned, fractured land had lost much of the pitch-black color that had made it resemble the Demon Realm—and much of the dense magical power that had permeated it.
Morgoth didn’t care.
He began to rouse the endless power within his heart: magical power, nearly infinite and utterly pure, born of corruption.
Or rather, he was about to.
Then he sensed someone he hadn’t expected.
*Vwoom.*
The magical power that had seemed ready to erupt like a volcano sank back down.
So did the Black Dragon’s gaze.
The air trembled uneasily.
The wind fell still.
Morgoth’s tightly closed lips parted.
“My apologies.
I didn’t realize a guest had arrived.”
Dark mist drifted away as he spoke in a low voice.
Beyond it, someone answered.
“I’m asking because I’m curious.”
The voice was calm, yet seething like lava.
“What’s that in your hand?”

chapters.title: Chapter 1162
paragraphs: For an instant, it was as if the world had stopped.
The faint haze of magical power around me, the mountains of monster corpses, the roars of the monsters that had survived—all of it vanished.
I could no longer feel or see any of it.

Only one sight remained: far away, a man with pitch-black hair hanging down like a cloak held a pure-white skeleton in his hand. The two of them were burned into my retinas as though they were the only things left in the world.
Pain clenched my heart.
“What are you holding?”
My restrained voice crossed the hundred or so meters between us. At the other end stood a man gazing silently at me.
No—a wicked Black Dragon wearing human skin.
“Ah. This?”
His voice was beautiful enough to seem otherworldly, and carried an evil so pure it was all the more horrifying.
“A clue to satisfying a desire I’ve held for a very long time. And a valuable trophy.”
One corner of Morgoth’s mouth curled upward.
“Perhaps someone’s friend, too.”
“A friendship between a human and a monster. A moving story. Judging by the fact that you’ve come here alone, it seems it was all true.”
I didn’t know exactly what had happened here, or what had been said.
But I was certain of one thing.
The Skeleton King had done everything he could, and he’d done it for me—for all of us.
That was why I couldn’t ask the most important question. His obsidian eyes watched me closely, taking in every part of me.
“Are you afraid?”
As if he’d read my mind. I answered briefly.
“Yeah.”
“Of what?”
“There’s a crazy Dragon standing in front of me, and he’s holding someone I know very well. I want him to still be alive.”
Maybe it was how readily I’d answered. After a brief silence, Morgoth gave a quiet laugh.
“You’re honest. Almost disconcertingly so.”
“So? Your answer?”
“Didn’t I already tell you? A valuable trophy. He was so violent in his rampage that he’s a little damaged, but I have no desire to see him shattered to pieces.”
The meaning was clear.
He was still alive.
The Skeleton King.
It was the answer I’d been desperately waiting for since the moment I set foot in this godforsaken ruin. Only then did I let out the breath I’d been holding.
“Thanks, you son of a bitch.”
“Don’t mention it. I couldn’t pass up such a precious opportunity after all this time.”
“You don’t make a habit of taking hostages, do you?”
“Hostage-taking? My intellect and stature are far too great for such cheap amusement.”
“That’s good to hear.”
“Perhaps. Or perhaps it’s the worst news you could have heard. I draw a clear distinction between trophies and everything else.”
“A distinction?”
“If something is too dangerous to possess, it must be destroyed. That way, there’s no trouble later.”
Morgoth’s smile deepened.
“Just like you.”
At that moment—
*Vwoom.*
Magical power churned around us. A wave of power, unbelievably pure and vast.
And murderous intent so vivid I could almost touch it.
“Was this your plan from the start?”
“No. But the moment we first met, I realized I might make the same mistake Asmodeus once did. And, more than anything...”
His gaze swept over me, unpleasant in its mixture of interest and regret, as though it could see through my entire body.
“Prey.”
His hair, long enough to reach the ground, rose into the air like the wings of a being from myth.
Not an angel’s wings. A demon’s.
“You already see me as prey, don’t you, Jin Taekyung? Young, strong human hero.”
For an instant, silence hung between us. Then I spoke.
“Yeah. I do.”
A Hunter. A sword and shield for humanity, and a hunter.
But that wasn’t the only reason I’d come to face him head-on.
If Morgoth had truly been someone I could trust, I would have gladly done whatever he wanted. I would have bowed at his feet. If he’d told me to cut off my own arms and legs, I would have done it.
My life?
If the deaths of Cheon Taemin and me could bring peace to billions of people, I would have given up my life without a second thought.
That was my duty.
But just as Morgoth had understood something when he first saw me, I’d understood something about him.
His eyes.
They were so clear they seemed pure—and no different from a child’s eyes as he watched an ant crawl across the asphalt on a midsummer afternoon.
That was why tens of millions of lives had been ground to dust.
Right here, in the very place where I stood.
And there was one more thing.
“He’s not a trophy.”
“What?”
“He’s not some trophy. That guy.”
My voice boiled over, so strange it sounded like someone else’s. I took a step.
Slowly. Heavily.
As I put my foot down harder than ever before, memories as vivid as yesterday sank in deeper than the footprint it left.
*Thud.*
“Human, why don’t you make a deal with me instead?”
“A deal?”
Yeah. It was there.
An A-rank Gate. Black Wizard’s Black Forest.
We’d first met in that dark, damp forest thick with dead trees. And then we’d stayed together.
For far longer than I’d expected.
*Thud.*
“Hey, Warlord Mon.”
“Do not call me by such a name. I am the master of the Black Forest and commander of the mighty undead legion.”
“Hmm. All right.”
“At last, you understand.”
“So, Golgoli.”
“...Damn it.”
I couldn’t say exactly when it had happened—when I’d begun to see him as more than just a monster.
“Something wrong? Why’ve you been so down all day?”
“I was just thinking about something.”
“What?”
“What kind of being was I, in the past?”
That day, I’d told him as he brooded that I didn’t really know, but he’d probably been a pretty decent guy.
I’d let the words slip as though I were talking to myself, embarrassed for no good reason. He hadn’t forgotten them.
“Human, I have a question.”
Even now, I could see it all clearly.
The spearhead of White Flame, which the Arch Lich had sent flying at me when I was too exhausted and injured to move.
The Skeleton King forcing his way out of my Inventory by his own power and shielding me with his entire body.
“Human. I have a question.”
That voice I’d thought I would never hear again.
“What you said to me before—did you mean it?”
“Of course I did.”
Only after hearing my answer did the dim lights in his eyes curve like a crescent moon.
“I see.”
The Skeleton Warlord I’d first met in the Black Forest fell.
“You asked me why.”
Then, on human land, a new being who’d sacrificed himself to protect humans rose once more with a shining crown.
He gave back the words I’d once said to him—words he would never forget.
“You’re cunning, but you’re a pretty decent human. That’s all.”
The Skeleton King.
King and master of the dead who wander the Nine Springs.
And...
*My friend.*
Hot.
My eyes, fixed solely on Morgoth. My two dantians, pouring out Scorching Yang Qi without pause like a volcano erupting after a long wait.
And the step I took, carrying every memory that had just passed through me.
*Crack.*
A deep rumble spread. The devastated ground crumbled again.
Hairline fractures spread in every direction like a spiderweb, then erupted.
*Fwoosh—KABOOM!*
Flamefire Path.
I shot forward as a single, blazing streak of fire.
It happened in an instant.
*BOOM!*
With a sudden flare of blue-black flames, the hundred or so meters between the two of them disappeared at once.
No—*vaporized* might have been more accurate.
The heat Morgoth felt was that horrifyingly intense, and the speed surpassed even sound.
But—
*I can see it.*
The Black Dragon’s obsidian eyes flashed as he read it all: the streak of fire rushing up to his face, and something suddenly emerging from its immense heat.
*Whoosh!*
Morgoth’s eyes flew wide. A silver spearhead slashed down at an angle, reflected in them.
Where had it come from? How?
He hadn’t sensed the power of any magic.
Before he could find an answer, the flames carried on the spearhead drove into his chest.
Or so it seemed.
For the briefest moment.
*Flash—slice!*
In a moment split into smaller moments, Morgoth crossed the distance in an instant. He silently raised a hand to touch the area around his chest.
More precisely, to the patch of skin that had been scorched black by the slightest graze.
It was only the third time in thousands of years that he’d felt pain.
But unlike the undead monster who’d caused him pain the second time, the human approaching from afar with his spear lowered still held immense power.
Enough to make Morgoth ask with genuine curiosity, “Are you, by any chance, one of my kind?”
Slowly but carefully closing the distance, Jin Taekyung answered calmly.
“Yeah. Long time no see, son.”
“Your vulgar speech makes it clear you’re not one of my kind...but how can a human grow so strong so quickly?”
Morgoth already knew about Jin Taekyung. He knew a great deal.
And until Morgoth had been summoned to this world, Jin Taekyung’s power had been nothing like this.
“A lot’s happened. Things even you couldn’t possibly imagine.”
“Things even I couldn’t imagine...”
How could that not fascinate him?
But Morgoth forced down the curiosity rising from deep within him. The human before him was too dangerous to let a moment’s curiosity distract him.
“A pity. I’ll never get to hear that interesting story of yours.”
Muttering under his breath, Morgoth curled both hands like claws and seized the empty air.
No—he tore it.
*Grrrrrrk.*
Warped space opened its jaws. Beyond the gap, where only darkness rippled, beings that had remained hidden until now emerged.
*Clank, clank.*
Sharp spears and blades. Armor covering every inch of their bodies.
There were hundreds of them—thousands—and they resembled one another like twins born of the same womb. Jin Taekyung recalled the first day he’d returned to this world.
“Those are...”
“My most loyal guardians.”
Dragon-tooth soldiers.
Guardians born of Dragons and existing only to serve Dragons.
But they weren’t the only thing that made Jin Taekyung freeze.
“...Faye Chen?”
A familiar face appeared among the Dragon-tooth soldiers, and a low groan escaped his lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 1163
paragraphs: Partings always brought sadness and regret.
All the more so when death made the parting with someone close permanent.
But this was never the kind of reunion he wanted.
“...Faye Chen?”
The name came out like a groan.
Even from a distance, the face was instantly recognizable. And yet it had never looked so unfamiliar.
No.
The faces.
“Long ago, in the world where I lived, there were some exceptionally gifted beings. They were called warriors or heroes.”
The wicked Dragon’s voice, steeped in old memories, reached Jin Taekyung as he stood frozen like a statue.
“At first, they were a nuisance. I didn’t much care for them coming all the way to my lair and behaving rudely over some trivial matter.”
Morgoth had never quite understood them.
All he’d done was burn a few cities and wipe out a kingdom. Why come all the way to his lair to make a scene?
“At least, that was how I felt until I met one human.”
He had stood out even among the hundreds of heroes who had come before him.
He was strong, resilient, and fought more desperately than anyone.
Perhaps that was why, when the man died without leaving so much as a proper corpse—reduced to a little pool of blood like all the other intruders—Morgoth felt regret for the first time.
Along with it came a powerful desire to possess him, rising from deep within.
“That was when I began collecting ‘trophies’ in earnest.”
Not mere cold, hard gold and jewels, but special trophies, each retaining its own memories and light.
Humans, elves, dwarves. Sometimes monsters.
Those he could force to submit, he did. Those who refused every offer, he killed so he could keep them by his side anyway.
His most precious trophies, given the name Guardians.
And he had continued this fascinating collection in the unfamiliar world called Earth.
“They’re still unfinished, but the material is good. The results are excellent.”
“What do you think of my new Guardians?”
Jin Taekyung didn’t answer the question, which was brimming with satisfaction.
He couldn’t. All he could do was look at the bloodless faces now standing at the head of the Dragon-tooth soldiers and recite their names to himself.
*Faye Chen, Joel Schumacher, Pablo Albatroses...*
Seven names.
Seven S-rank Hunters.
Heroes who had represented their countries. Comrades who had trusted one another to watch their backs.
Over the past several days of the Black Dragon’s great invasion, they had been reported killed in battle, their bodies never found.
Now they stood here.
Denied rest even in death.
Puppets robbed of their very souls.
*Shing.*
They raised sharp swords, maces, halberds, and shields. They drew their bows.
At Jin Taekyung, of all people.
At the one light that had shown them the way when they could see nothing in the darkness. Their hope.
*Fwoooosh.*
A cold wind swept across the devastated land.

The monsters had surrounded him on every side. Their murderous intent whipped around him like blades. Beyond the thousand Dragon-tooth soldiers forming an immense wall before their master, the wicked Dragon smiled, his teeth gleaming white.
“Now, shall we begin?”
Those words were the signal.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
A wave of monsters poured in without end, shaking heaven and earth.
At the same time, Jin Taekyung’s frozen expression shifted. His eyes narrowed to half-lidded slits.
*Whoosh—KABOOM!*
Blue-black flames burst forth, coiling around his spearhead and flooding the whole area with blinding light.
*Slice!*
He slashed.
*Thwack! Thud-thud-thud!*
He stabbed.
*Crunch!*
He smashed and crushed.
And then—
*Rumble!*
He pushed forward.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System** You defeated the Lv. 98 Enhanced Minotaur Warrior! You defeated the Lv. 110 Enhanced Twin-Headed Ogre! You defeated the Lv. 120 Enhanced Death Knight! ... EXP gained is reduced due to the difference in strength! You gained a small amount of EXP!
Jin Taekyung let out the breath he’d been holding.
The chimes ringing incessantly in his ears seemed to grow more distant. The monsters’ stench and roars had never felt closer or clearer.
“Gwoooar!”
Suddenly, a shadow fell across hundreds of heads.
A Cyclops—a one-eyed giant as tall as a walking skyscraper—slammed both fists down with a roar that shook heaven and earth.
*BOOM!*
Compressed air exploded. The mountain of force behind its fists crushed and burst everything they touched.
Everything except the one person it had to bring down.
By the time the giant spotted the human, smaller than its palm, a spearhead wreathed in blue-black flames was already driving into its single eye.
*Thud!*
The spear pierced the eye as easily as a knife through tofu. The terrible heat carried through its tip melted the giant’s brain, and its massive body toppled.
*Whoooosh—BOOM!*
A thick cloud of dust billowed upward.
Monsters caught beneath the dead giant screamed. Others lost sight of their target in the dust and hesitated.
They had no idea it was the last mistake they would ever make.
*Fwoosh!*
The cloud of dust split in two.
No—it evaporated.
A spear shot through the air like a ray of light, sweeping through the Liches commanding the monster army that had survived the enormous explosion.
*Rumble!*
Dozens of layered defensive spells were useless. So were Blink spells cast in the blink of an eye.
The unprecedented force behind the spearhead rendered them all meaningless.
Its power and speed were so astonishing that even *overwhelming* fell short.

The flash was fierce enough to blind anyone who faced it.

chapters.title: Chapter 1164
paragraphs: It was a pillar of light, vast and dazzling.
*Flash!*
A brilliance that seized everyone’s attention in an instant.
Morgoth knew better than anyone what had descended from the distant sky. He simply couldn’t understand how it had become reality.
“How?”
Someone answered the question that slipped from his lips.
“Why are you so surprised?”
Jin Taekyung.
It was him.
Despite the exhaustion in his voice, a faint smile—one that hadn’t been there before—rested on his lips.
“Just accept it. The weather’s nice. Don’t overthink it.”
“...What?”
Morgoth instinctively looked up, following Jin Taekyung’s pointing finger. Only then did he realize what he’d overlooked.
It had split apart.

The dark clouds had blocked every trace of clear sky and bright sunlight. His magical power had cut everything off from the world as it was. But the Black Dragon’s vast territory, once almost another Demon Realm, had begun to lose its hold.
The rift had opened because of Morgoth’s own greed—and the sacrifice of someone willing to face even Erasure.
“I told you. He wasn’t some trophy.”
At Jin Taekyung’s low voice, Morgoth thought of the precious trophy he had just moved to his subspace.
No. The Skeleton King.
“Yes. Perhaps he wasn’t.”
Resolve had led to sacrifice, and sacrifice had brought about this upheaval. The tremendous explosion of power the Skeleton King had unleashed by throwing away his life had made all this possible.
That was the chief reason the Magic of an utterly insignificant human had dared encroach on the great Black Dragon’s domain.
But...
“What can a force that small possibly change?”
His voice steady, Morgoth looked toward the distant horizon. More precisely, toward the group coming into view beyond the fading flash.
*BOOM!*
Before the light had vanished, a thunderous boom shook heaven and earth.
The monster army charged at the humans who had suddenly appeared to block its retreat. Over the monsters’ heads poured an endless rain of fire, unleashed by humanity’s strongest War Mage.
“A Warp on this scale, and wide-area Magic. Quite impressive. A step above the human mage from a few days ago.”
Quite impressive.
That was all Morgoth had to say about Magic Johnson, but there wasn’t a trace of arrogance in his appraisal.

Dragons were mysterious creatures born for Magic—Magic itself, one might say—and Morgoth stood at the pinnacle of their kind. Before he had even reached adulthood, he had touched the limits of Magic. To him, the Magic of other races was little more than child’s play. That remained true even in this unfamiliar world called Earth.
Otherwise, Merlin—the Grand Mage who, after Siegfried Bassmann’s death, had been one of only two left alongside Magic Johnson—wouldn’t have chosen to blow himself up in the battle a few days ago.
“He caught on quickly. He saw me collecting his comrades’ bodies and chose death without hesitation.”
Morgoth had felt a little regret at losing such a rare trophy as a Grand Mage. Not anymore.
“I suppose I should thank you. I never expected you to give me such fine trophies.”
Greed he had held in check until now glinted in his obsidian eyes.
Of the thousands of humans closing in as they crushed the monster army, only two posed even the slightest threat to him.

But even Magic Johnson and Chuck Hagel were no more than trophies in Morgoth’s eyes. Jin Taekyung, already worn down by considerable fatigue, faced a wall of a thousand Dragon-tooth soldiers—each one practically a Named Monster in its own right.
The seven Guardians stood with them, reborn far more powerful than before.
“Nothing has changed. This battle is over.”
He was right.
Anyone would have thought so. The odds were overwhelmingly in Morgoth’s favor.
And yet...
If that was true, why was Jin Taekyung still smiling?
In Jin’s heat-shimmering eyes, Morgoth saw someone he barely recognized: himself, his face rigid despite the words he’d just spoken.
“What’s so funny?”
Unable to hold back, Morgoth demanded an answer. Jin Taekyung raised the spear he’d been leaning on like a staff.
“I just feel a little better.”
“...You feel better?”
“Yeah. I’ve been in situations like this plenty of times. Heard what you just said plenty of times, too.”
Jin Taekyung spat out the phlegm that had gathered in his mouth.
“You know, the usual crap. ‘I’m different from everyone else.’ ‘I never let my guard down.’ ‘I’ll kill you for sure.’ ‘It’s all over.’ And so on.”
All those times he’d hovered between life and death.
They were memories so awful Jin Taekyung never wanted to revisit them. But right now, remembering them felt different.
Why?
Simple.
“The weird thing is, not one of those bastards ever followed through on what they said.”
It was true. He’d fought every one of them, and he’d beaten every one of them.
Even with his arms and legs crushed, his insides churned to mush, and death at his heels, he had survived.
But perhaps the deepest reason he’d won so many hopeless battles wasn’t just his strange power, the System.
“Why was that? Some of them really could’ve killed me. So why did they waste time talking and doing pointless things? Why leave themselves open?”
He was afraid.
Always. At every moment.
In battle, and even in the quiet moments of everyday life.
He feared that someday a powerful enemy would kill him. It tormented him that he might have to get back on his feet at the cost of someone else’s life.
So whenever he faced an enemy, he hurled insults. He piled on every kind of abuse, then dragged up even the smallest scraps of anger and grief buried deep inside him to smother his fear.
He had to make himself stronger somehow.
People called him a hero, but he knew he was far too weak to carry that burden.
Looking back, though, he hadn’t been the only one afraid of the person across from him.
“Then, all of a sudden, I started feeling better.”
Jin Taekyung had finally realized something.
“The guys I beat were afraid of me, too.”
“All that crap they said came from fear. Just like yours does now.”
Jin Taekyung smiled faintly at Morgoth’s suddenly frozen face.
“What, did I hit a nerve?”
Morgoth didn’t answer.
No—he couldn’t. Everything Jin Taekyung had said was true. His pride and insight were too great for him to deny it.
“...Fear.”
He’d forgotten it. Or rather, he’d tried to forget the one time he had ever felt that pathetic emotion.
But at last, Morgoth had no choice but to admit that what he felt toward Jin Taekyung was more than caution.
“Yes. I see. I was a little afraid of you, too.”
The strength of their fear might differ, but its nature was the same.
Muttering in a low voice, Morgoth looked at the tiny human who had dared to make him feel afraid.
“But I swear one thing to you.”
*Vwooom.*
The wind stopped. The air around them shuddered.
“I will be different from anyone you’ve ever faced.”
At that moment—
*Fwoosh!*
Darkness erupted around Morgoth, engulfed his body, and swelled. It rose as high as the spire that now lay in ruins and spread as wide as a fortress wall.
Jin Taekyung instinctively understood what the phenomenon before him meant.
*Polymorph.*
Would the world look like this if the sun vanished without a trace?
The Black Dragon finally shed his human skin. Darkness surrounded him, blackening the sky overhead and the battlefield for hundreds of meters around him.
As if announcing the end of the world.
But Jin Taekyung’s gaze didn’t waver. Not even as the darkness, its work done, slowly dissipated and a thousand Dragon-tooth soldiers charged toward him at their master’s command.
*It’s coming. It has to.*
He knew that just as darkness existed wherever there was light, a new light awaited beyond this darkness.
And his faith was rewarded.
Just as Jin Taekyung had once answered the voice of someone crying out for salvation.
*Flash!*
In an instant, the world lit up.
The horizon, sinking into darkness like an extinguished campfire, and the land, being swallowed by an even deeper gloom, were bathed in light.
Dozens, then hundreds of pillars of it.
The hearts of those who had crossed thousands—tens of thousands—of kilometers, again and again, to answer the call.
“...What is this?”
Countless Warp Magic Formations set the horizon ablaze. At Morgoth’s groan, rumbling like thunder from high in the distant sky, Jin Taekyung spoke.
“I’ll swear one thing, too.”
His low voice carried on the wind. He stepped forward and leveled his spear at the enemies bearing down on him.
“You’ll end up just like them.”
*Fwoosh—slice!*
As fierce flames rose like dawn and lit the battlefield, a mighty roar raced along the horizon and shook the field of battle.
