“Then, all of a sudden, I started feeling better.”
Jin Taekyung had finally realized something.
“The guys I beat were afraid of me, too.”
“All that crap they said came from fear.
Just like yours does now.”
Jin Taekyung smiled faintly at Morgoth’s suddenly frozen face.
“What, did I hit a nerve?”
Morgoth didn’t answer.
No—he couldn’t.
Everything Jin Taekyung had said was true.
His pride and insight were too great for him to deny it.
“...Fear.”
He’d forgotten it.
Or rather, he’d tried to forget the one time he had ever felt that pathetic emotion.
But at last, Morgoth had no choice but to admit that what he felt toward Jin Taekyung was more than caution.
“Yes.
I see.
I was a little afraid of you, too.”
The strength of their fear might differ, but its nature was the same.
Muttering in a low voice, Morgoth looked at the tiny human who had dared to make him feel afraid.
“But I swear one thing to you.”
*Vwooom.*
The wind stopped.
The air around them shuddered.
“I will be different from anyone you’ve ever faced.”
At that moment—
*Fwoosh!*
Darkness erupted around Morgoth, engulfed his body, and swelled.
It rose as high as the spire that now lay in ruins and spread as wide as a fortress wall.
Jin Taekyung instinctively understood what the phenomenon before him meant.
*Polymorph.*
Would the world look like this if the sun vanished without a trace?
The Black Dragon finally shed his human skin.
Darkness surrounded him, blackening the sky overhead and the battlefield for hundreds of meters around him.
As if announcing the end of the world.
But Jin Taekyung’s gaze didn’t waver.
Not even as the darkness, its work done, slowly dissipated and a thousand Dragon-tooth soldiers charged toward him at their master’s command.
*It’s coming.
It has to.*
He knew that just as darkness existed wherever there was light, a new light awaited beyond this darkness.
And his faith was rewarded.
Just as Jin Taekyung had once answered the voice of someone crying out for salvation.
*Flash!*
In an instant, the world lit up.
The horizon, sinking into darkness like an extinguished campfire, and the land, being swallowed by an even deeper gloom, were bathed in light.
Dozens, then hundreds of pillars of it.
The hearts of those who had crossed thousands—tens of thousands—of kilometers, again and again, to answer the call.
“...What is this?”
Countless Warp Magic Formations set the horizon ablaze.
At Morgoth’s groan, rumbling like thunder from high in the distant sky, Jin Taekyung spoke.
“I’ll swear one thing, too.”
His low voice carried on the wind.
He stepped forward and leveled his spear at the enemies bearing down on him.
“You’ll end up just like them.”
*Fwoosh—slice!*
As fierce flames rose like dawn and lit the battlefield, a mighty roar raced along the horizon and shook the field of battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 1165
paragraphs: *Rrrrrumble!*
If light could turn to liquid and overflow, would it look like this?
The ground shook as if an earthquake had struck. Watching waves of aura wash across the horizon and surge toward him, Morgoth knew instinctively:
If he didn’t act now, he might never get another chance to unleash everything he had.
“Answer my call.”
His low voice reverberated far and deep.
Language had power.
And the ancient Dragon’s words, imbued with immense magical power, reached a realm no other race had ever entered.
*Craaaack!*
The empty air split open.
At the same time, countless eyes gleamed ominously from within the dark rift in space.
“Gwoooar!”
Shadows large and small plummeted to the ground with roars full of killing intent.
With a single Warp spell, Morgoth had gathered his remaining forces from the cities they occupied across the region. He gave the order in a cold voice.
“Kill them all.”
That one command was the signal.
Monsters charged at humans, humans charged at monsters, and soon light and darkness blurred together.
*Clang-clang-clang!*
*Thwack! Splatter!*
The shriek of steel and the sickening sound of torn flesh swallowed the battle cries. Blood mist hung thick across the battlefield, and the Black Dragon watched it all without a flicker in his eyes.
His shock had lasted only an instant.
Morgoth had already regained his composure. His mind was colder than ever.
Even if his elite monster legion, the force that had guarded his stronghold, had suffered heavy losses, he still had the reinforcements he’d just summoned. That alone was enough.
No—even if every one of those monsters were wiped out, it wouldn’t matter.
The fate of the world hung on this battle. Its outcome would be decided not by mere numbers, but by whether one human lived or died.
*Jin Taekyung.*
There he was.
A blue-black flame slowly cutting through the thousand Dragon-tooth soldiers surrounding him like a dense forest.
At the same time, the short vow that small, insignificant human had spoken earlier echoed in Morgoth’s ears—and chilled a corner of his heart.
*Me? Morgoth? Becoming just like them?*
The Black Dragon bared his gleaming teeth and let out a low growl.
Wrong. He was nothing like anyone else.
With the Demon King Asmodeus gone, Morgoth alone was the true ruler destined to reign over every world—and that was exactly what he would become.
“Fire Lance.”
*Fwoosh—KABOOM!*
A dozen or so spears of flame appeared out of nowhere, about to rain down on Jin Taekyung.
“Ice Blaster!”
A desperate shout rang out from somewhere. A massive spike of ice tore through space and intercepted the flames.
*KABOOM!*
Space shook.
The deflected flames struck the empty ground. Steam billowed up, thick enough to obscure everything within a hundred-meter radius.
But the Black Dragon’s gleaming eyes saw clearly through it all.
A group of people covered head to toe in blood and dust, their eyes still blazing.
“Clear a...!”
The towering Grand Mage caught his breath, then roared.
“Clear a path!”
*Whoosh! Whoooooosh!*
With a battle cry that seemed to pierce the sky, the thousands-strong suicide squad—the first to reach this dreadful battlefield—charged toward the Dragon-tooth soldiers.
No.
They charged toward their Alliance Leader, their one and only hope.
It was a battle no one could control.
*BOOM!*
*Clang! Krrrunch!*
Flashes and explosions burst and mingled without pause.
Blood sprayed like fountains. Severed arms and legs rolled limply across the ground.
And through the chaos, a voice I’d been waiting for reached my ears.
“Wind Cutter!”
Magic Johnson. There he was.
At the same time, the blades of wind that rushed in passed close by the two Dragon-tooth soldiers charging at my flank.
*Shwaa!*
Two heads floated into the air.

If he’d aimed anywhere but their necks, even the Grand Mage’s Magic wouldn’t have been enough to kill them in one blow. But Magic Johnson had fought them before, in the Middle East. He knew their weakness exactly.
He also knew this wasn’t the time for a long, friendly greeting.
“Fuck.”
To the man who’d greeted me with a single syllable, I sent a dagger I’d just summoned from my Inventory.
More precisely, I threw it at the Dragon-tooth soldier lunging over his shoulder.
*Thwack!*
A dagger thrown with all a normal Murim martial artist’s strength would rightly be called a hidden weapon. But my Strength had long since surpassed that of most large monsters.
The dagger flashed forward and shattered the helmet made of some unknown metal—and the head beneath it. Drenched in the enemy’s brain matter, Magic Johnson muttered another curse.
“This is hell.”
“Sorry, but it’s too late to go back.”
“Everyone here knows that. We knew, and we came anyway.”
That was true.
They’d known their lives would be in danger, yet they’d answered my call willingly.
There were only twenty S-rank Hunters left in the entire world—or rather, now only a dozen or so—and they’d chosen only the very best before racing here from all over the globe.
Across continents and oceans.
But the tide of this Great War, with everything humanity had at stake, was still as dark and damp as the clouds overhead.
“Damn it, what the hell? There are this many of those awful things?”
Anyone who’d ever faced a Dragon-tooth soldier would react the same way.
They had more magical power than even the strongest Death Knights, which ranked at the top of A-rank. Their bodies were horribly tough, and they were stubbornly hard to kill.
Calling each one as formidable as a Named Monster would be no exaggeration.
But even Magic Johnson, who knew all this well, didn’t know one thing yet.
The Dragon-tooth soldiers weren’t the only obstacle we had to overcome to reach Morgoth.
*Shiiiiing!*
Something shot toward us like a beam of light.
With no time to catch my breath, I angled my spear blade and caught it on the flat.
*Clang!*
I’d poured plenty of internal energy into the spear, but its shaft still trembled.
Magic Johnson let out a low groan at the familiar face beyond it.
“Faye Chen?”
His mouth fell open. His eyes wavered.

He’d known that old comrade for decades, since the beginning of the Great Cataclysm. Seeing her shook Magic Johnson more than anything had yet. And when the number of familiar faces reached seven, his whole body trembled.
“What is this?”
“Guardians.”
“What?”
“That’s what Morgoth calls them. His Guardians. They protect him.”
Magic Johnson clenched his teeth as he understood what I meant.
Even I, who knew nothing about Magic, could clearly sense the magical power controlling them. The Grand Mage would have felt it all the more.
“...Guardians.”
Bitterness, anger, grief.
His voice carried them all. Then it gradually quieted, leaving only one.
Anger.
And Magic Johnson wasn’t the only one feeling it.
“Near the end of the Great Cataclysm, we talked about it when we were all together.”
*Boom!*
A fist shot forward like a cannonball, followed by a roar.
Chuck Hagel crushed the Dragon-tooth soldiers blocking his path one by one as he went on.
“If we survived this goddamn war, we’d live happier than anyone else in the world until the day we died.”
The fists he kept throwing carried more than the mysterious power called aura.
They carried memories.
The memories of those days, so painful they could have killed him, yet filled with hope that things would soon get better, poured forth with his aura.
“Then why?!”
*Krrrunch!*
Shattered weapons flew in every direction, along with pieces of the Dragon-tooth soldiers’ armor and bodies.
And the tears of an old soldier who had lost his longtime friends.
“Why are they like this now?!”
His roar held all his grief and anger.
Why had it come to this?
Why couldn’t they keep even that simple promise to live happily for a long time? Why did they have to suffer this humiliation even after death?
But no voice answered his questions.
The only answer was the Black Dragon’s Magic once again filling the sky, and the footsteps of his old comrades as they advanced.
*Fwoosh, crackle!*
*Shiiiiing!*
Giga Lightning.
Dozens of bolts plunged down like divine punishment. The seven Guardians and countless Dragon-tooth soldiers charged forward, pitch-black magical power streaming behind them like cloaks.
They came with a force that seemed impossible to stop.
But they didn’t break through.
Because I wasn’t alone anymore.
“Stone Wall!”
A single spell rang through the roar of battle.
Dozens of voices joined in it.
Magic Johnson stood at their head. Behind him were the world’s greatest mages, following humanity’s only Grand Mage.
*KABOOM!*
The sky darkened, then flashed.
A ceiling of rock suddenly appeared over our allies’ heads. When it met the lightning, a tremendous explosion shook the battlefield.
No—the two spells canceled each other out.
Several mages, unable to withstand the backlash, coughed up blood and fell to their knees. The enraged Black Dragon’s roar thundered across the battlefield.
“How dare you!”
*Rrrrrumble!*
As immense magical power began shaking space again, I shot straight forward, leaving the falling rocks behind me.
Just as I always had.
But one thing was different.
This time, people were following me.
*Whoooooosh!*
Another group of familiar faces finally broke through the chaotic battlefield.
The brown-haired foreigner at the front tipped his head toward me.
“Too late?”
“Not at all.”
“Good. Though I wouldn’t have apologized if I were.”
That irritating way of speaking was exactly as I remembered it.
Prince Felix had joined us with four S-rank Hunters. He added, “Go. Now. We’ll handle things here.”
I didn’t answer.
I held back the heat rising deep in my chest and pushed forward with all my might.
Behind me, seven S-rank Hunters clashed with their old comrades.
*Slice!*
I cut one down, then another.
*Krrrunch!*
Kept going. Didn’t stop.
And then—
*Crack!*
Toward the monster who was the beginning and end of it all.
*BOOM!*
I shot forward like a streak of flame.
“Morgoth!”
In the Black Dragon’s vast, gleaming eyes, a human leaping upward, stomping on thin air, was reflected.

chapters.title: Chapter 1166
paragraphs: *Fwoooosh.*
For an instant, time slowed.
The sounds around him faded into the distance, and his heartbeat thundered in his ears.
At the same time, instinct and reason whispered in unison.
*Now.*
His senses sharpened until every hair on his body stood on end. Jin Taekyung shot upward on the explosive force of Flamefire Path and brought his spear down with all his strength.
Toward the Black Dragon’s eye—larger than Jin’s entire body, and blacker than anything else.
*Fwoosh—KABOOM!*
A line of fire split the air.
No—the countless seams hidden within it.
*Shhhhk.*
A chillingly low, faint whistle.
That was all.
Nothing else could be seen or heard.
Even if someone else had been standing right there, watching it all unfold, they would never have understood what had happened.
But the two beings who had finally come face-to-face knew.
That single strike had cut through dozens of layers of the highest-grade defensive magic at once.
*I cut it.*
A shiver ran up Jin Taekyung’s spine.
It worked.
As his insight deepened and his martial prowess grew, he had begun to sense the flow of qi more and more clearly. Now he could sense it in the monster before him, too.
But the spearhead that had torn through the defensive magic never reached its target.
*Rrrumble—!*
An immense force suddenly fell on him from above.
And the force humanity called gravity was faster and heavier than Jin Taekyung had expected.
*Whoooosh—BAM!*
A cloud of dust rose in the wake of his body as it slammed down at tremendous speed.
Just as Jin Taekyung had cut through the defensive magic with a single attack, Morgoth had sent him crashing to the ground with overwhelming gravity. The Black Dragon muttered in a low voice.
“Did you think I wouldn’t anticipate even this?”
The words slipping between the Black Dragon’s teeth were more than mere sound.
“Wind Cutter.”
The magic within the Dragon’s words stirred. Countless blades of wind formed, then tore through the cloud of dust.
*BOOM!*
The thick dust cloud burst apart. Jin Taekyung raced over ground sliced through like tofu, dodging as Morgoth unleashed one spell after another.
Morgoth’s voice continued, almost as if he were talking to himself.
“Thank you. Thanks to you, I’ve finally realized something important.”
Until now, fear had seemed to a great being like Morgoth nothing more than a weak emotion.
So he had tried to forget it.
He simply hadn’t been able to.
But today, watching one human, he had glimpsed a great truth he had been refusing to face.
“If you fully acknowledge and accept the fear lurking in your heart, you can no longer call it fear.”
Yes.
Morgoth believed that was why Jin Taekyung—and humans—could be strong.
Their lives were absurdly short, their bodies fragile.
Humans were undeniably weak. They had neither the long lives of elves, nor the dwarves’ strength, nor monsters’ ability to reproduce quickly.
But because they knew their own weakness and fear, they spent their lives struggling to grow stronger, each in their own way.
Like the person fighting his way through a curtain of magic that now surrounded him on all sides, closing in without a gap, relying on nothing but a single spear.
“And so, I too will grow stronger.”
Morgoth dropped the barest courtesy he had maintained for the sake of his own dignity, not his opponent’s. He let go of the last sliver of arrogance that remained. Then he added quietly:
“Because I’m... afraid of you, you bastard.”
At that moment—
*CRACK—KABOOM!*
The ground caved in within a radius of a hundred meters around Jin Taekyung. Countless thorny vines burst through the cracks and surged toward him.
*Shwaaa!*
A sharp whistle rang out from every direction.
This was no ordinary binding spell, nor were these common thorny vines.
Their stems were as thick as the trunks of mature trees, covered from end to end in enormous thorns.
They had drunk their fill of the Black Dragon’s magical power instead of sunlight. Each one was strong enough to crush a human body in an instant, and Jin Taekyung could feel the power within them.
He also knew there was only one way to escape this tenacious magical prison closing in from every direction.
*Grit.*
He steadied his breathing. Clenched his teeth.

He planted a step with the weight of a thousand geun and used that foot as his pivot, gathering the internal energy he had left—not even half of what he’d started with—and pouring it into the tip of White Flame.
Then—
He swung.
A storm that swept everything away, and hellfire capable of burning anything.
*Whoooooosh!*
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
In the midst of a life-or-death struggle, the first form of the Blazing Flame Divine Spear, at last reaching the edge of its realm, flowed along the spearhead.
The fiery storm spread beyond a single line into a vast circle, hungrily devouring everything in its path.
The ice and lightning that had ceaselessly blanketed the sky and rained down.
The thorny vines that surged from every direction, seeming to swim through the ground.
*KABOOOOOM!*
White ash and embers that had not yet gone out drifted like snowflakes, brushing past Jin Taekyung as he stood alone and upright in the heat haze rising from the ground.
At the same time, Morgoth instinctively knew.
Now that Jin Taekyung had poured out all the strength he had left at once, this was the moment he had been waiting for.
It was why he had waged a relentless war of attrition, using tens of thousands of monsters—and even the thousand Dragon-tooth soldiers he had spent so long creating—as bait.
“Dark Vine.”
*CRRACK!*
Black thorny vines erupted again and surged toward Jin Taekyung.
And that wasn’t all.
*Rrrrumble!*
“Gravity.”
A force far beyond the bounds of ordinary gravity magic shook the sky. Magic spells of devastating power filled the gaps, each one as powerful as the dazzling flashes they produced.
All in one direction, for one purpose.
And this time, nothing unexpected happened.
*BOOM! Shrrrk!*
His knees buckled first under a weight of dozens of metric tons. Thick thorny vines slithered over him like living snakes and bound his whole body.
At the same time, dozens of spells converged in the air, shining down on one human like a small sun.
*Jin Taekyung.*
As Morgoth watched him, bound like a criminal and waiting for death to come, a thought suddenly crossed his mind.
If he hadn’t been a Dragon.
Or if Jin Taekyung had possessed a Dragon Heart, brimming with power almost without limit like his own, perhaps Jin Taekyung would be the one standing there now instead of him.
But...
*At least today, I was stronger.*
It was the difference in what they had been born with.
The size of the vessel that could contain their power, the total amount of strength they possessed—those were different.
Morgoth and Jin Taekyung.
Jin Taekyung and Morgoth.
The two beings were different in every way, and each had fought the other with everything they had. But Morgoth’s vessel of power was deeper and larger than Jin Taekyung’s.
That was all.
That was the sole reason this battle—and, beyond it, the fate of the world—had been decided.
*Meeting you was the greatest amusement I have ever experienced.*
With the highest praise he could offer, the Black Dragon opened his enormous jaws.
*Vwooom.*
The Dragon’s heart, deep within his body, shuddered.
No matter how much he emptied and poured out, pure magical power continued to fill him without end. Its chillingly low rumble swirled between the Dragon’s teeth, dark as a cave.
Dragon Breath.
A supreme power granted only to dragonkin.
Because he feared harming the Dragon-tooth soldiers, and because he had so little time to release it, its range and destructive power fell far short of their usual level.
But it was more than enough.
His only purpose was to erase a single human from this world without leaving a trace.
*Jin Taekyung. The weakest of humans, and yet a hero more resilient than anyone.*
*Gooooong.*
His chest suddenly swelled.
At the same time, the immense magical power flowing from the Dragon Heart—the purest, deepest darkness—finally became a single flash and shot forward.
Carrying heartfelt respect, and a murderous intent heavier still.
*This is the end.*
At that moment—
*KABOOOOOM!*
A beam of darkness, black enough to swallow the sun, tore through space like a bolt of lightning.
The world stopped.
Or at least, that was how it seemed to Jin Taekyung.
But his eyes, dimmer than usual, weren’t fixed on the countless spells coloring the air, or the Dragon’s breath, which held more power than all of them combined.
*So this is what it was.*
Jin Taekyung gazed clearly—not with his eyes, but with his mind.
At himself, thoroughly bound and forced to his knees.
At the enormous Black Dragon looking down on him with haughty disdain.
And at this world, and the secrets it had hidden.
It was a sensation that had come to him after another life-or-death struggle, one he had already experienced once in the not-so-distant past.
“People often fail to believe the truth, even when it’s right in front of them, and pass it by. It’s truly a pity.”
The voice echoed from his memory, belonging to the old man who had served as his Helper in the Tutorial, the Martial God without equal in all history—or the savior of humanity.
“You saw what cannot be seen, and avoided what cannot be avoided. So why can’t you believe what you did yourself?”
In another space, one that existed in neither dream nor reality, the Absolute One had asked him that question.
Back then, Jin Taekyung hadn’t answered.
No—he couldn’t.
He had been caught in a sensation that ruled his body and flesh.
Just like now.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
He heard it, but didn’t hear it.

**System** Martial arts are built through endless training and pain, and perfected in battles fought on the brink between life and death. Congratulations. The **Fire Dragon Divine Spear** has reached **Great Completion**. You have gained a tremendous amount of **EXP** and **Fame** as a reward. **Level Up!** Status effect **Trance** applied.
He saw it, but didn’t see it.
No-self.
True to the meaning of those two characters, Jin Taekyung forgot everything.
His memories up to that point. The many emotions lurking like thorns in his mind and heart.
Even Jin Taekyung himself.
And yet his pupils, now tinged with a deep blue-black light, were reading everything in the world.
*Mind’s Eye.*
Feeling something he hadn’t experienced since that day, Jin Taekyung lifted his spear as if entranced.

sentences.text: *Fwoooosh.*
For an instant, time slowed.
The sounds around him faded into the distance, and his heartbeat thundered in his ears.
At the same time, instinct and reason whispered in unison.
*Now.*
His senses sharpened until every hair on his body stood on end.
Jin Taekyung shot upward on the explosive force of Flamefire Path and brought his spear down with all his strength.
Toward the Black Dragon’s eye—larger than Jin’s entire body, and blacker than anything else.
*Fwoosh—KABOOM!*
A line of fire split the air.
No—the countless seams hidden within it.
*Shhhhk.*
A chillingly low, faint whistle.
That was all.
Nothing else could be seen or heard.
Even if someone else had been standing right there, watching it all unfold, they would never have understood what had happened.
But the two beings who had finally come face-to-face knew.
That single strike had cut through dozens of layers of the highest-grade defensive magic at once.
*I cut it.*
A shiver ran up Jin Taekyung’s spine.
It worked.
As his insight deepened and his martial prowess grew, he had begun to sense the flow of qi more and more clearly.
Now he could sense it in the monster before him, too.
But the spearhead that had torn through the defensive magic never reached its target.
*Rrrumble—!*
An immense force suddenly fell on him from above.
And the force humanity called gravity was faster and heavier than Jin Taekyung had expected.
*Whoooosh—BAM!*
A cloud of dust rose in the wake of his body as it slammed down at tremendous speed.
Just as Jin Taekyung had cut through the defensive magic with a single attack, Morgoth had sent him crashing to the ground with overwhelming gravity.
The Black Dragon muttered in a low voice.
“Did you think I wouldn’t anticipate even this?”
The words slipping between the Black Dragon’s teeth were more than mere sound.
“Wind Cutter.”
The magic within the Dragon’s words stirred.
Countless blades of wind formed, then tore through the cloud of dust.
*BOOM!*
The thick dust cloud burst apart.
Jin Taekyung raced over ground sliced through like tofu, dodging as Morgoth unleashed one spell after another.
Morgoth’s voice continued, almost as if he were talking to himself.
“Thank you.
Thanks to you, I’ve finally realized something important.”
Until now, fear had seemed to a great being like Morgoth nothing more than a weak emotion.
So he had tried to forget it.
He simply hadn’t been able to.
But today, watching one human, he had glimpsed a great truth he had been refusing to face.
“If you fully acknowledge and accept the fear lurking in your heart, you can no longer call it fear.”
Yes.
Morgoth believed that was why Jin Taekyung—and humans—could be strong.
Their lives were absurdly short, their bodies fragile.
Humans were undeniably weak.
They had neither the long lives of elves, nor the dwarves’ strength, nor monsters’ ability to reproduce quickly.
But because they knew their own weakness and fear, they spent their lives struggling to grow stronger, each in their own way.
Like the person fighting his way through a curtain of magic that now surrounded him on all sides, closing in without a gap, relying on nothing but a single spear.
“And so, I too will grow stronger.”
Morgoth dropped the barest courtesy he had maintained for the sake of his own dignity, not his opponent’s.
He let go of the last sliver of arrogance that remained.
Then he added quietly:
“Because I’m... afraid of you, you bastard.”
At that moment—
*CRACK—KABOOM!*
The ground caved in within a radius of a hundred meters around Jin Taekyung.
Countless thorny vines burst through the cracks and surged toward him.
*Shwaaa!*
A sharp whistle rang out from every direction.
This was no ordinary binding spell, nor were these common thorny vines.
Their stems were as thick as the trunks of mature trees, covered from end to end in enormous thorns.
They had drunk their fill of the Black Dragon’s magical power instead of sunlight.
Each one was strong enough to crush a human body in an instant, and Jin Taekyung could feel the power within them.
He also knew there was only one way to escape this tenacious magical prison closing in from every direction.
*Grit.*
He steadied his breathing.
Clenched his teeth.

He planted a step with the weight of a thousand geun and used that foot as his pivot, gathering the internal energy he had left—not even half of what he’d started with—and pouring it into the tip of White Flame.
Then—
He swung.
A storm that swept everything away, and hellfire capable of burning anything.
*Whoooooosh!*
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
In the midst of a life-or-death struggle, the first form of the Blazing Flame Divine Spear, at last reaching the edge of its realm, flowed along the spearhead.
The fiery storm spread beyond a single line into a vast circle, hungrily devouring everything in its path.
The ice and lightning that had ceaselessly blanketed the sky and rained down.
The thorny vines that surged from every direction, seeming to swim through the ground.
*KABOOOOOM!*
White ash and embers that had not yet gone out drifted like snowflakes, brushing past Jin Taekyung as he stood alone and upright in the heat haze rising from the ground.
At the same time, Morgoth instinctively knew.
Now that Jin Taekyung had poured out all the strength he had left at once, this was the moment he had been waiting for.
It was why he had waged a relentless war of attrition, using tens of thousands of monsters—and even the thousand Dragon-tooth soldiers he had spent so long creating—as bait.
“Dark Vine.”
*CRRACK!*
Black thorny vines erupted again and surged toward Jin Taekyung.
And that wasn’t all.
*Rrrrumble!*
“Gravity.”
A force far beyond the bounds of ordinary gravity magic shook the sky.
Magic spells of devastating power filled the gaps, each one as powerful as the dazzling flashes they produced.
All in one direction, for one purpose.
And this time, nothing unexpected happened.
*BOOM!
Shrrrk!*
His knees buckled first under a weight of dozens of metric tons.
Thick thorny vines slithered over him like living snakes and bound his whole body.
At the same time, dozens of spells converged in the air, shining down on one human like a small sun.

chapters.title: Chapter 1167
paragraphs: It wasn’t a simple thrust.
More precisely, it was something beyond attack or defense.
*Why should it be either?*
The question surfaced through Jin Taekyung’s hazy consciousness. He tilted the White Flame’s spearhead, wreathed in blue-black fire, upward.
Toward the Dragon’s Breath pouring down to blanket the sky.
Like a fool trying to stop a waterfall with an umbrella that had no fabric.
*Shh.*
A movement so simple it could hardly be called a form.
But what that tiny movement did next was beyond even an Ancient Dragon of unprecedented power and knowledge to predict.
*Rrrrrumble!*
Morgoth’s pupils widened.
As time resumed its rapid flow, his eyes flew wide before he even realized it.
*What is this...?!*
It was splitting apart.
A massive pillar of magical power, several meters in diameter, was splitting into dozens of streams the moment it touched the spearhead.
Even now, it continued to split.
*How is that possible?*
Morgoth had lived for thousands of years.
Sometimes as a human, an elf, or a dwarf. Sometimes wearing the hide of a monster. He had enjoyed the pleasures only the strong could afford and amassed countless experiences and knowledge.
That was precisely why Morgoth found this all the harder to understand.
How was such a thing possible?
How could a human smaller than his claw read the flow of energy within Dragon Breath?
But Morgoth’s questions were no more than empty echoes.
Even Jin Taekyung, lost in Trance, couldn’t properly answer them.
No—his consciousness had retreated somewhere so deep and distant that he didn’t even know what he was doing.
He simply followed what he saw.
*Rrrrrumble!*
Dark. Pitch-black in every direction.
A muffled roar filled his ears. The magical power diverted up, down, left, and right by the spearhead had unwittingly formed a rounded barrier around Jin Taekyung alone.
At least, that was how it looked from the outside.
*Fwoooosh.*
Why?
It was bright. Radiant.
Though darkness seemed to have swallowed the world, Jin Taekyung’s blue-black eyes saw countless lights glittering before him.
*Beautiful.*
He gazed at the strands of color filling his vision.
Some were red, others blue.
Some shone a dazzling white. Others held a darkness so pure he couldn’t fathom its depth.
The dozens of kinds of Magic that arrived a step behind the Breath were just like that.
Water, fire, ice, gusts of wind, lightning.
Each was powerful enough to kill thousands. All had been cast for one purpose: to erase a single person from this world. Jin Taekyung was grateful that person was him.
Had those spells been aimed at his allies instead, they would have died horribly.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
It all happened in an instant.
An old iron spear appeared in midair, and at the same moment, Jin Taekyung instinctively drew up the energy in his Middle Dantian.
*Fwoosh!*
It was swift and powerful.
More so than ever before since he had opened his Middle Dantian.
Wreathed in flame, the iron spear streaked through space like a bolt of lightning. It pierced the core of every spell in its path before finally losing all its power.
*KABOOOOOM!*
Sky and earth shook.
The spells, which had exploded before reaching their target, painted the sky in a dazzling display. Witnessing the unbelievable sight, the Black Dragon opened his enormous jaws wide.
He drew even more power from the vast magical force dormant within his Dragon Heart.
*Rrrrrumble!*
An immense pressure came through the spearhead.
And then, beneath the Dragon’s Breath pouring down harder and harder without pause, Jin Taekyung raised the knee buried deep in the ground.
*I have to get up.*
One thought filled his mind.
He had to go. There was no other choice.
And for now, he could forget everything else.
The pain of his bones slipping out of place.
The horrifying mass of magical power that threatened to swallow his body and spearhead at any moment.
The thorny vines constricting his entire body, and the immense gravity pressing down on both shoulders.
*Crack!*
His foot came forward, as unsteady as a child taking its first step.
But as the deep footprint showed, Jin Taekyung’s strength and Will carried more weight than ever before.
More than mere Magic could hold back.
*Crack!*
The thorny vines wrapped around him like chains tore apart, and the gravity that had weighed on him like a ten-thousand-geun boulder began to weaken.
*Crack.*
One step.
*Crack.*
Another.
Slowly, without hesitation, Jin Taekyung advanced.
Toward the enormous shadow in his dream-blurred vision, with the spearhead shining alone at the center of the pitch-black Breath to light his way like a torch.
And behind him stood a comrade willing to brave any danger for his sake.
“May the flames of hell consume our enemies—”
The Grand Mage’s cry rang through the din like a roar.
*Fwoooosh!*
The sky flushed red. A dozen or so fireballs emerged from between the storm clouds and took aim at the Black Dragon’s head.
“Hell Fire!”
*Rrrrrumble!*
The spell was complete. A fierce heat rushed in, scorching the sky.
But Morgoth wasn’t even slightly startled by this sudden attack.
No—when he saw that it was Magic, not a blade, coming for him, he sneered in anger.
He was no one but a Dragon.
Born of wonder, one of the species that ruled Magic—and once the Dragon Lord who had led all his kind from the highest place.
*Disappear.*
He didn’t even need to speak.
Morgoth possessed a powerful will and magical power greater still. His Magic existed in a realm beyond the reach of any other species, humans included.
*PAAAM!*
Anti Magic.
The Dragon’s magical power devoured the human’s mana.
Ash and embers scattered through the air. Far away, Magic Johnson—who had risked intervening while fighting the Guardians—coughed up blood and fell to his knees.
Mana Backlash.
The deadliest injury a mage could suffer.
Yet a gentle smile had formed on the Grand Mage’s blood-soaked lips.
Because the brief opening he had created gave someone else a chance, even if only for a moment, to escape the gravity.
“Go, Jin.”
His lips barely moved around the faint words.
*Fwoosh.*
Flames surged from the tip of Jin Taekyung’s foot as it touched down.
Heat strong enough to overcome the momentarily weakened gravity and carry him beyond the range of the Magic surrounding a radius of dozens of meters.
*KABOOM!*
Energy compressed, then exploded.
And then—
A charge.
*Whooooosh!*
Jin Taekyung raced forward, cutting through the Dragon Breath that stretched ahead in a single line.
The closer he came—and the more danger Morgoth sensed—the fiercer the Breath pouring toward the ground became. It didn’t matter.
If anything, the rougher it grew, the more clearly he could follow the flow of its power.
Leaving behind the countless roars and screams blanketing the battlefield.
Without a moment’s hesitation, he pressed on. Forward, and farther forward.
At last, as the Dragon’s enormous shadow loomed over him like a mountain, Jin Taekyung instinctively knew what he had to do.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear, Second Form.
Heavenly Strike.
*Rrrrrumble!*
No one there had ever seen anything like it.
The spearhead, wreathed in blue-black flame, rose through the colossal pillar of darkness, cleaving it in two.
Like a dragon soaring into the sky.
Becoming the fire dragon itself.
It all began and ended in an instant.
*Fwoooosh!*
The darkness scattered. The Dragon’s Breath had finally spent its power.
And a human had done it.
As Morgoth watched the unbelievable sight, he wondered where it had all gone wrong.
Had the arrogance and complacency deep in his heart grown into a snowball large enough to come crashing down on him like this?
Or—
Had the strength and will of a mortal with barely a hundred years to live truly surpassed his own?
*No. That can’t be.*
His name was Morgoth.
Master of the lofty Silver Mountains. Archduke of the Demon Realm.
The ancient Black Dragon muttered to himself, alone in the slowed world, and spread his enormous wings.
Then he dove toward the small figure shooting skyward once more, cutting through the heavens.
*PAAAM!*
Compressed air exploded.
From sky to ground.
From ground to sky.
Two shadows shot toward each other.
The Dragon’s claw, wrapped in pitch-black magical power, and the spearhead filled with blue-black fire tore through space.
As if they had lived for this moment alone.
Beyond the howling wind, Morgoth let out a fierce cry and put everything he had into a slash of his massive claw.
At that same instant, he realized something.
The foreleg he had just swung had already been cut by someone else.
And the wound remained even now, after he had returned to his true form.
*The Skeleton King.*
A shallow wound, but one that had never healed.

To some, he had been no more than a trophy. To someone else, he had been a friend. Perhaps it was Morgoth’s instinct that made him remember, at that very moment, the final trace of the Skeleton King’s stubborn resolve.
Perhaps.
Just perhaps.
The long game he had played for thousands of years might finally be coming to an end.
And ominous instincts were never wrong.
*Shhk.*
A low, sharp slicing sound.
The spearhead, carrying its wielder’s Will, cut into the last trace his friend had left behind.

*Whooooosh!*
Jin Taekyung raced forward, cutting through the Dragon Breath that stretched ahead in a single line.
The closer he came—and the more danger Morgoth sensed—the fiercer the Breath pouring toward the ground became.
It didn’t matter.
If anything, the rougher it grew, the more clearly he could follow the flow of its power.
Leaving behind the countless roars and screams blanketing the battlefield.
Without a moment’s hesitation, he pressed on.
Forward, and farther forward.
At last, as the Dragon’s enormous shadow loomed over him like a mountain, Jin Taekyung instinctively knew what he had to do.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear, Second Form.
Heavenly Strike.
*Rrrrrumble!*
No one there had ever seen anything like it.
The spearhead, wreathed in blue-black flame, rose through the colossal pillar of darkness, cleaving it in two.
Like a dragon soaring into the sky.
Becoming the fire dragon itself.
It all began and ended in an instant.
*Fwoooosh!*
The darkness scattered.
The Dragon’s Breath had finally spent its power.
And a human had done it.
As Morgoth watched the unbelievable sight, he wondered where it had all gone wrong.
Had the arrogance and complacency deep in his heart grown into a snowball large enough to come crashing down on him like this?
Or—
Had the strength and will of a mortal with barely a hundred years to live truly surpassed his own?
*No.
That can’t be.*
His name was Morgoth.
Master of the lofty Silver Mountains.
Archduke of the Demon Realm.
The ancient Black Dragon muttered to himself, alone in the slowed world, and spread his enormous wings.
Then he dove toward the small figure shooting skyward once more, cutting through the heavens.
*PAAAM!*
Compressed air exploded.
From sky to ground.
From ground to sky.
Two shadows shot toward each other.
The Dragon’s claw, wrapped in pitch-black magical power, and the spearhead filled with blue-black fire tore through space.
As if they had lived for this moment alone.
Beyond the howling wind, Morgoth let out a fierce cry and put everything he had into a slash of his massive claw.
At that same instant, he realized something.
The foreleg he had just swung had already been cut by someone else.
And the wound remained even now, after he had returned to his true form.
*The Skeleton King.*
A shallow wound, but one that had never healed.
To some, he had been no more than a trophy.
To someone else, he had been a friend.
Perhaps it was Morgoth’s instinct that made him remember, at that very moment, the final trace of the Skeleton King’s stubborn resolve.
Perhaps.
Just perhaps.
The long game he had played for thousands of years might finally be coming to an end.
And ominous instincts were never wrong.
*Shhk.*
A low, sharp slicing sound.
The spearhead, carrying its wielder’s Will, cut into the last trace his friend had left behind.

chapters.title: Chapter 1168
paragraphs: It connected.
And it cut.
That was all.
The whole thing began and ended in an instant. There was nothing more to explain.
Jin Taekyung had never harbored a trace of doubt. The hellfire spearhead he drove forward without hesitation could melt and cleave through anything.
Even a Dragon’s bone and hide.
*Shhk.*
A hair’s breadth.
That was all the difference.
Yet that sliver of distance, shorter than a dagger, made a difference as vast and deep as the distance between heaven and earth.
The enormous claw barely grazed his Fire Dragon Armor. But the spearhead rose in a perfect arc and drove straight into the tiny wound etched into the Dragon’s foreleg.
*Fwoooosh!*
Blood burst forth like a waterfall.
Strangely silver, the Dragon’s blood flooded Jin Taekyung’s vision. Its vicious acidity even began to melt his exposed skin and parts of his Fire Dragon Armor.
He didn’t care.
No—he had no reason to.
Compared to everything that had happened and everything still to come, this much pain was nothing.
*Grit.*
Jin Taekyung clenched his teeth against the faint pain.
Planting a foot on the Dragon’s foreleg beneath him like a stepping-stone, he drove his tightly clenched fist forward with all his strength.
*Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.*
*BAM!*
Compressed air exploded from the fist he drove forward like lightning.
The fierce heat in his knuckles swallowed the spray of blood, opening a new path beyond it.
*Whoooosh!*
He charged.
One man staking everything on a charge, a storm of hellfire that would melt and devour anything in its way.
*CRRRUNCH!*
A trail of flame cut forward like an icebreaker smashing through a glacier.
The spearhead, buried deep in the enemy’s flesh and bone, spewed lava as it climbed higher and higher.
Flames rose in the wake of Jin Taekyung’s arrowing form, so vivid and fierce that they drew the eyes of everyone still locked in battle.
Human and monster alike.
Not one of them was an exception.
Without realizing it, they lowered the blades in their hands or hid their sharp claws and fangs.
Every living thing that had survived this horrific battlefield sensed it instinctively.
That rising flame, devouring space itself, would decide all their fates.
If there were any exceptions, they were the two beings who had faced only each other from the start.
Leaving the vast battlefield and its countless watching eyes behind, the Ancient Dragon and the human raced toward their final moment, gazing at each other like figures in a myth.
*Jin Taekyung.*
*Morgoth.*
The names passed between them without a sound—not from their mouths, but through their eyes across the open air.
They heard without hearing.
And without speaking, they felt.
And he could feel the emotions in the enemy’s eyes as they drew closer like the wind, as though defying the slowing of time.
What Jin Taekyung saw now was a Dragon’s eyes filled with terrible pain and fear.
*Yeah. It hurts, doesn’t it?*
With a thought that would never reach Morgoth, Jin Taekyung put more strength into his charge.
He ran up the Dragon’s long, massive foreleg like a flight of stairs, toward the head towering above him like a skyscraper.
*Like it hurt the people you killed with your own hands. Or the ones who lost someone precious because of you.*
Jin Taekyung suddenly wished Morgoth’s pained roar—every emotion he felt, every ounce of his suffering—could reach them all.
Tens of millions had died.
Hundreds of millions had lost family, friends, and homes.
That was why Jin Taekyung couldn’t stop.
It was what fueled his will to keep moving forward.
*CRRRUNCH!*
Perhaps that was why his will surpassed the limits of his body.

Why the flame on his spearhead, weakening as the emptiness in his lower dantian grew, roared back to life. Why, even as the Dragon’s acidic blood melted away parts of his skin and muscle, he no longer felt the pain.
*Whooooom!*
The sky suddenly darkened. Gusts slammed in from both sides.
Jin Taekyung didn’t waver.
He simply swept the spearhead that had been cutting through the enemy’s body upward, toward the two wings bearing down on him with enough force to crush a mountain.
*Shhhh.*
The rolling flames rose at an angle.
One line, chillingly swift and savage.
In the arc of blue-black fire that suddenly appeared in the air were the Dragon’s two wings, which had ruled the vast sky and blanketed the earth for thousands of years.
*Shhk!*
—Kraaaaaa!
The Dragon’s body thrashed with a muffled scream. Jin Taekyung pressed down on it and dug in his toes.
*Fwoosh—BAM!*
Flamefire Path.
Propelled upward by an explosion worthy of its name, his figure appeared in Morgoth’s pitch-black eyes.
No—that wasn’t right.
He soared into the sky like a fire dragon that had finally reached the time of its ascension. His form wasn’t merely reflected in those eyes; it overflowed from them.
*Is this what it feels like when time stops?*
In that strange sensation, with every sound and movement around him gone, Morgoth watched Jin Taekyung.
He saw eyes sunk to unfathomable depths, their blue-black light unlike anything he had ever seen. He felt the countless fragments of emotion within them.
And, a step too late, he understood.
*Too late.*
Morgoth couldn’t tell whether reason or instinct had reached that conclusion. But one thing was certain.
In this world where everything had stopped, the spearhead slowly descending toward him was the only thing that moved. No ability he possessed could stop it or evade it.
That left him one path.
—Kraaaaaa!
His enormous jaws gaped open.
In the Ancient Dragon’s last, death-defying struggle, the immense magical power and countless teeth lurking within his maw flashed toward a single human.
And at that very moment—
*Rrrrk.*
Jin Taekyung gripped the spear shaft with all the strength he had left.
Muscles swelled throughout his body. Fire raced through hundreds of acupoints and spread to every limb and bone.
*Thump. Thump. Thump.*
His heart hammered furiously.

His lower dantian was so empty that the recovery he’d gained from leveling up might as well never have happened. His mind, pushed far beyond its limits, had been crying out with exhaustion for some time.
But he didn’t stop.
More precisely, he had no reason to.
*I can see it.*
In this new world painted with lines of every color, one trajectory shone brighter than all the rest.
Following the path he had read through the Mind’s Eye, Jin Taekyung poured all his strength and will into the spearhead.
*Fwoosh—*
As time began to move again, the flame on the spearhead wavered.
But it wasn’t a sign of danger. It was a change—and an evolution—that took place in an instant.
*Shhhh.*
The wavering flame gathered into one.
It came together and connected, no longer a flame but a single line, as though it had become the spearhead itself. Then, at last, it settled.
One step beyond fire’s innate savagery lay hellfire refined to the utmost degree.
It was a peak Jin Taekyung had reached through his own enlightenment. A third path no one had ever taught him.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
Third Form.
*Fwoooosh.*
Space twisted.
The spearhead, raised as though to cleave the sky, and the refined flame within it gave off a terrifying heat.
Like another sun prepared to bring forth a new sky.
*Open Heaven.*
A fierce shiver seized Jin Taekyung’s body and mind. With a roar that made no sound, he brought down the hellfire spearhead.
*KABOOOOOM!*
The blue-black sun opened a world drowned in darkness.
They heard it, but didn’t hear it.
They saw it, but didn’t see it.
Amid mountains of corpses and rivers of blood, countless living creatures watched an unbelievable sight unfold in the distance. In that moment, they all felt the same thing.
A shudder.
They shuddered.
A flash too bright to look at filled their vision. A muffled roar blocked their ears. Yet every survivor could feel it clearly.
This long and terrible battle had finally come to an end.
As the light slowly faded, what emerged beyond it proved them right.
*Fwoooosh.*
A fierce wind swept through, wrapping around the enormous body as it fell, silver blood spraying from it like a waterfall.
Yes. It was a fall.
And with it came the downfall of an Ancient Dragon who had lived for thousands of years.
What falls has wings. But his wings would never take flight again.
*KABOOOOOM!*
The earth shook. Dust billowed up and swept across the area like a desert sandstorm.
Yet tens of thousands of eyes that had witnessed it all remained fixed on the sky.
More precisely, on the one figure moving through the terrible stillness weighing down on the world.
*Step.*
He walked slowly through the air as though climbing down an invisible staircase.
Even from a distance, he looked utterly exhausted. But no one there dared entertain the thought, or feel anything of the sort.
With the sky—its clouds torn away without a trace—at his back, he descended toward the ground against the falling sun. His very presence inspired an overwhelming awe.
As if he were something beyond human.
Or a glimpse of someone the world would remember forever, as that person had once been.
The breathless murmur escaped someone’s lips. Watching Jin Taekyung with trembling eyes, the others remembered one important thing they had forgotten.
They had won.
They—
No. Humanity had won.
And the one who had led them was a new savior of humanity.
