chapters.title: Chapter 1186
paragraphs: Everything has a beginning.
Even a white-haired old man was once a baby. Even a pebble by the roadside didn’t always look the way it does now.
Everything in the world comes together according to a fixed order and changes with the passage of time.
Nothing is perfect from the start. Nothing lasts forever.
That is the law of nature, the order of the world as everyone knows it.
And yet, the group pushing through the pale mist was thinking the same thing.
Or rather, they were wondering whether everything they had always taken for granted might be little more than an illusion.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was one of them.
*Damn it.*
He swallowed the curse rising in his throat and looked around.
Mist coiled in every direction. Beyond it, black branches appeared and vanished in fleeting glimpses. Rugged mountains climbed without end.
Order? Laws?
Those ideas had long since been wiped from his mind.
The landscape looked as if it had been perfect in this form from the beginning and would remain unchanged ten thousand years from now. Jeok Cheongang licked his parched lips.
The sight was more chilling than a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords. Looking at it made his hundred-plus years of life, and everything he had learned in them, feel almost meaningless.
If there was any comfort, it was that he wasn’t the only one who felt that way.
“Damn Tianshan.”
The voice suddenly reached his ear. Jeok Cheongang silently agreed, then parted his lips.
“Don’t say that. The youngsters will lose heart if they hear you.”
There was only one person who would send him a Sound Transmission in a situation like this.
The Slaughter Saint’s reply came at once.
“That’s why I’m using Sound Transmission.”
“Don’t use that, either.”
“Why not?”
“It wastes internal energy.”
A dozen paces ahead, the Slaughter Saint turned to Jeok Cheongang with an incredulous look.
“Do I look like some Third Rate swordsman off the street? And if you’re so worried about wasting internal energy, why answer me instead of practicing what you preach?”
“This old man can afford it.”
“Why can you afford it?”
“My internal energy runs deep. Unlike some people’s.”
“...You can still crack jokes at a time like this.”
“I have to. At a time like this.”
This time, it was the Slaughter Saint’s turn to agree.
Jeok Cheongang’s subdued tone came through even in Sound Transmission, and the Slaughter Saint’s gaze grew troubled.
“Like I said earlier, this is no easy place. I thought I’d seen a fair bit of the world after traveling all across it, but... I’ve never heard of or seen anything like this.”
Unlike Jeok Cheongang, who had spent most of his life on Mount Jiuhua, the Slaughter Saint had lived as a wanderer—first as an assassin, then as a physician.
In his youth, he had traveled a thousand li to take someone’s life. In his old age, he had searched for herbs ten thousand li away to save one.

Even a young woodcutter who lived day to day cutting trees would have his own experiences and his own life. For someone who had made his mark at opposite ends of life and death, calling his experience “a fair bit” was an understatement born of extraordinary modesty.
Of course, to Jeok Cheongang, who shared the same reality, it sounded entirely sincere.
“I expected as much, but it seems even you don’t have an answer.”
“There’s no way forward, nothing we can do. We can’t even tell day from night. What can we possibly do?”
The Slaughter Saint was right.
The mist blocking their way wasn’t confined to the ground.
Dark clouds hung overhead.
At first, they had thought the enormous black mass was passing through. Instead, it had covered the sky.
It had swallowed the moon and stars that had faintly lit the way above them at first. It wouldn’t allow even a single ray of sunlight through.
As though it meant to frighten the rude intruders who had come without its permission.
“Do you think any of this is a coincidence?”
“A coincidence?”
Jeok Cheongang let out a hollow laugh before he knew it.
“The old me would certainly have thought so. Before I met a certain impudent brat who’s riding on his master’s back while the old man works himself to the bone at his age.”
Jeok Cheongang gazed at the face of the “impudent brat” resting on one of his shoulders.
His Disciple had appeared out of nowhere one day and turned the life of an old, sick man upside down.
Now he was changing not just one man’s life, but everyone’s world.
“There are no more coincidences for us. Everything that happens from here on is intended, inevitable. And maybe...”
*Maybe it was fate, decided from the very beginning.*
Jeok Cheongang quietly swallowed the words he had been about to add.
It wasn’t that he didn’t believe in fate.
If all of this was fate, it was far too cruel to Jin Taekyung. Worse, Jeok Cheongang was afraid of how this story might end.
“Maybe what?”
“No, nothing. Let’s leave it. What matters more is the situation we’re in.”
Jeok Cheongang’s words and behavior were plainly unnatural, but the Slaughter Saint didn’t press him.
He was a little disappointed, but everyone had worries of their own. And the Jeok Cheongang he had come to know was far more thoughtful and sensitive than people gave him credit for.
Especially where Jin Taekyung was concerned.
*Then again, I’m hardly in a position to judge him for that.*
The Slaughter Saint’s gaze shifted past Jeok Cheongang’s shoulder.
The younger members of the group were racing over the rugged terrain, breathing hard. Behind them, Great Sir and the Bow Saint brought up the rear, their faces calm.
His gaze rested on them for only a moment. Then he spoke as if nothing had happened.
This time, in his own voice rather than through Sound Transmission.
“We should take a short break.”
His voice carried through the mist, which had grown denser still.
The Slaughter Saint had made the right call.
The moment they stopped, Hyuk Mujin began retching. Instead of patting him on the back, Gung Gibang pulled out some jerky.
“...You traitor. Is that jerky really so good?”
Ju Hwaran eventually helped Hyuk Mujin stop retching. Gung Gibang answered his accusation without hesitation.
“Of course.”
“Seriously, this stuff is incredible. Is it because it came from sweat-blood horses? The flavor’s remarkably consistent.”
“Don’t glare at me. Just eat. You’ll need your strength. Or you could sit down and circulate your qi like that fellow.”
Hyuk Mujin glanced between Song Ilseom, who was already sitting cross-legged, and Gung Gibang, who was still tearing into his jerky. Then his expression hardened as he made up his mind.
“Give me a piece. I want to see what’s so good about it that you’re eating like a beggar who hasn’t had a meal in three days.”
When they had first met, there had been a considerable gap between them in both standing and martial prowess. But they had traveled together long enough to become all but friends.
Gung Gibang grinned, showing his yellow teeth.
“Excellent decision. Oh, Young Lady Ju, would you like some, too?”
“No, thank you. I think I’d better circulate my qi for a while.”
Replenishing one’s strength and refining one’s internal energy were both good choices.
Climbing mountains—especially rugged ones at this altitude—was exhausting in a way that running across flat ground wasn’t.

Besides, even they, whose martial arts were far less advanced than those of the masters traveling with them, could feel the heavy air hanging over all of Tianshan and the strange phenomena that defied explanation.
“Damn it. I can’t even remember the last time I felt warm sunlight.”
Hyuk Mujin answered Gung Gibang with his mouth stuffed full of jerky.
“We got some in the desert.”
“How was that warm sunlight? I was scared to go out during the day in case I burned to death. Though by the time we were halfway across, I did start to miss it.”
“Fair enough. That weather was a real pain in the ass.”
In truth, “a real pain in the ass” didn’t begin to cover it.
What kind of desert had no cacti or bugs, yet got alternating hailstorms and downpours for more than half a month?
But that was the world now.
And to survive in a changed world, they had to change, too.
“I’m dying here. How many peaks have we climbed already?”
“Five.”
“Already? That’s more than I thought.”
“Not when you consider how hard we’ve been running. And we don’t know how much farther we have to go.”
The Tianshan Mountains were wide.
No, “wide” didn’t do them justice. They were vast.
The range stretched for more than a thousand li and covered a full third of Xinjiang.
And that wasn’t all. It was a Sacred Land where only a select few of the old Demonic Cult’s members had been allowed to enter—and a Land of Ruin where outsiders were certain to die.
They still had no idea which of its hundreds of peaks held the Cult’s headquarters.
“Terrible.”
“Terrible.”
“At least nothing’s happened yet. That should mean we haven’t been spotted.”
“If the Captain heard you say that, he’d smack you one.”
“Why?”
“He hates that sort of talk. Says it’s bad luck. Then he starts on about ‘cli’ or ‘guli’ or something that sounds like copper. I never know what he means.”
“Honestly, I can never figure him out.”
“Tell me about it.”
The two muttered almost to themselves, then lay on their backs and stared blankly at the sky.
Or rather, at the dark clouds covering every inch of it.
“How long exactly have we been here?”
“More than a day, less than two.”
“Are you sure?”
“I’m sure.”
“Impressive, when we can’t even tell night from day.”
Hyuk Mujin answered firmly.
“Because the Captain still hasn’t woken up.”
“Oh, right. He’s supposed to wake up within two days at the latest.”
“Exactly. So it definitely hasn’t been two days yet.”
Gung Gibang studied him for a moment, then gave a quiet laugh.
“What?”
“It’s just... How do I put this? You really are something.”
“What do you mean?”
“Almost everything seems to revolve around Jin Taekyung.”
“I don’t know. It’s just so natural to me.”
“Don’t get me wrong. I’m not saying it’s strange, or that I don’t understand. I’m saying it because I know exactly how it feels.”
The smile on Gung Gibang’s lips faded.
“That’s what a martial family is. You may not share blood, but sometimes the bond runs deeper than blood.”
Gung Gibang fell into memories for a moment, and Hyuk Mujin went quiet.
It felt as though a wound long held closed had finally split open.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan. The Beggars’ Sect.
Their martial families, their other homes—and the names of two enormous stones weighing down their hearts.
What had happened to the people who had marched west with their banners held high?
If they were still alive, would they ever meet again?
They could trade silly remarks and force smiles, but reality was cold enough to make them shudder.
And it moved so quickly that they had no time to fight off the chill before it seeped into their bones.
*Shhhhhhhh.*
A sudden sense of wrongness.
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened. In them, the mist writhed as though it were alive.

paragraphs: A snake.
That was the first word that came to everyone’s mind when they saw the mist writhing toward them.
Gloomy and dark, it crept closer like a huge predator that had spotted its prey. Their legs had gone stiff as stone and would hardly lift from the ground.
Something beyond what they could see was stirring a primal fear in them.
And the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was one of the few people who could recognize the true nature of the power within that mist before anyone else—and understand it clearly.
*This is...!*
There was no doubt.
Demonic qi.
No—magical power, as it was now also called. That abyssal energy flowed through his five senses, binding his body and mind.
Terrifyingly fast. Insidiously.
Yet even as fear welled up inside him, Jeok Cheongang felt an intense pull he couldn’t explain.
It was a strange feeling. Like the warm embrace of a mother he could no longer remember. If he gave himself over to the mist, everything would be easier.
Surely a peaceful paradise awaited him in that hazy world, free of hardship and anguish—
*Crunch!*
Pain stung his tongue, and blood filled his mouth.
Jeok Cheongang had bitten down in the nick of time. His senses clear again, he spat out the blood and roared.
“Hah!”
His azure dragon’s roar, driven by mighty internal energy, shook the air in every direction.
He wasn’t the only one to let out a cry like a beast’s roar.
The Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint had reacted at the same instant. The two superhumans groaned as they watched the mist falter, if only briefly.
Dark arts.
An immensely powerful, sinister force unlike anything they had ever seen was consuming the space around them.
No—perhaps all of Tianshan.
But they faced an even greater problem.
“Ahhh...”
Their companions stared dreamily ahead, voices vacant. Their hands reached through empty air as their feet carried them slowly toward the mist.
Not one of them was spared. Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin were closest to it, but even Ju Hwaran and Song Ilseom, farther away, were moving toward it.
They looked like people who had lost their souls. Sensing the danger, the three veteran masters shot toward them without hesitation.
And just as they reached out, their hands moving like streaks of light—
*Whoosh!*
A sharp whistle cut through the air. Space warped.
The mist had curled into the razor-sharp claw of a giant beast. Jeok Cheongang saw the darkness steeped within it reflected in his reddish eyes.
“How dare you!”
*Fwoosh—BOOM!*
Flames burst from his Flame Divine Palm with his furious cry, shattering the claw of magical power and heating the air. The infernal blaze would not let it come an inch closer.
But he soon realized the brief attack had been deliberate.
*Shhhhhhh.*
Pale steam billowed up. Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened.
He couldn’t see them.
Gung Gibang’s threadbare collar had been within reach. Hyuk Mujin’s head had been right there, making Jeok Cheongang want to smack it on sight.
No.
*They’re gone.*
That was the only way to put it. He had seen their bodies disappear into the mist, as though erased from the world.
*What in the...*
Jeok Cheongang swallowed the groan rising in his throat and looked around. Then he realized something else.
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin weren’t the only ones who had vanished.
He let out the breath he had been holding.
When had it happened? Had it begun with that strange sense of déjà vu?
He didn’t know. The scenery before him looked unchanged, but everything else was different.
No one was there. No one.
Even the Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint, who had stood scarcely thirty feet away, were nowhere to be seen. He could sense neither their presence nor a trace of their qi.
*An illusion technique? Or a Mystic Gate Formation?*
Dark arts he had heard of in rumors, and others he had faced himself on the battlefields of the Great Faction War, flashed through his mind. None gave him an answer.
Even Jeok Cheongang, who had lived for more than a century and dominated an era, had never encountered dark arts like these.
*This is something else entirely.*
Even the great fiends of the previous generation, notorious under names like the Illusion Fiend and Guiguzi, had never managed anything like it.
More precisely, Jeok Cheongang’s formidable martial prowess had never allowed them to.
Even the strongest dark arts had their limits.

The Illusion Fiend, the Demonic Cult’s greatest master of illusion, had had both eyes gouged out. Guiguzi, who had slaughtered hundreds of orthodox Murim warriors with his intricate Mystic Gate Formation, had melted into a pool of blood.
Both at the hands of one man: the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
But...
*I’ve never seen or heard of a formation like this.*
Jeok Cheongang stretched his senses farther than ever before. The longer he searched, the more certain he became.
No matter how bizarre the dark arts, there should be a flow of energy and a core at its center. In this strange space, he could find neither.
Only the dark mist approaching with the uniquely sticky, unpleasant energy of demonic qi—and someone’s steady breathing against his back.
“Sleeping through all this. You’ve got it easy, you know.”
A faint smile touched his lips despite his grumbling. He glanced at the Disciple who would have protested bitterly if he were awake, then muttered as though making a promise to himself.
“Don’t worry. Whatever happens, I won’t let a single hair on you come to harm...”
His voice trailed off.
After a moment’s silence, he added with a sigh, “Just bear with it. Losing one hair won’t kill you.”
His Disciple offered no answer. Jeok Cheongang fixed his fiercely shining eyes on the dense mist.
“What are you waiting for? Crawl the hell out here!”
The beings beyond the pale veil answered his call.
*Grrrr.*
The mist rolled in waves. At last, countless eyes gleamed within it.
Jeok Cheongang drew a slow breath.
“Come in a whole pack, have you?”

Heat shimmered around him as Extreme Yang energy spread through his limbs and every part of his body. He raised both fists, wrapped in fierce flames, toward the monsters that did not belong in this world.
“Come.”
The long night had begun.
The mist was too thick to see an inch ahead. Countless shadows surged through it.
At the center of it all, flames burned ever more fiercely.
*Boom!*
One palm strike.
No more, no less. The motion was devastating in its efficiency. In its wake lay only heat enough to melt rock—and death.
*Thud!*
A huge body that could not be called human sank to its knees.
The three red eyes in its single head were still fixed on their prey, but the chest melted away without a trace proved which of them had been the hunter.
*Grrk.*
Light drained swiftly from its eyes. Before the monster had breathed its last, the hunter had already turned to set other living things ablaze.
*Crunch!*
He smashed, burst, and crushed without pause.
Hands, feet, legs, knees, elbows—sometimes even his forehead. Every part of him was a weapon, and every blow meant something’s death.
Neither the five-foot-tall monsters nor the three-headed, six-armed ones could break through the blazing wall of fire.
Claws sharper than scythes and rusty blades in place of arms struck relentlessly at his limbs. Jeok Cheongang’s body and mind never faltered.
It was like the day Mount Jiuhua had been engulfed in flames, decades ago.
No. He was stronger and colder now than he had been then—beyond comparison.

The thousand members of the Demonic Cult who had drawn the old monster known as the Fire King out of Mount Jiuhua had at least looked human. These were cursed beings that should never have appeared in the human world.
*Kyarruk!*
*Kraaaaah!*
They carried a madness and killing intent unlike anything he had felt before. They had clearly lost their reason long ago and moved only at their master’s command. Still, they charged without cease—
*RrrrCRUNCH!*
—and died without respite.
*Splaaat!*
Blood sprayed high into the air. With a single sweep of his hand, as if brushing away insects, Jeok Cheongang sent hundreds of shreds of flesh flying in every direction.
“Is that all?”
In the sudden gap left by death, he swept his gaze around him and muttered, “Did you think that would be enough to bring this old man down?”
The words of his Master came to mind. Time had blurred even the man’s face.
*Cheongang, the world is vast, and there are many strong people.*
The world beyond Mount Jiuhua had been as vast as his Master had said.
The Heavenly Demon, who had swallowed half the world, and the great fiends who followed him were strong. So were the Daoists and the damned monks who held the Central Plains.
But that wasn’t all his Master had said.
*But you could become one of the strongest among them.*
As always, his Master had been right.
And the young life he carried on his back made him stronger still.
“If you won’t come to me, I’ll come to you.”
*Hiss.*
Heat rose where he planted his foot.
Had even these mindless monsters retained their instincts? Faced with the overwhelming difference in strength, they had halted their attack.
Jeok Cheongang started toward them.
Or rather, he meant to.
Until a voice he could never forget pierced his ear.

Jeok Cheongang froze.
The fierce light in his eyes faded like a lamp caught by the wind. Reflected in them was the face of someone who could not be here—and should not be.

sentences.text: A snake.
That was the first word that came to everyone’s mind when they saw the mist writhing toward them.
Gloomy and dark, it crept closer like a huge predator that had spotted its prey.
Their legs had gone stiff as stone and would hardly lift from the ground.
Something beyond what they could see was stirring a primal fear in them.
And the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was one of the few people who could recognize the true nature of the power within that mist before anyone else—and understand it clearly.
*This is...!*
There was no doubt.
Demonic qi.
No—magical power, as it was now also called.
That abyssal energy flowed through his five senses, binding his body and mind.
Terrifyingly fast.
Insidiously.
Yet even as fear welled up inside him, Jeok Cheongang felt an intense pull he couldn’t explain.
It was a strange feeling.
Like the warm embrace of a mother he could no longer remember.
If he gave himself over to the mist, everything would be easier.
Surely a peaceful paradise awaited him in that hazy world, free of hardship and anguish—
*Crunch!*
Pain stung his tongue, and blood filled his mouth.
Jeok Cheongang had bitten down in the nick of time.
His senses clear again, he spat out the blood and roared.
“Hah!”
His azure dragon’s roar, driven by mighty internal energy, shook the air in every direction.
He wasn’t the only one to let out a cry like a beast’s roar.
The Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint had reacted at the same instant.
The two superhumans groaned as they watched the mist falter, if only briefly.
Dark arts.
An immensely powerful, sinister force unlike anything they had ever seen was consuming the space around them.
No—perhaps all of Tianshan.
But they faced an even greater problem.
“Ahhh...”
Their companions stared dreamily ahead, voices vacant.
Their hands reached through empty air as their feet carried them slowly toward the mist.
Not one of them was spared.
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin were closest to it, but even Ju Hwaran and Song Ilseom, farther away, were moving toward it.
They looked like people who had lost their souls.
Sensing the danger, the three veteran masters shot toward them without hesitation.
And just as they reached out, their hands moving like streaks of light—
*Whoosh!*
A sharp whistle cut through the air.
Space warped.
The mist had curled into the razor-sharp claw of a giant beast.
Jeok Cheongang saw the darkness steeped within it reflected in his reddish eyes.
“How dare you!”
*Fwoosh—BOOM!*
Flames burst from his Flame Divine Palm with his furious cry, shattering the claw of magical power and heating the air.
The infernal blaze would not let it come an inch closer.
But he soon realized the brief attack had been deliberate.
*Shhhhhhh.*
Pale steam billowed up.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened.
He couldn’t see them.
Gung Gibang’s threadbare collar had been within reach.
Hyuk Mujin’s head had been right there, making Jeok Cheongang want to smack it on sight.
No.
*They’re gone.*
That was the only way to put it.
He had seen their bodies disappear into the mist, as though erased from the world.
*What in the...*
Jeok Cheongang swallowed the groan rising in his throat and looked around.
Then he realized something else.
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin weren’t the only ones who had vanished.
He let out the breath he had been holding.
When had it happened?
Had it begun with that strange sense of déjà vu?
He didn’t know.
The scenery before him looked unchanged, but everything else was different.
No one was there.
No one.
Even the Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint, who had stood scarcely thirty feet away, were nowhere to be seen.
He could sense neither their presence nor a trace of their qi.
*An illusion technique?
Or a Mystic Gate Formation?*
Dark arts he had heard of in rumors, and others he had faced himself on the battlefields of the Great Faction War, flashed through his mind.
None gave him an answer.
Even Jeok Cheongang, who had lived for more than a century and dominated an era, had never encountered dark arts like these.
*This is something else entirely.*
Even the great fiends of the previous generation, notorious under names like the Illusion Fiend and Guiguzi, had never managed anything like it.
More precisely, Jeok Cheongang’s formidable martial prowess had never allowed them to.
Even the strongest dark arts had their limits.
The Illusion Fiend, the Demonic Cult’s greatest master of illusion, had had both eyes gouged out.
Guiguzi, who had slaughtered hundreds of orthodox Murim warriors with his intricate Mystic Gate Formation, had melted into a pool of blood.
Both at the hands of one man: the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
But...
*I’ve never seen or heard of a formation like this.*
Jeok Cheongang stretched his senses farther than ever before.
The longer he searched, the more certain he became.
No matter how bizarre the dark arts, there should be a flow of energy and a core at its center.
In this strange space, he could find neither.
Only the dark mist approaching with the uniquely sticky, unpleasant energy of demonic qi—and someone’s steady breathing against his back.
“Sleeping through all this.
You’ve got it easy, you know.”
A faint smile touched his lips despite his grumbling.
He glanced at the Disciple who would have protested bitterly if he were awake, then muttered as though making a promise to himself.
“Don’t worry.
Whatever happens, I won’t let a single hair on you come to harm...”
His voice trailed off.
After a moment’s silence, he added with a sigh, “Just bear with it.
Losing one hair won’t kill you.”
His Disciple offered no answer.
Jeok Cheongang fixed his fiercely shining eyes on the dense mist.
“What are you waiting for?
Crawl the hell out here!”
The beings beyond the pale veil answered his call.
*Grrrr.*
The mist rolled in waves.
At last, countless eyes gleamed within it.
Jeok Cheongang drew a slow breath.
“Come in a whole pack, have you?”
Heat shimmered around him as Extreme Yang energy spread through his limbs and every part of his body.
He raised both fists, wrapped in fierce flames, toward the monsters that did not belong in this world.
“Come.”
The long night had begun.
The mist was too thick to see an inch ahead.
Countless shadows surged through it.
At the center of it all, flames burned ever more fiercely.
*Boom!*
One palm strike.
No more, no less.
The motion was devastating in its efficiency.
In its wake lay only heat enough to melt rock—and death.
*Thud!*
A huge body that could not be called human sank to its knees.
The three red eyes in its single head were still fixed on their prey, but the chest melted away without a trace proved which of them had been the hunter.
*Grrk.*
Light drained swiftly from its eyes.
Before the monster had breathed its last, the hunter had already turned to set other living things ablaze.
*Crunch!*

Jeok Cheongang’s body and mind never faltered.
It was like the day Mount Jiuhua had been engulfed in flames, decades ago.
No.

These were cursed beings that should never have appeared in the human world.
*Kyarruk!*
*Kraaaaah!*
They carried a madness and killing intent unlike anything he had felt before.
They had clearly lost their reason long ago and moved only at their master’s command.
Still, they charged without cease—
*RrrrCRUNCH!*

*Splaaat!*
Blood sprayed high into the air.
With a single sweep of his hand, as if brushing away insects, Jeok Cheongang sent hundreds of shreds of flesh flying in every direction.

So were the Daoists and the damned monks who held the Central Plains.

chapters.title: Chapter 1188
paragraphs: It was as if time had stopped.
The foul odors and reek of blood that had filled the air faded, and the monsters’ roars became faint echoes. But Jeok Cheongang noticed none of the changes around him.
No—he couldn’t.
All his senses were fixed on a single person.
*Squish.*
Unhurried footsteps approached through a pool of blood.
The countless monsters had stopped moving and parted to either side. Between them, someone came into view, filling Jeok Cheongang’s vision.
The sight chilled his heart so deeply it hurt.
The voice that slipped between his bloodless lips was more than a sound. It was a groan he couldn’t hold back, a scream he had barely managed to suppress.
“Have you been well?”
A voice he had never forgotten. A face that had grown a little unfamiliar.
The name of the man he was seeing again after well over ten years spilled from Jeok Cheongang’s lips with a cold breath.
“Cheon-ah, how are you—?”
The man, Jangcheon, smiled faintly at his former Master.
“It’s been a long time since anyone called me that.”
Each quiet word burrowed into Jeok Cheongang’s ears, raked through his lungs, and pierced his heart.
“I was worried you might not recognize me.”
As if that were possible.

Even if a hundred years had passed instead of ten, Jeok Cheongang would have recognized him. Then or now, however much had changed, Jangcheon was someone he could never forget for as long as he lived.
“But I needn’t have worried. You, of all people, would never forget me, Master. I nearly failed to recognize you, though, unworthy Disciple that I am.”
Since the day they had parted in a dark back alley, the Disciple had aged a little, while his Master had grown much younger.
But it wasn’t only Jeok Cheongang’s appearance that had changed when he Returned to Youth, leaving him looking like a middle-aged man.
Everything had changed.
Every last thing.
And among those changes was a truth no one could undo.
“You... weren’t you already dead?”
It had been a day of heavy snowfall, or so Jeok Cheongang had heard.

Somewhere on an unnamed mountainside near Jeongyang in Shanxi Province, Jangcheon had died before several witnesses. Miserably, wretchedly, as though he were being judged for the many atrocities he had committed.
But then—
How could—
“Dead? Me?”
His eyes widened for a moment, then curved with a laugh.
“Ha. Did you think I was the kind of bastard who’d die that easily?”
“No. I heard, quite clearly—”
“Yes, you heard. You didn’t see it for yourself.”
Jeok Cheongang’s gaze wavered at the calm reply.
It was true.

By the time he had asked around and found the place, only a few traces of the fierce battle remained. Jangcheon’s body was nowhere to be found. No one knew exactly why, and Jeok Cheongang hadn’t wanted to know.
Jeok Cheongang had only thought that the heavy snow said to have continued for nearly seven days and nights, along with the mountain beasts, might have erased Jangcheon’s last traces from the earth.
That was all.
He had left a bottle of liquor and a few drops of tears there, then returned to his own life.
That was what had happened.
“...You were alive all this time?”
“I nearly died. At the hands of that brat you’re looking after like a sacred ancestral tablet.”
Jangcheon’s pale, misty gaze settled on Jin Taekyung’s face over Jeok Cheongang’s shoulder.
“I can feel a familiar power in him. The qi of our sect, the Fire Gate Clan. Once, only you and I carried it.”
Jeok Cheongang said nothing. Jangcheon took another slow step.
*Squish.*
“I’ve heard no end of it. Apparently, I have a Junior Brother I never knew about.”
“You’re wrong. About all of it.”
Jeok Cheongang forced the words through clenched teeth.
“This boy is not your Junior Brother, and you are no Disciple of mine.”
“Why not?”
“Because you were cast out. You died committing unforgivable atrocities. That is the only truth.”
*Crack.*
His lips split, and blood filled his mouth.
But the sight before him—which had to be an illusion—didn’t change. Neither the shadowed face of his former Disciple nor the voice that kept reaching his ears.
“But Master, look. I’m still alive, aren’t I?”
“Don’t call me that!”
Even at Jeok Cheongang’s thunderous shout, Jangcheon kept coming. He looked at him with eyes full of regret.
“I knew what you must think of me, Master.”
“Shut your mouth!”
“After I came back from the brink of death, I spent a great deal of time thinking about everything that had happened. Every day felt like ten years.”
*Squish.*
The pool of blood rippled beneath his advancing steps.
Behind him, the monsters stood still as though they had agreed not to move. As Jangcheon drew closer, Jeok Cheongang could sense no danger or killing intent from him.
But—
*That can’t be. It’s all an illusion. I’m hearing things.*
Jeok Cheongang clenched his fists. The qi within him surged as though it had sensed its master’s turmoil, threatening to slip beyond his control. He subdued it and began to draw it up again.
Then Jangcheon said something he had never expected to hear.
“I was wrong. This unworthy Disciple was wrong about everything.”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes trembled. Unlike his body, which had regained its youth, they still held the weight of all his years.
“Please forgive me. No—Master, punish this wretched man yourself.”
No. That couldn’t be.
He must not fall for lies conjured by dark arts.
And yet—
The Extreme Yang energy gathering in his clenched fists wavered like a candle in the wind, then went out.
Just as it had on the day when, despite possessing martial arts powerful enough to look down on the world, he could do nothing but watch his Disciple walk away.
“I won’t make excuses. Whatever punishment you give me, I’ll bear it all.”
The words he had wanted so badly to hear.
“I betrayed your trust, disgraced our sect, and killed innocent people. I committed sins I can never wash away.”
The scene he had imagined countless times.
“So please, kill me.”
“...Enough.”
“Kill me. With the very hands that took me in more than twenty years ago.”
“Enough. Stop.”
Jeok Cheongang couldn’t breathe. His heart ached as though an unseen hand were squeezing it.
Everything he was seeing and hearing had to be nothing but an illusion.
It had to be.
Yet the wound deep inside him, the one he had thought long since closed, was tearing open again.
“Master.”
Jeok Cheongang did not answer.
He only stared blankly at his old Disciple as his vision grew hazy. Old, worn memories overlaid the sight.
“If I can’t take you as my Master... I’ll kill myself.”
Even after more than twenty years, he remembered clearly.
“No, kill me now. With the very hands that saved me.”
The desperate look in the boy’s eyes.
“Might Makes Right. Didn’t you teach me that, Master? That’s what Murim is—no, what the world is. The weak should die at the hands of the strong.”
The murderer’s smile he could never forget.
“Kill me. It’s the only way to stop me.”
And the feeble old man who, in the end, had failed to stop him.
Even after he had gone out into the world to correct that mistake, he had lingered for a long time at the very spot where wild beasts and snow-laden winds had passed.
“Old man, has something happened?”
It was the place where the man who had lived as Jangcheon had fallen under the name Jopil.

A traveler, finding it strange that Jeok Cheongang still stood there late into the night, motionless as a stone monument, had asked him what was wrong. Jeok Cheongang had answered that his only blood relative had died there.
The man had been foolish and useless beyond words, but he had come hoping to at least recover the body.
And in that moment, he had realized that even after nearly ten years, he still wasn’t ready.
“Master.”
The clear voice scattered the layers of memory.
Tears streamed down Jeok Cheongang’s face like water through a broken dam. Through them, he saw the Disciple he had wanted so badly to meet again.
“Cheon-ah.”
“Yes. Your Disciple is listening, Master. I’m here with you.”
*Squish.*
One step.
*Squish.*
Another step.
*Squish.*
They were close enough to feel each other’s breath.
Jeok Cheongang beckoned to the Disciple he had finally met again. Jangcheon took the last step toward his Master’s small embrace.
With him came a streak of light prepared, from the very beginning, for this moment alone.
*Thnk.*
Pain hotter than any Scorching Yang Qi.
Blood burst forth at the same instant, as though to prove this was real.
*Shhk! Patter, patter!*
Fresh blood spattered the ground. Across a handspan of empty space, their gazes met.
One deeply sunken. The other wide with disbelief.
In the brief silence, Jangcheon’s lips parted.
At Jangcheon’s question, his agitation impossible to hide, Jeok Cheongang smiled sadly.
“I wanted to be fooled for a moment. I wasn’t fooled.”
He tightened his grip on the blade he had caught at the last instant.
*Crreeeak.*
It hurt.
Every time the dagger embedded in his palm twisted, a dizzying pain spread through his body.
But it didn’t matter. This was nothing compared to the mind demon that had tormented him moments before.
“What’s your name?”
It had been more than twenty years ago.
He had met a boy who endured kicks raining down on his whole body and still managed to shove a dirt-covered bun into his mouth.
“...I don’t know.”
Jeok Cheongang had seen his younger self in the boy: a fierce little child who had once wandered the world begging for food, without even knowing his own name.
Perhaps that was why the old man’s heart had acted on a whim.
“Jangcheon. From now on, your name is Jangcheon.”
The Master had given him a name and a new life. The Disciple had thrown them both away and left.
The wound that departure had carved deep in Jeok Cheongang’s heart had become a scar that would never fade.
But...
“I think I can let you go now.”
Yes. At last.
With those words Jangcheon would never hear, Jeok Cheongang threw a single punch.
*Kwaaaaaah!*
Fierce flames consumed Jangcheon—or rather, whatever had taken on his likeness—and swept across the mountainside.

The other wide with disbelief.
In the brief silence, Jangcheon’s lips parted.
At Jangcheon’s question, his agitation impossible to hide, Jeok Cheongang smiled sadly.
“I wanted to be fooled for a moment.
I wasn’t fooled.”
He tightened his grip on the blade he had caught at the last instant.
*Crreeeak.*
It hurt.
Every time the dagger embedded in his palm twisted, a dizzying pain spread through his body.
But it didn’t matter.
This was nothing compared to the mind demon that had tormented him moments before.
“What’s your name?”
It had been more than twenty years ago.
He had met a boy who endured kicks raining down on his whole body and still managed to shove a dirt-covered bun into his mouth.
“...I don’t know.”
Jeok Cheongang had seen his younger self in the boy: a fierce little child who had once wandered the world begging for food, without even knowing his own name.
Perhaps that was why the old man’s heart had acted on a whim.
“Jangcheon.
From now on, your name is Jangcheon.”
The Master had given him a name and a new life.
The Disciple had thrown them both away and left.
The wound that departure had carved deep in Jeok Cheongang’s heart had become a scar that would never fade.
But...
“I think I can let you go now.”
Yes.
At last.
With those words Jangcheon would never hear, Jeok Cheongang threw a single punch.
*Kwaaaaaah!*
Fierce flames consumed Jangcheon—or rather, whatever had taken on his likeness—and swept across the mountainside.

chapters.title: Chapter 1189
paragraphs: “Grrrraaaaaah!”
It wasn’t a scream a human could make—or even a sound any living creature could produce.
It was all that remained to a monster that had already died once and forgotten pain: a warning bell announcing that his corrupted soul had burned away, the final cry of his second death.
*Fwoooooom!*
The hellfire of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist swept wildly through the space.
Then came a blinding flash, followed by an even louder roar.
*RrrrRUMBLE!*
The ground shook. Embers and ash churned together and scattered in every direction.
Beyond them, a shadow slowly crumpled.
Jangcheon.
No—one of the monsters wearing Jangcheon’s likeness.
*Black Ghost.*
Jeok Cheongang recognized it at once.
A monster given new life using the body and soul of the dead.
Neither dead nor alive, Black Ghosts were among the strangest and most powerful of the countless monsters under the Lord of Heaven.
Yes, this was surely—
*Magic, after all.*
A space where even the wind brushing his skin felt alien. Phenomena too intricate and bizarre to be explained by a mere formation.
The suspicion he had harbored became certainty. Jeok Cheongang felt the flow of qi around the area begin to churn.
And he sensed the cause of the change, too.
*Shhhhh.*
A sudden cold wind pressed down on the heat haze distorting the space and settled the drifting embers and ash.
It wasn’t an ordinary wind. It was a wave of qi announcing the arrival of something else.
“So, you’ve come.”
Jeok Cheongang looked steadily at the new intruders.
East, west, south, and north.
Four shadows had appeared around him, each gazing his way.
Different faces, yet somehow alike.
“Master.”
Four voices rang out as one.

There was Jangcheon as a dirt-covered child, just as he’d looked the day they first met. Jangcheon as a boy, pleading to be accepted as a Disciple. Jangcheon as a young man, and Jangcheon as he’d looked on the day he left.
All frozen in forms from a day that could never be taken back.
“Master. I’ve come. Cheon-ah is here.”
The four Jangcheons spoke together and stepped forward. At the same time, the countless monsters encircling the area tightened their ring.
A net over heaven and earth, drawn tight for one man alone.
Yet even amid the monsters’ killing intent, Jeok Cheongang spoke calmly.
“How strange. Four more Disciples I never knew I had.”
“Master. How could you forget me?”
The voice rang out from every direction, as if all four shared a single body. Jeok Cheongang gave a bitter smile.
“I haven’t forgotten. I’ve only decided to keep you in my memories.”
He wasn’t speaking to the monsters wearing the illusion. He was speaking to his old Disciple, who wasn’t there.
It didn’t matter if his words reached no one. Only now did he know for certain, and if he didn’t say it now, he might never get the chance.
Even if the living Jangcheon had appeared before him, his choice would have been the same.
“I was a poor Master, and you were a poor Disciple. But let’s leave the wrongs we did each other for some distant day when we meet again.”
Spilled water couldn’t be gathered up, and time that had passed couldn’t be turned back.
What mattered was now. And Jeok Cheongang still had someone precious to protect.
“So, Cheon-ah.”
As he had long ago, Jeok Cheongang spoke his old Disciple’s name gently, letting it leave his lips.
His eyes moved from one face to the next, taking in the features still etched vividly in his memory. He felt the warmth and breath of someone on his back.
He felt that he was alive, and resolved to stay that way.
“I expel you from the sect.”
In that instant—
*Whoosh!*
A flash erupted in the dark mist.
No. It was a flame burning as bright as light—a giant of fire, finally risen to his feet.
*Fwoooooom!*
The heat of the Flamefire Path distorted the space.
One step. Nearly a hundred yards vanished, and the monsters’ wide eyes rushed closer.
*Crunch!*
No more words or thoughts were needed.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, crushed everything before him.
Enemies surged in from every direction, but he saw and felt everything happening around him.
With his eyes, his ears, and sometimes with a sixth sense beyond the other five.
“Grrrraah!”
A group of monsters charged at him, each with eight arms and three heads.
They looked like asuras from legend. Their many arms—impossible now to tell whether they belonged to humans or beasts—whipped wildly, raining blows down on Jeok Cheongang’s head.
Or, more precisely, on the spot where he had been.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
Their attacks cut through empty air and carved up the ground. Then a voice pierced the monsters’ ears.
Quiet, yet hot as fire—and somehow colder than ice.
“How many hearts do you have?”
That was the last thing they heard.
*Fwoosh—SPLAT!*
Even as their consciousness faded, the monsters didn’t know when or how they had died.

They didn’t know Jeok Cheongang had launched himself off the ground, extended his Palm Force, and slashed downward with it. Nor did they know that the horrific heat within it had burned not only their hearts, but every organ in their bodies.
But the four pairs of eyes watching Jeok Cheongang did know.
They had been waiting for this moment from the start. As if on cue, they moved together without a hair’s breadth of error.
*ShhhhK!*
A low, faint whistle slipped into his senses, keen as a blade and chilling enough to raise goose bumps.
Jeok Cheongang, who had just melted dozens of monsters in an instant, immediately sensed the ominous energy closing in on him.
He sensed that there was more than one.
But their speed—and the power they carried—exceeded anything he’d expected.
In that slowed instant, Jeok Cheongang sensed four streaks of Force flying at him from his blind spots.
He twisted with all his might, moving by instinct more than reason.
*Shhk!*
Blood sprayed with a cool slicing sound.
Not the monsters’ green blood, with its foul stench and poisonous fumes, but the red blood of a living human.
Even through the sting of pain, Jeok Cheongang regained his balance at the last possible moment and landed with a satisfied smile.
What a relief.
His own flesh had been cut, but Jin Taekyung hadn’t so much as been scratched.
The smile brought on by that relief didn’t last long.
His wound wasn’t serious. The battle, however, was clearly going against him.
A Master fighting to protect his Disciple, against countless monsters charging without fear of death.
And the greatest problem of all: the four Black Ghosts, carefully measuring their distance and looking for an opening even now.
*Strong. Stronger than I expected.*
They seemed at least a step above the other Black Ghosts he had faced—perhaps nearly two.
He had no way of knowing whether that was because of the Magic surrounding the area or because these four were particularly powerful Black Ghosts. But one thing was certain.
*This will be a tough fight.*
In truth, even that didn’t begin to describe it.
Their individual strength was formidable, but the four Supreme Peak masters moved like one organism, sharing their thoughts. Even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t afford to underestimate them.
That would have been true even if they were living humans. But these monsters felt neither emotion nor pain.
And everything was going in their favor.
Even now.
“Grrrraaaah!”
The monsters roared and charged again, while the Black Ghosts vanished among them. Jeok Cheongang understood their intentions at once.
*They’re taking turns wearing me down...!*
To break a huge rock quickly, you needed a sharp chisel and a heavy hammer. Given enough time, though, even the occasional shower would do.
Drop by drop, the water struck the hard surface of the rock until cracks began to form.
But the monsters surging endlessly under the Black Ghosts’ command were neither light raindrops nor a passing shower.
They were waves.
Raging waves, driven by the force to smash through any reef and a blind madness that sent them hurling their lives away without hesitation.
But Jeok Cheongang wasn’t a rock that would stand still and wait to be worn down.
*I’ll end this at once.*
His nature was fire. He had raised a greater flame than anyone under heaven, and so he was the Fire King.
*Crack.*
Jeok Cheongang clenched his teeth.
His eyes glowed red, piercing the dark mist. Space warped along the heat haze rising in strands from his entire body.
*Fwoooosh.*
Energy like molten lava surged through his limbs and every part of his body. A breath like steam escaped between his slowly parting lips.
“I’ll kill every last one of you.”
If they were rocks, he would melt them. If they were waves, he would make them evaporate.
Even if he himself turned to ash, even if everything burned away, the Fire Gate Clan’s flame would not go out.
No—a blaze greater than his own would rise from it.
“Come!”
The giant’s roar shook the air in every direction as he completed his preparations.
“Whoa, you startled me. My ears are going to burst.”
Jeok Cheongang barely managed to rein in the internal energy that had nearly surged back against him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1190
paragraphs: Silence fell for a moment.
The monsters blinked their glowing eyes at the unexpected turn of events. So did the four Black Ghosts who were supposed to be commanding them.
In that brief stillness, Jeok Cheongang slowly turned his head. Over his shoulder, he found a pair of eyes staring blankly at him.
“What is it, you bastard?”
Unlike his Master, who had barely managed to squeeze out the words, the Disciple answered without hesitation.
“It’s me.”
“Not that.”
“What, then?”
“When did you wake up? No—how?”
“I just woke up.”
“...I mean, how?”
Jeok Cheongang wondered if he was seeing things.
Hadn’t the Slaughter Saint—and the Divine Physician himself—insisted that the effects wouldn’t fully wear off for at least another half a day?
*Could this be a hallucination caused by Magic or something?*
Just as that rather plausible suspicion began to grow, a familiar voice reached his ears again.
“What kind of question is that? I woke up because I woke up.”
The expression and tone were unmistakably annoyed.
With much of his suspicion fading, Jeok Cheongang asked, “Proof?”
“What proof? Do you wake up every morning thinking, ‘Wow, that’s crazy. How on earth did I wake up today?’ Well, considering your age, maybe you do.”
You could imitate the outside, but what was inside never changed.
Jeok Cheongang’s fists began to itch, as though he’d been reunited with his long-lost soulmate. At last, he let go of every doubt.
“So it really is you!”
“Yes, it’s me. So could you lower your voice a little? I’ve been listening to you this whole time, and I think my eardrums are a little busted.”
“I should’ve known better than to believe a word that quack said—wait. What do you mean, you’ve been listening this whole time?”
“Exactly what it sounds like.”
“You were awake? Since when?”
“When you said, ‘How many hearts do you have?’ Judging by that line alone, you sounded like the Heavenly Demon.”
At that answer, Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet sigh of relief.
Thank goodness.
If Jin Taekyung had regained consciousness a little earlier, he would have seen what happened before. He would have been hurt to learn that his Master still hadn’t been able to put that burden down.
Then a thought struck Jeok Cheongang.
“...If you were already awake, why did you stay quiet?”
“At first, I thought it was a dream.”
Jin Taekyung answered without a hint of shame, then added, “But it was comfortable, so I stayed put a little longer.”
“Heh.”
Jeok Cheongang smiled warmly at his Disciple’s honesty.
“Still comfortable?”
“Of course.”
“How strange. I’m not comfortable.”
“One thing I’ve learned from all my years of living is that life isn’t always comfortable.”
“And do you plan to keep living?”
“Isn’t that obvious?”
“Then how about you get down already?”
“My back’s nice and warm from your Scorching Yang Qi, so could I stay up here another seven or eight minutes?”
“Of course. Anything’s possible.”
The smile vanished from Jeok Cheongang’s lips.
“You’ll just be half dead.”
“Ah. I’d rather not.”
With a deep sigh, Jin Taekyung hopped down to the ground.

He didn’t have to focus, put any strength into it, or draw on his internal energy. The moment he thought of moving, the thick iron chains binding Master and Disciple together burst apart like a spiderweb crushed beneath a boulder.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
The act was as simple as breathing. Its consequences were anything but.
*Shhhhing—SPLAT!*
A harsh metallic shriek. A blurred streak cutting through the air. Then the dreadful sound of torn flesh and blood gushing up like a fountain.
A group of monsters caught by the chains as they flew apart crumpled like straw. Four glowing gazes flashed around them.
“—Jin. Taekyung.”
The voices echoed through the space, layered over one another.
Jin Taekyung studied the Black Ghosts’ faces and shrugged.
“Yeah, it’s your hyung.”
“—The chosen one.”
“—Target confirmed.”
“—Carry out the order. As that person wills.”
“Pick one of you to do the talking. You all look so alike I can barely tell you apart as it is.”
His tone and expression were calm. But White Flame, the spear now in his hand, gleamed unmistakably through the mist.
“Still, there’s something familiar about those mugs. I feel like I’ve seen them somewhere.”
Jeok Cheongang faltered at the unexpected response, then swallowed a bitter smile.
Perhaps it was only natural that Jin Taekyung didn’t recognize those faces. To him, they were just one among countless villains he’d glimpsed for a fleeting instant.
*It’s probably better if he doesn’t remember.*
A Master should always be a pillar for his Disciple, someone he could lean on.
That was why Jeok Cheongang didn’t want him to know. He couldn’t let him see how rotten he was inside, beneath a surface that looked so solid.
*Yes. This is enough.*
Suppressing the words circling in his heart, Jeok Cheongang spoke in a deliberately calm tone.
“Well, even if you have seen them, what would that change?”
“Fair enough.”
*Bzzzz.*
At Jin Taekyung’s answer, the silver spearhead trembled.
A tremendous energy began to pulse at last, and dark blue flames rose and billowed.
“Be careful. These things are different from the ones we’ve faced so far.”
“I know.”
“You do?”
“Yeah. I’ve been to places like this so many times I’m sick of them.”
Jin Taekyung drew a deep breath. The air was unpleasantly damp and foul-smelling.
He knew this place.
More precisely, he could feel its true nature against every inch of his skin.
Even if those translucent letters hadn’t appeared in midair, that fact wouldn’t have changed.

**System You have entered the restricted area **Tianshan Mountains**. - You have entered the mutated Gate **Forest of Death-I**. - The abilities of all enemies within this restricted area and Gate have been greatly increased. - All manner of evil Magic and the energy of death are consuming the area. Do not let your guard down. - You have not yet met the Gate-clearing conditions.
A Gate. A passage through which demons marched into another world—and a land of death that had become their prison.
A graveyard that had swallowed countless Hunters.
*Whoosh.*
The flames wrapping around the spearhead surged higher.
They burned like a campfire sheltering souls that had died in the cold, and like a gravekeeper’s torch driving off the unclean things wandering this vast cemetery.
Higher. Fiercer.
Until their dark blue light filled his Master’s wide eyes.
Jeok Cheongang drew a sharp breath.
The flames before him were that vast, that hot—
And that bright.
They shone with a different light from his Master’s, yet carried an even warmer power.
Jin Taekyung gave his wide-eyed Master a faint smile.
“I told you. A lot’s happened.”
What was Jeok Cheongang supposed to say?
He didn’t spend long wondering. After a brief moment at a loss for words, he clenched his fists.
“Let’s go.”
No answer or question followed that brief command.
The moment the words left his lips, Master and Disciple were already surging toward their enemies, setting the air ablaze.
No.
The two Fire Kings.
*Rrrrrumble!*
Their flames merged into hellfire nothing could extinguish and tore through the darkness.
I don’t know.
I don’t know exactly how much time passed after I lost consciousness, or how many monsters I cut down in this place.
Truthfully, none of that mattered.
Looking back, I’d always been that kind of guy.
Like someone being chased, I’d race ahead with my eyes fixed forward, only to come to my senses somewhere I’d never expected.
And then—
*I had to run again. Without even having time to look back.*
I still don’t know the true name of the thing chasing so close that I can feel its breath on the back of my neck.
All I can do is cling with all my strength to a hope that seems ready to go out at any moment, and believe that if I take one more step—just one more—I’ll finally reach the end of this road.
Yeah.
Just like right now.
*Shhhaaa.*
Thousands of times. Tens of thousands.
No—more times than I could count.
As I repeated that familiar movement, an unnervingly low whistle ran along the spearhead slicing through the air.
The strike was precise and swift. The result it would bring was just as clear.
*Shhk.*
A slicing sound as familiar as the wind—and the sensation of death traveling up the shaft in my hands.
*It’s over.*
I was certain, and this time reality agreed.
*Splash.*
The enemy before me dropped to its knees in a pool of blood—or, by now, what would more accurately be called a stream.
But there was no groan of pain, no pleading look begging to survive.
The last Black Ghost stared at me with unfeeling eyes and said only this:
“—That person. Is waiting.”
Like an actor carefully delivering every word of the line he’d been given.
“—For you, Jin Taekyung.”
And that was all.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System Mutated Gate **Forest of Death-I** successfully cleared! - You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP! - Level up! - All status ailments and fatigue have been recovered. - Gate-clearing conditions have been met.
A clear ringing sounded for me alone, and strength filled me once more. Beyond the fading mist, a field of magical power appeared in midair.
But neither Jeok Cheongang nor I reacted to any of the changes around us.
I looked at him. He looked silently at the Black Ghost that had met its end.
At the soulless shell of a boy who had once been someone’s joy and reason for living.
Then, after a silence that was brief but felt long, Jeok Cheongang turned away.
“Damn it, what kind of place is this? I can’t even tell how to get out. I feel like a lost child.”
He grumbled as usual, but his voice was thick, as though soaked through. Somehow, I heard relief in it.
Or at least I wanted to.
For his sake.
I hoped the tremor in the voice that had said *I can finally let you go now* would ease, if only a little. The painful shudder I’d felt through my back, too.
*This is enough.*
If someone was facing and overcoming the pain they’d hidden inside all alone, then I could only believe that keeping my eyes closed for a moment had been the right choice.
A pillar was a reassuring support simply by being there. But it couldn’t stand upright on its own.
“What are you waiting for? Get moving.”
“Yes.”
I smiled faintly and nodded.
“I’ll lead the way.”
We walked on together.

sentences.text: Silence fell for a moment.
The monsters blinked their glowing eyes at the unexpected turn of events.
So did the four Black Ghosts who were supposed to be commanding them.
In that brief stillness, Jeok Cheongang slowly turned his head.
Over his shoulder, he found a pair of eyes staring blankly at him.
“What is it, you bastard?”
Unlike his Master, who had barely managed to squeeze out the words, the Disciple answered without hesitation.
“It’s me.”
“Not that.”
“What, then?”
“When did you wake up?
No—how?”
“I just woke up.”
“...I mean, how?”
Jeok Cheongang wondered if he was seeing things.
Hadn’t the Slaughter Saint—and the Divine Physician himself—insisted that the effects wouldn’t fully wear off for at least another half a day?
*Could this be a hallucination caused by Magic or something?*
Just as that rather plausible suspicion began to grow, a familiar voice reached his ears again.
“What kind of question is that?
I woke up because I woke up.”
The expression and tone were unmistakably annoyed.
With much of his suspicion fading, Jeok Cheongang asked, “Proof?”
“What proof?
Do you wake up every morning thinking, ‘Wow, that’s crazy.
How on earth did I wake up today?’ Well, considering your age, maybe you do.”
You could imitate the outside, but what was inside never changed.
Jeok Cheongang’s fists began to itch, as though he’d been reunited with his long-lost soulmate.
At last, he let go of every doubt.
“So it really is you!”
“Yes, it’s me.
So could you lower your voice a little?
I’ve been listening to you this whole time, and I think my eardrums are a little busted.”
“I should’ve known better than to believe a word that quack said—wait.
What do you mean, you’ve been listening this whole time?”
“Exactly what it sounds like.”
“You were awake?
Since when?”
“When you said, ‘How many hearts do you have?’ Judging by that line alone, you sounded like the Heavenly Demon.”
At that answer, Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet sigh of relief.
Thank goodness.
If Jin Taekyung had regained consciousness a little earlier, he would have seen what happened before.
He would have been hurt to learn that his Master still hadn’t been able to put that burden down.
Then a thought struck Jeok Cheongang.
“...If you were already awake, why did you stay quiet?”
“At first, I thought it was a dream.”
Jin Taekyung answered without a hint of shame, then added, “But it was comfortable, so I stayed put a little longer.”
“Heh.”
Jeok Cheongang smiled warmly at his Disciple’s honesty.
“Still comfortable?”
“Of course.”
“How strange.
I’m not comfortable.”
“One thing I’ve learned from all my years of living is that life isn’t always comfortable.”
“And do you plan to keep living?”
“Isn’t that obvious?”
“Then how about you get down already?”
“My back’s nice and warm from your Scorching Yang Qi, so could I stay up here another seven or eight minutes?”
“Of course.
Anything’s possible.”
The smile vanished from Jeok Cheongang’s lips.
“You’ll just be half dead.”
“Ah.
I’d rather not.”
With a deep sigh, Jin Taekyung hopped down to the ground.
He didn’t have to focus, put any strength into it, or draw on his internal energy.
The moment he thought of moving, the thick iron chains binding Master and Disciple together burst apart like a spiderweb crushed beneath a boulder.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
The act was as simple as breathing.
Its consequences were anything but.
*Shhhhing—SPLAT!*
A harsh metallic shriek.
A blurred streak cutting through the air.
Then the dreadful sound of torn flesh and blood gushing up like a fountain.
A group of monsters caught by the chains as they flew apart crumpled like straw.
Four glowing gazes flashed around them.
“—Jin.
Taekyung.”
The voices echoed through the space, layered over one another.
Jin Taekyung studied the Black Ghosts’ faces and shrugged.
“Yeah, it’s your hyung.”
“—The chosen one.”
“—Target confirmed.”
“—Carry out the order.
As that person wills.”
“Pick one of you to do the talking.
You all look so alike I can barely tell you apart as it is.”
His tone and expression were calm.
But White Flame, the spear now in his hand, gleamed unmistakably through the mist.
“Still, there’s something familiar about those mugs.
I feel like I’ve seen them somewhere.”
Jeok Cheongang faltered at the unexpected response, then swallowed a bitter smile.
Perhaps it was only natural that Jin Taekyung didn’t recognize those faces.
To him, they were just one among countless villains he’d glimpsed for a fleeting instant.
*It’s probably better if he doesn’t remember.*
A Master should always be a pillar for his Disciple, someone he could lean on.
That was why Jeok Cheongang didn’t want him to know.
He couldn’t let him see how rotten he was inside, beneath a surface that looked so solid.
*Yes.
This is enough.*
Suppressing the words circling in his heart, Jeok Cheongang spoke in a deliberately calm tone.
“Well, even if you have seen them, what would that change?”
“Fair enough.”
*Bzzzz.*
At Jin Taekyung’s answer, the silver spearhead trembled.
A tremendous energy began to pulse at last, and dark blue flames rose and billowed.
“Be careful.
These things are different from the ones we’ve faced so far.”
“I know.”
“You do?”
“Yeah.
I’ve been to places like this so many times I’m sick of them.”
Jin Taekyung drew a deep breath.
The air was unpleasantly damp and foul-smelling.
He knew this place.
More precisely, he could feel its true nature against every inch of his skin.
Even if those translucent letters hadn’t appeared in midair, that fact wouldn’t have changed.

**System You have entered the restricted area **Tianshan Mountains**. - You have entered the mutated Gate **Forest of Death-I**. - The abilities of all enemies within this restricted area and Gate have been greatly increased. - All manner of evil Magic and the energy of death are consuming the area.
Do not let your guard down. - You have not yet met the Gate-clearing conditions.
A Gate.
A passage through which demons marched into another world—and a land of death that had become their prison.
A graveyard that had swallowed countless Hunters.
*Whoosh.*
The flames wrapping around the spearhead surged higher.
They burned like a campfire sheltering souls that had died in the cold, and like a gravekeeper’s torch driving off the unclean things wandering this vast cemetery.
Higher.
Fiercer.
Until their dark blue light filled his Master’s wide eyes.
Jeok Cheongang drew a sharp breath.
The flames before him were that vast, that hot—
And that bright.
They shone with a different light from his Master’s, yet carried an even warmer power.
Jin Taekyung gave his wide-eyed Master a faint smile.
“I told you.
A lot’s happened.”
What was Jeok Cheongang supposed to say?
He didn’t spend long wondering.
After a brief moment at a loss for words, he clenched his fists.
“Let’s go.”
No answer or question followed that brief command.
The moment the words left his lips, Master and Disciple were already surging toward their enemies, setting the air ablaze.
No.
The two Fire Kings.
*Rrrrrumble!*
Their flames merged into hellfire nothing could extinguish and tore through the darkness.
I don’t know.
I don’t know exactly how much time passed after I lost consciousness, or how many monsters I cut down in this place.
Truthfully, none of that mattered.
Looking back, I’d always been that kind of guy.
Like someone being chased, I’d race ahead with my eyes fixed forward, only to come to my senses somewhere I’d never expected.
And then—
*I had to run again.
Without even having time to look back.*
I still don’t know the true name of the thing chasing so close that I can feel its breath on the back of my neck.
All I can do is cling with all my strength to a hope that seems ready to go out at any moment, and believe that if I take one more step—just one more—I’ll finally reach the end of this road.
Yeah.
Just like right now.
*Shhhaaa.*
Thousands of times.
Tens of thousands.
No—more times than I could count.
As I repeated that familiar movement, an unnervingly low whistle ran along the spearhead slicing through the air.
The strike was precise and swift.
The result it would bring was just as clear.
*Shhk.*
A slicing sound as familiar as the wind—and the sensation of death traveling up the shaft in my hands.
*It’s over.*
I was certain, and this time reality agreed.
*Splash.*
The enemy before me dropped to its knees in a pool of blood—or, by now, what would more accurately be called a stream.
But there was no groan of pain, no pleading look begging to survive.
The last Black Ghost stared at me with unfeeling eyes and said only this:
“—That person.
Is waiting.”
Like an actor carefully delivering every word of the line he’d been given.
“—For you, Jin Taekyung.”
And that was all.
*Ding.
Ding.
Ding.*

**System Mutated Gate **Forest of Death-I** successfully cleared! - You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP! - Level up! - All status ailments and fatigue have been recovered. - Gate-clearing conditions have been met.
A clear ringing sounded for me alone, and strength filled me once more.
Beyond the fading mist, a field of magical power appeared in midair.
But neither Jeok Cheongang nor I reacted to any of the changes around us.
I looked at him.
He looked silently at the Black Ghost that had met its end.
At the soulless shell of a boy who had once been someone’s joy and reason for living.
Then, after a silence that was brief but felt long, Jeok Cheongang turned away.
“Damn it, what kind of place is this?
I can’t even tell how to get out.
I feel like a lost child.”
He grumbled as usual, but his voice was thick, as though soaked through.
Somehow, I heard relief in it.
Or at least I wanted to.
For his sake.
I hoped the tremor in the voice that had said *I can finally let you go now* would ease, if only a little.
The painful shudder I’d felt through my back, too.
*This is enough.*
If someone was facing and overcoming the pain they’d hidden inside all alone, then I could only believe that keeping my eyes closed for a moment had been the right choice.
A pillar was a reassuring support simply by being there.
But it couldn’t stand upright on its own.
“What are you waiting for?
Get moving.”
“Yes.”
I smiled faintly and nodded.
“I’ll lead the way.”
We walked on together.
The place was still dark, covered in blood and corpses.
But for some reason, it seemed a little brighter.

chapters.title: Chapter 1191
paragraphs: The only path connecting reality and a Gate.
The sensation of passing through a magical field was more than familiar to a veteran Hunter like me. Even so, it was often unpleasant enough to make me shudder.
Like now.
*Whoooosh.*
Was this what it felt like to be swept into a whirlpool?
The cold, sticky sensation of magical power wrapped around my entire body, then spat me out somewhere on the other side.
The moment I opened my eyes in the new space, I realized something I hadn’t known before.
*It’s different.*
Branches packed so tightly they covered the sky. Steep hills.
The mountains of corpses and rivers of blood that had filled every direction were gone.
But the scenery wasn’t the only thing that had changed.
Magical power.
That filthy energy should have fallen away the moment I left the Gate. Instead, it was still clinging to my body.
No. It filled this entire space.
“This is...”
The words came out like a groan.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been shuddering at the magical field’s repulsive sensation, reacted at once when I fell silent.
“What is it?”
Normally, I’d have laughed it off and said it was nothing.

But the intense sense of déjà vu pressing in on all five senses since the moment I opened my eyes brought back memories from less than a few weeks ago. And Jeok Cheongang already knew most of the truth about me.
“I’ve been somewhere like this before. Very recently, in fact.”
“Ah. Could it be...?”
“Yes. The incident I told you about.”
A gigantic mushroom cloud swallowing civilization. A metropolis with no trace of life.
And a being waiting for me in a dark castle newly raised above the blackened earth.
*Morgoth.*
That was it.
This place carried an energy remarkably like the Dragon Lair the Black Dragon Duke Morgoth had built atop the ruins of Moscow.
An energy intense enough that you could call it the Demon Realm.
*No. It’s even stronger.*
According to Jeok Cheongang, I’d been unconscious for a little over a day.
I hadn’t felt magical power this pure until I approached Morgoth’s Dragon Lair. Here, power nearly as strong was already churning all around us.
*So this is what the System meant by a restricted area.*
Now I understood.
All kinds of absurd rumors floated around Murim, but if anything, the stories about this damn mountain range had understated the truth.
Now that I’d seen and felt the Tianshan Mountains for myself, I knew they were a forbidden land. A Land of Ruin.
Uninvited guests who hadn’t received their master’s permission shouldn’t enter—and couldn’t leave.
And this endless range of dark mountains showed no sign of revealing the secrets it hid within its vast bulk.
Not its master. Not the other uninvited guests besides Jeok Cheongang and me.
“I don’t see the others.”
“I suspected as much when that strange thing—whatever it was called—caught us. Seems I was right.”
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes at the mist drifting around us, but that didn’t make the missing people suddenly appear.
Even a superhuman who could make out an ant over three hundred yards away couldn’t peer through the space between reality and a Gate with human eyes.
*...Right. That would be impossible.*
Then a thought crossed my mind.
*With human eyes.*
I couldn’t be sure this idea would work. Frankly, the odds favored me wasting my strength and making things worse.
But when there’s only one path ahead—and you’ve already traveled it once—then no matter how huge an obstacle stands in the way, you have to smash through it and keep going.
*Bzzzzzz.*
The air began to tremble. I took a deep breath and raised my spearhead.
Slowly enough to make someone yawn, I spread the energy coiled within me through my entire body.
I felt Jeok Cheongang react to the move, but only for a moment. Then everything around me fell silent.
More precisely, my concentration reached its peak and shut out everything I didn’t need, down to the slightest noise.
For one purpose alone.
To find the other spaces hidden behind the invisible veil.
And then—
*Keeeeeng.*
A ringing like thunder filled my ears. A terrible headache struck without warning, turning my vision white.
*Ding.*
Somewhere, a clear chime rang faintly. I knew my reckless attempt had succeeded—and that I couldn’t let this fleeting opening slip away.
*Drip. Drip.*
Had the tiny blood vessels in my eyes burst one by one? Or was it the blood slipping between my lips without my noticing?
Everything I saw was red. Pain stabbed through my chest and brain.
It didn’t matter.
I’d already seen it. Read it.
*Cut.*
I let out the breath I’d been holding and brought the spearhead slashing down from high above me.
Along the single path my other eye—the Mind’s Eye—had shown me.
*Shhhhaaa—*
A blinding flash split the world. Split the invisible veil.
**System Status effect **Trance** has ended.
That was the first line to appear before Jin Taekyung’s eyes.
It was the signal flare. A signal flare announcing a wave of System notifications.
*Ding. Beep.*

**System Special ability **Mind’s Eye** has been activated because its activation conditions have been met! - Your insight into **Mind’s Eye** has deepened. - Always exercise caution. This ability can cause severe harm to the user’s mind and body, and in the worst case, can lead to death! - Status effect **Exhaustion** has been applied! - Status effect **Extreme Fatigue** has been applied! - Status effect **Internal Injury** has...
Jin Taekyung gasped for breath.
His chest felt tight. Nausea rose, and his disoriented body swayed from side to side.
Through vision warped like a heat haze, he saw Jeok Cheongang rush up to support him, shouting something. His battered senses could barely register the man’s words or touch.
For a moment.
Then a second wave swept over him, accompanied by a cascade of chimes.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System Mutated Gate **Forest of Death-II** destroyed! - Mutated Gate **Forest of Death-III** destroyed! - ... - Mutated Gate **Forest of Death-VI** destroyed! - You have achieved the very rare achievement **Knock, and It Shall Be Opened**! - You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP as a reward for achieving a very rare achievement! - You have acquired the Title **Door Opener**! - Level up! - All injuries and fatigue have been recovered as a result of leveling up!
High risk, high reward.
The attempt had been dangerous, but the payoff was worth it.
He’d gained all at once the EXP it would take to defeat several Black Ghosts—and, more importantly, achieved his main goal.
“What on earth...!”
At his Master’s stunned expression, the Disciple curled his bloodied lips into a smile.
“You can see for yourself.”
The changes around them were already plain to the naked eye.
*Grrrrk.*
The empty air warped, like the face of a monster forced to spit something out.
And then—
*Whoooosh.*
Several previously invisible gaps opened their maws one after another.
They spilled out the darkness that had filled them, along with what they’d hidden away.
More precisely—
“Arrrgh! You sons of bitches—you’re worse than beggars!”
“Come forth! I am Hyuk Mu—best hero the great Jin Family of Taiyuan has to offer!”
One beggar who didn’t hesitate to criticize himself, and one martial artist whose fierce loyalty to his family was matched only by his willingness to trade self-awareness for a piece of candy.
In the suffocating silence, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s greatest hero finally spoke.
“Don’t be fooled, beggar. This is all their dark arts.”
The beggar, who was a little better than a son of a bitch, shot back.
“Do I look like an idiot who’d fall for this? I saw through this crap ages ago.”
“Heh. Just what I’d expect from the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar.”
“You’re not bad yourself. You figured it out right away.”
Master and Disciple watched them with distant eyes and had much the same thought.
*Can’t we put those guys back?*
*Should I just put them back in?*
Unfortunately, neither got the chance.
Before they could seriously consider how, a second rift opened.
*Whoooosh.*
Beyond the darkness fading away, a man appeared in a rush. His eyes were as cold as his expression as he surveyed the area, then asked Jin Taekyung,
“Dark arts?”
“This asshole’s at it too.”
At the answer that came without a pause, Song Ilseom lowered his blood-dripping blade.
“It’s really you.”
“Glad you’re alive. Where’s Young Lady Ju?”
“She’ll be out soon. It might’ve been a trap, so I went first.”
Song Ilseom hesitated, then added, “The employer’s safety comes first.”
“I didn’t ask— Ah, Young Lady Ju!”
“Benefactor! Great Hero Jin! Young Master Jin!”
Unlike the three before her, Ju Hwaran ran toward Jin Taekyung without the slightest hesitation.
More precisely, she would have—
If the third and fourth rifts hadn’t opened at the same time.
“Wow! I’ve never felt anything this gross before!”
Cheongpung emerged sounding remarkably cheerful for someone who’d just said that. Behind him, a shadow appeared like a ghost, as though it were one with the magical power. It acted without a word.
*Shwack—CLANG!*
A flash crossed the space faster than sound.
Jin Taekyung knocked aside the dagger flying at him with terrifying speed and shrugged.
“You could’ve just said something. Did you really have to go that far?”
“Assassins and physicians have a few things in common. Being suspicious of everything around us is one of them. The more we question, the fewer mistakes we make.”
“So, are you satisfied now?”
“I think I’m less suspicious of the reality I’m seeing, at least.”
The Slaughter Saint looked at Jin Taekyung with a curious glint in his eyes.
“I’m more suspicious of myself now, though. How did you wake up already?”
“Because you’re a quack.”
“Well, I’m nothing special. Anyone with the Heavenly Martial Physique and martial arts like mine could do it.”
The Slaughter Saint squeezed his eyes shut at the Master and Disciple’s mocking, arrogant answers. Just then, someone emerged from the fifth and final rift.
Unlike the others, she neither hurried nor moved stealthily. Not a drop of blood stained her clothes or skin.
But Bow Saint’s eyes were different from usual.
A tempest.
It lasted only a moment, but a few people saw it clearly: the traces of fierce emotion in eyes that were usually clear and unshakable.
Just as a wave striking a reef can’t hide its white foam, that emotion had left its mark somewhere in her eyes, black as the night sky.
Before anyone could form a clear suspicion about what they’d just seen, the low-voiced conversation between a beggar and a hero reached everyone’s ears.
“What? Is it real?”
“I told you it isn’t. Leave it to the Successor Beggar to talk like a filthy footwrap.”
“No, it looks real to me, no matter how I look at it.”
“I said it’s *real dark arts*.”
“Ha, shit. Is that so?”
Hyuk Mujin delivered the final blow to the frowning Gung Gibang.

“But dark arts can never be perfect. They grant power to those who abandon the proper path, but there’s always a flaw. Look—we’re one person short. They managed to imitate everyone else, but they must not have dared try that man.”
Everyone listening suddenly remembered something they’d forgotten.
Even now, after the final rift had closed, Great Sir was nowhere to be seen.

*Can’t we put those guys back?*
*Should I just put them back in?*
Unfortunately, neither got the chance.
Before they could seriously consider how, a second rift opened.
*Whoooosh.*
Beyond the darkness fading away, a man appeared in a rush.
His eyes were as cold as his expression as he surveyed the area, then asked Jin Taekyung,
“Dark arts?”
“This asshole’s at it too.”
At the answer that came without a pause, Song Ilseom lowered his blood-dripping blade.
“It’s really you.”
“Glad you’re alive.
Where’s Young Lady Ju?”
“She’ll be out soon.
It might’ve been a trap, so I went first.”
Song Ilseom hesitated, then added, “The employer’s safety comes first.”
“I didn’t ask— Ah, Young Lady Ju!”
“Benefactor!
Great Hero Jin!
Young Master Jin!”
Unlike the three before her, Ju Hwaran ran toward Jin Taekyung without the slightest hesitation.
More precisely, she would have—
If the third and fourth rifts hadn’t opened at the same time.
“Wow!
I’ve never felt anything this gross before!”
Cheongpung emerged sounding remarkably cheerful for someone who’d just said that.
Behind him, a shadow appeared like a ghost, as though it were one with the magical power.
It acted without a word.
*Shwack—CLANG!*
A flash crossed the space faster than sound.
Jin Taekyung knocked aside the dagger flying at him with terrifying speed and shrugged.
“You could’ve just said something.
Did you really have to go that far?”
“Assassins and physicians have a few things in common.
Being suspicious of everything around us is one of them.
The more we question, the fewer mistakes we make.”
“So, are you satisfied now?”
“I think I’m less suspicious of the reality I’m seeing, at least.”
The Slaughter Saint looked at Jin Taekyung with a curious glint in his eyes.
“I’m more suspicious of myself now, though.
How did you wake up already?”
“Because you’re a quack.”
“Well, I’m nothing special.
Anyone with the Heavenly Martial Physique and martial arts like mine could do it.”
The Slaughter Saint squeezed his eyes shut at the Master and Disciple’s mocking, arrogant answers.
Just then, someone emerged from the fifth and final rift.
Unlike the others, she neither hurried nor moved stealthily.
Not a drop of blood stained her clothes or skin.
But Bow Saint’s eyes were different from usual.
A tempest.
It lasted only a moment, but a few people saw it clearly: the traces of fierce emotion in eyes that were usually clear and unshakable.
Just as a wave striking a reef can’t hide its white foam, that emotion had left its mark somewhere in her eyes, black as the night sky.
Before anyone could form a clear suspicion about what they’d just seen, the low-voiced conversation between a beggar and a hero reached everyone’s ears.
“What?
Is it real?”
“I told you it isn’t.
Leave it to the Successor Beggar to talk like a filthy footwrap.”
“No, it looks real to me, no matter how I look at it.”
“I said it’s *real dark arts*.”
“Ha, shit.
Is that so?”
Hyuk Mujin delivered the final blow to the frowning Gung Gibang.
“But dark arts can never be perfect.
They grant power to those who abandon the proper path, but there’s always a flaw.
Look—we’re one person short.
They managed to imitate everyone else, but they must not have dared try that man.”
Everyone listening suddenly remembered something they’d forgotten.
Even now, after the final rift had closed, Great Sir was nowhere to be seen.
